mcqs.question: The following European powers entered into Indian trade at one time or the other : 1. The British 2. The Dutch 3. The French 4. The Portuguese Select the correct chronological order of their entry from the code given below : Code:
mcqs.explanation: The order of the arrival of the European powers in India was as follows— Portuguese, Dutch, British, French.

mcqs.question: Who were the first Europeans to come to India for trade ?
mcqs.explanation: Among the given options, the Portuguese were the first to establish trade relations with India in the medieval period. Vasco da Gama was the first Portuguese to reach Calicut, a port on the western coast of India, on 20 May 1498. With his arrival, a new sea route to India was discovered. The then ruler of Calicut, the Zamorin, welcomed Vasco da Gama.

mcqs.question: Who was the real founder of Portuguese power in India?
mcqs.explanation: The real founder of Portuguese power in India was Afonso de Albuquerque (1509-15 A.D.). He established the Portuguese state in India as a territorial power. His first major achievement was the conquest of Goa from the Adil Shahi Sultan of Bijapur in February 1510. The conquest of Goa confirmed Portuguese naval supremacy on the south- western coast and marked the establishment of a territorial Portuguese state in India. The first fort built by the Portuguese in India (also the first European fort in India) was constructed at Cochin in 1503 A.D. by Afonso de Albuquerque. At that time, he was not the Governor.

mcqs.question: At which one of the following places in India did the Portuguese build their first fortress ?
mcqs.explanation: The first fort built by the Portuguese in India (also the first European fort in India) was constructed at Cochin in 1503 A.D. by Afonso de Albuquerque. (At that time, he was not the Governor).

mcqs.question: Among the following factories in Bengal, the one established by the Portuguese was :
mcqs.explanation: Among the factories mentioned in the question, the trading centre (factory) at Hooghly was established by the Portuguese. Trading centres were established at Chinsurah by the Dutch and at Serampore by the Danes. It is worth noting that Bandel was located near the Portuguese factory at Hooghly, and the Portuguese also established their settlement and church there.

mcqs.question: Which of the following factories of Bengal was established by the Dutch ?
mcqs.explanation: Among the given options, the factory at Chinsurah was established by the Dutch. It should be noted that although Chinsurah was located in Hooghly itself, option (b), Chinsurah, is the most appropriate answer to the question.

mcqs.question: With reference to Pondicherry (Now Puducherry), consider the following statements: 1. The first European powers to occupy Pondicherry were the Portuguese. 2. The second European powers to occupy Pondicherry were the French. 3. The English never occupied Pondicherry. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.explanation: The Portuguese were the first to establish their colony in Pondicherry. After them, the Danes and the Dutch established their trading posts there, and later, in 1673 A.D., the French established their settlement there. The English also captured Pondicherry in 1793 A.D., and under the Treaty of Paris (1814), it was handed back to France. Thus, only statement 1 is correct.

mcqs.question: Who among the following was the founder of Calcutta ?
mcqs.explanation: Job Charnock, the head of the Kasimbazar factory, chose Sutanuti or Sutanooti (the site of Calcutta) in place of Hooghly for the English trading centre. Therefore, he is generally regarded as the founder of Calcutta. However, in its judgment delivered in May 2003, a division bench of the Calcutta High Court held that Job Charnock could not be regarded as the founder of Calcutta, and stated that Calcutta (Kalikata) existed even before his arrival. On this basis, 24 August 1690 also cannot be accepted as the Foundation Day of Calcutta.

mcqs.question: In India the First Municipal Corporation was set up in which one among the following places?
mcqs.explanation: The first Municipal Corporation in modern India was established in 1688 AD in the Presidency city of Madras.

mcqs.question: The secret of success of East India Company in India was :

options.b: The company army received western training and they had modern arms.
options.c: Indian soldiers lacked fidelity consequently the one who paid them sufficiently could have them on his service

mcqs.explanation: All the three reasons mentioned in the question contributed to the success of the East India Company in India.

mcqs.question: Which of the following British companies got the first charter permitting them to trade in India ?

options.c: The English Company trading to the East Indies

mcqs.explanation: Among the companies mentioned in the question, the Levant Company was the first to receive a charter in 1592 AD to trade in India through the land route. On 31 December 1600, Queen Elizabeth I granted the first charter for trade by the sea route with the East Indies, known as the Royal Charter of Incorporation, to “The Governor and Company of Merchants of London Trading into the East Indies,” and with this the British East India Company came into existence. At that time, the Mughal emperor of India was Akbar (1556–1605 AD).

mcqs.question: Which one of the following European trading companies was the first to establish its factory at Surat?
mcqs.explanation: Among the European trading companies, the British East India Company was the first to establish a factory at Surat. In 1613 AD, Jahangir granted the English permission to establish a permanent factory at Surat. The Dutch established their factory at Surat in 1616 AD, while the French established theirs in 1668 AD. It is noteworthy that the East India Company first established its factory in 1611 AD at Masulipatnam, but it was temporary. It established its first permanent factory in 1613 AD at Surat. The French also established their first factory in 1668 AD at Surat itself.

mcqs.question: In which of the following years, was the authority of the British established over the fort of Prayagraj (U.P.)?
mcqs.explanation: The Nawab of Awadh, Saadat Ali Khan II, transferred the fort of Prayagraj (Allahabad) to the British in 1798 AD. Therefore, none of the given options was correct.

mcqs.question: French East India Company was constituted during the reign of-
mcqs.explanation: The French East India Company was established in 1664 AD by Colbert, the minister of Louis XIV, and it was called “Compagnie des Indes Orientales.” The French company was established by the state, and the state itself bore all its expenses. In 1667 AD, an expedition under the leadership of Francis Caron set out for India, and in 1668 AD the French established their first trading factory at Surat.

mcqs.question: The French failed to establish power in the Deccan because:

options.a: Duplex was not a capable general
options.b: The English had a strong army
options.c: The French were not liked by the Indians
options.d: Pondicherry was not a strategic centre

mcqs.explanation: One of the main reasons for the defeat of the French was their weak navy. According to Voltaire, during the War of the Austrian Succession, the sea power of France declined so much that by the time of the Seven Years’ War, they did not have even a single warship. On the other hand, the English possessed a powerful army.

mcqs.question: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer from the code given below the lists: List- I List- II A. Pondicherry 1. Dutch B. Goa 2. French C. Tranquebar 3. Portuguese D. Sadras 4. Danish (Dane) Code : A B C D
mcqs.explanation: The correct matching is as follows— Pondicherry – French Goa – Portuguese Tranquebar – Danish (Danes) Sadras – Dutch

mcqs.question: In which of the following places the Dutch established their trading centre in India?
mcqs.explanation: The major trading centres established by the Dutch in India were – Nagapattinam, Chinsurah, Machilipatnam, Surat, Bharuch, Agra, Cochin, Ahmedabad, and Patna.

mcqs.question: Carnatic War was fought between :
mcqs.explanation: The First Carnatic War (1746-48) was merely an extension of the War of the Austrian Succession, which had begun in 1740. Contrary to the orders of their home governments, war broke out between the two sides (the English and the French) in 1746. The immediate cause of the war was the capture of some French ships by the English fleet under the leadership of Captain Barnett.

mcqs.question: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below the lists: List-I List-II A. First Carnatic War 1. Ended by Treaty of Paris B. Third Carnatic War 2. Britishers Lost C. Second Carnatic War 3. Inconclusive War D. First Mysore War 4. Ended by Treaty of Aix La Chapelle Code : A B C D
mcqs.explanation: The correct matching is as follows— First Carnatic War – Ended with the Treaty of Aix- la-Chapelle Third Carnatic War – Ended with the Treaty of Paris Second Carnatic War – Inconclusive war First Mysore War – British Lost

mcqs.question: Which one of the following is not correctly matched?
mcqs.explanation: The correct matching of the wars mentioned in the question is as follows— First Carnatic War – 1746–48 Second Carnatic War – 1749–54 Third Carnatic War – 1758–63 Third Battle of Panipat – 1761

mcqs.question: With reference to the Treaty of “Aix-la-Chapelle-1748” which of the following statements is/are correct? 1. The Ist Carnatic War was ended. 2. The English got back Madras. Select the correct answer using the codes given below. Codes :
mcqs.explanation: The Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle (1748) ended the War of the Austrian Succession. As soon as the war in Europe ended, the First Carnatic War also came to an end, and Madras was restored to the English. Therefore, both statements 1 and 2 are correct.

mcqs.question: In the Battle of Wandhiwash (1760) –
mcqs.explanation: In January 1760, in the Battle of Wandiwash fought between the British and the French, the French were defeated. In this battle, the British army was led by Eyre Coote, while the French army was led by Count de Lally.

mcqs.question: With reference to "the causes of the success of British and failure of the French in India" which of the following statements is/are correct? 1. Getting huge wealth and manpower from the conquest of Bengal by British. 2. Naval superiority of the British. Select the correct answer from the codes given below. Codes:
mcqs.explanation: There were several reasons for the success of the British in India. These included their superior naval strength, the enormous wealth and manpower gained from control over Bengal, coordination among the different units of the Company, capable leadership, etc.

mcqs.question: Which one of the following was the last Governor of Bengal appointed by the Mughal Emperor ?
mcqs.explanation: In 1717, Mughal Emperor Farrukhsiyar appointed Murshid Quli Khan as the Governor (Subedar) of Bengal. After the death of Murshid Quli Khan, his son-in-law Shuja-ud-Din became the Subedar of Bengal, and he was recognized by the then Mughal Emperor Muhammad Shah ‘Rangila’. Therefore, Murshid Quli Khan was the last Governor of Bengal appointed by a Mughal emperor.
mcqs.chapter: East India Company and Nawabs of Bengal

mcqs.question: Sirajuddaula was defeated by Lord Clive in the battle of-
mcqs.explanation: British supremacy in India began with the Battle of Plassey. In the Battle of Plassey (23 June, 1757), the English under the leadership of Robert Clive defeated Siraj-ud-Daulah, the Nawab of Bengal.
mcqs.chapter: East India Company and Nawabs of Bengal

mcqs.question: Who among the following has been called as a “Heaven Born General” ?
mcqs.explanation: Clive was a popular leader and a skilled soldier. William Pitt remarked that he was “A Heaven Born General.”

mcqs.question: Which of the following shifted his capital from Murshidabad to Munger ?
mcqs.explanation: Mir Qasim shifted his capital from Murshidabad to Munger. Possibly, he wanted to stay away from the conspiratorial atmosphere of Murshidabad and also remain distant from Calcutta so that British interference could be minimized.

mcqs.question: The most decisive battle that led to the establishment of supremacy of the British in India was :
mcqs.explanation: On 22 October, 1764, the British defeated the combined army of Mir Qasim, Shuja-ud-Daulah, the Nawab of Awadh, and the Mughal Emperor Shah Alam II of Delhi in the Battle of Buxar. In this battle, the English forces were led by Major Hector Munro. The result of this battle put the seal on the decisions of Plassey; after this, no other power remained to challenge the English in India. The region up to Allahabad came under the control of the English, and the road to the conquest of Delhi was opened. From the point of view of establishing British dominance in India, the Battle of Buxar proved to be the most decisive.

mcqs.question: Who was the Nawab of Bengal when the Battle of Buxar was fought?
mcqs.explanation: Mir Jafar was the Nawab of Bengal at the time of the Battle of Buxar.
mcqs.chapter: East India Company and Nawabs of Bengal

mcqs.question: Which one of the following rulers had granted Diwani to the East India Company ?
mcqs.explanation: After the victory of the British in the Battle of Buxar, by his farman dated 12 August, 1765, Mughal Emperor Shah Alam II granted the Diwani of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa to the Company. At that time, Robert Clive was the Governor of Bengal under the East India Company.
mcqs.chapter: East India Company and Nawabs of Bengal

mcqs.question: Usually there were certain Hindu castes who were placed at the high positions in the State of Nawabs of Oudh. Select the correct answer from the code given below. Code:
mcqs.explanation: In the state of the Nawabs of Awadh, Hindu officials were also appointed to high posts. Raja Tikait Rai and Raja Jhau Lal served as the Diwans (Finance Ministers) of Asaf-ud- Daula, and Raja Naval Rai served as the Prime Minister and Commander under Nawab Safdar Jang. Therefore, both the given statements are correct.
mcqs.chapter: East India Company and Nawabs of Bengal

mcqs.question: Which of the following opposed British in India vigorously?
mcqs.explanation: The Marathas opposed the British the most in India. Only after the three Anglo-Maratha Wars could Maratha power be suppressed. Finally, in 1818, Lord Hastings destroyed the remaining Maratha power and established British supremacy.
mcqs.chapter: East India Company and Nawabs of Bengal

mcqs.question: The kingdom of Ranjit Singh included –
mcqs.explanation: Ranjit Singh was born on 13 November, 1780 in the home of Maha Singh, the chief of Sukerchakia Misl. On 25th April 1809, the Treaty of Amritsar took place between Maharaja Ranjit Singh and British. The terms of the treaty prevented Singh from any further territorial expansion south of the Sutlej but on the other hand, as Cunningham said, Ranjit Singh occupied authority to spread kingdom in the West. He annexed Lahore (1799), Amritsar (1805), Multan (1818), Kashmir (1819) and Peshawar Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (1834). Thus, among given options, Sri Nagar was included in the kingdom of Ranjit Singh.

mcqs.question: Capital of Kingdom of Maharaja Ranjit Singh was:
mcqs.explanation: Zaman Shah invaded Punjab in 1798. While returning, his cannons had fallen in the Chenab River. Ranjit Singh returned them safely to Lahore. Hence, Zaman shah permitted him to occupy Lahore. In 1799, Ranjit Singh seized Lahore and made it capital.
mcqs.chapter: East India Company and Nawabs of Bengal

mcqs.question: At which place did Raja Ranjit Singh set up the Adalat- i-Ala?
mcqs.explanation: Judicial system of Maharaja Ranjit singh was very harsh. Highest court in his state was Adalati-i-Ala, situated in Lahore. Ranjit singh himself was its Chief Justice.
mcqs.chapter: East India Company and Nawabs of Bengal

mcqs.question: Who among the following has said, ‘God intended me to look upon all religions with one eye, that is why he took away the light from the other’?
mcqs.explanation: The above-statement was made by Maharaja Ranjit Singh. Ranjit Singh was born on 13 Nov. 1780 A.D. at Gujranwala.
mcqs.chapter: East India Company and Nawabs of Bengal

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is/are correct in the context of the Treaty of Lahore (1846)? I. The Maharaja left all his territories beyond the river Satluj forever. II. The Maharaja left his rights over all the forts between the Satluj and Beas rivers in favour of the Company. III. The English army could no longer pass through the Sikh State. Select the correct answer from the codes given below :
mcqs.explanation: Statement Truthfulness
mcqs.chapter: East India Company and Nawabs of Bengal

mcqs.question: Who was last king of Sikh Empire?
mcqs.explanation: Duleep Singh was the last ruler of the Sikh Empire in Punjab. In 1849, at the end of the Second Anglo-Sikh War, Punjab was annexed by the British, and Duleep Singh was given a pension and later sent to Britain.

mcqs.question: Regarding Punjab Merger, which of the following statement is false?

options.a: On 29th March, 1849, the Governor General announced that the state of Punjab had come to an end.
options.b: All the territories of Maharaja Duleep SIngh became part of the Indian British Empire.
options.c: Duleep Singh was given an annual pension of Rs. 2,50,000.

mcqs.explanation: By Lord Dalhousie’s proclamation dated 29 March, 1849, the whole of Punjab was annexed to the British dominions. Maharaja Duleep Singh was granted an annual pension of £50,000 (approximately `4–5 lakh) and was sent to England to receive education. Therefore, among the given statements, option (c) is false.

mcqs.question: Which one of the following statements is correct about Dalip Singh, the ex-Maharaja of Punjab?

options.a: He died in Paris on 23 October, 1893
options.c: He never renounced the Sikh faith.

mcqs.explanation: The former Maharaja of Punjab, Duleep Singh, died in Paris (France) on 22 October, 1893 (or, according to some sources, on 23 October, 1893). All the remaining statements are incorrect. Duleep Singh had renounced Sikhism and embraced Christianity. He had also travelled to Russia. His funeral rites were performed in England.

mcqs.question: Who among the following was not a member of ‘Board of Three’ to administer the State of Punjab after its annexation?
mcqs.explanation: After the annexation of Punjab into the British Empire, Lord Dalhousie formed a Council of three in 1849 to govern Punjab. In this council, Sir Henry Lawrence was appointed as President, while John Lawrence and Charles Grenville Mansel were appointed as members. H.M. Elliot and Robert Montgomery were not associated with this council.

mcqs.question: Who emerged victorious in the first Anglo-Mysore War (1767-69)?
mcqs.explanation: The First Anglo-Mysore War (1767–69 A.D.) was fought between the British and Hyder Ali. Against Hyder Ali, the Nizam, the Marathas, and the British came together in a tripartite alliance. Through his diplomatic skill, Hyder tried to break this alliance. He won over the Marathas by paying money and lured the Nizam by offering territory, and then attacked the Carnatic. Due to the initial success of the British, the Nizam again joined the British side. Nevertheless, Hyder Ali fought vigorously and captured Mangalore in 1768. In March 1769, his forces reached up to Madras. The British were compelled to sign the Treaty of Madras on 4 April, 1769, on Hyder Ali’s terms.

mcqs.question: Who among the following established a modern armory in Dindigul Mysore in 1755?
mcqs.explanation: In 1755 A.D., Hyder Ali captured Dindigul and converted this fort into a military outpost. He established a modern arsenal there.

mcqs.question: Who among the following Indian rulers established embassies in foreign countries on modern lines?
mcqs.explanation: Tipu Sultan established embassies abroad on modern lines.

mcqs.question: Tipu Sultan defeated the British Army in 1780 at –
mcqs.explanation: During the Second Anglo-Mysore War (1780–84 A.D.), Tipu defeated the British army at a place called Pollilur in 1780 A.D.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is correctly matched?

options.a: First Anglo-Mysore - Hyder Ali was defeated War
options.b: Second Anglo-Mysore - Hyder Ali defeated the War British
options.c: Third Anglo-Mysore - Tipu Sultan won the War battle and did not cede his territory to British.
options.d: Fourth Anglo-Mysore -Tipu was defeated and War was killed in the thick of battle

mcqs.explanation: The Fourth Anglo-Mysore War was fought in 1799 A.D. During this time, the English Governor-General was Lord Wellesley. On 4 May, 1799, the English army captured the fort of Srirangapatnam, and Tipu died fighting bravely. Therefore, option (d) is the correctly matched pair, whereas the other three pairs are not correctly matched.

mcqs.question: Consider the following events and arrange them in chronological order. I. Battle of Mudki II. Battle of Porto Novo III. Battle of Shakarkheda IV. Battle of Bedara Select the correct answer from the code given below: Code : A B C D
mcqs.explanation: The chronological order of the above events is as follows: Battle of Shakar Kheda – 1724 A.D. Battle of Bedara – 1759 A.D. Battle of Porto Novo – 1781 A.D. Battle of Mudki – 1845 A.D. Therefore, the correct answer is option (a).

mcqs.question: Match List- I with List- II and select the correct answer using the code given below the lists : List- I List- II A. Treaty of Allahabad 1. 1782 B. Treaty of Mangalore 2. 1784 C. Treaty of Salbai 3. 1769 D. Treaty of Madras 4. 1765 Code : A B C D
mcqs.explanation: The Treaty of Allahabad was concluded on 16 August 1765 between the British and Shuja-ud-Daula, the Nawab of Awadh. The Treaty of Mangalore was concluded in 1784 between the British and Tipu Sultan after the Second Anglo-Mysore War (1780–84). The Treaty of Salbai was concluded in 1782 between the British and the Marathas, under the mediation of Mahadji Scindia, after the First Anglo-Maratha War (1775–82). The Treaty of Madras was concluded in 1769 between Haidar Ali and the British after the First Anglo- Mysore War (1767–69).

mcqs.question: Consider the following events: 1. Clive's re-arrival in India 2. Treaty of Allahabad 3. Battle of Buxar 4. Warren Hastings became India's Governor. Select the correct chronological order of the above events from the codes given below. Codes:
mcqs.explanation: The chronological order of the given events is as follows: Battle of Buxar – 22 October 1764 Clive’s return to India – 3 May 1765 Treaty of Allahabad – 16 August 1765 Warren Hastings becoming the – 1772 Governor of Bengal There is an error in this question. Warren Hastings has been described as the Governor of India, which is incorrect. He became the Governor of the Calcutta Presidency, that is, Bengal, in 1772, and in 1774 he became the Governor- General of Bengal. Therefore, the nearest correct answer is option (b).

mcqs.question: Who led the 'Banaras Rebellion' against the Britishers?
mcqs.explanation: The ‘Banaras Revolt’ was led by Raja Chait Singh in 1781. During this revolt, the then Governor-General, Warren Hastings, fled and took shelter in Chunar Fort.

mcqs.question: At the time of the establishment of Asiatic Society in Calcutta, who was the Governor-General of Bengal?
mcqs.explanation: When the Asiatic Society was established in Calcutta on 15 January 1784, the Governor-General of Bengal was Lord Warren Hastings (1774–1785).

mcqs.question: The policy of ‘Ring Fence’ is related with-
mcqs.explanation: Ring-Fence Policy is associated with Warren Hastings and Wellesley. During the time of Warren Hastings, the Company tried to create buffer states around its territories. With the arrival of Wellesley, the Company’s relations with Indian princely states underwent a change. Wellesley’s objective was to compel Indian princely states to depend on the Company for their protection. He tried to bring Indian states within the orbit of British political power and military protection.

mcqs.question: Who among the following was prosecuted for impeachment by the British Parliament?
mcqs.explanation: An impeachment trial was conducted against Warren Hastings on account of his unjust and arbitrary acts. The trial continued from 1788 to 1795. However, the British Parliament acquitted him of all charges.

mcqs.question: Who established the judicial organization in India?
mcqs.explanation: The English laid the foundation of a new system of justice through a hierarchical organization of civil and criminal courts. Warren Hastings initiated this system, but Cornwallis strengthened it further. The Cornwallis Code of 1793 was based on the principle of separation of powers, under which revenue administration and judicial administration were separated.

mcqs.question: The enforcement of the Public Service was done in-
mcqs.explanation: The Covenanted Civil Service in India was created by Cornwallis. After becoming the Governor-General of Bengal, Cornwallis reorganized the administration. He abolished the revenue boards and framed new rules in this regard. He also introduced new rules regarding the private trade of Company officials. Through the Cornwallis Code, he made a clear distinction between revenue and judicial functions, which later formed the basis of the civil service system in India.

mcqs.question: In the second half of 18th century, who was often called the local representative of "Aura and Authority of Company Bahadur"?
mcqs.explanation: Lord Cornwallis separated the zamindars from their police duties, established a police station in every area of about twenty to thirty square miles, and appointed a police officer called the daroga. The daroga was appointed and supervised by the magistrate. The peasants regarded the daroga as the local representative of the “pomp and prestige of Company Bahadur.”

mcqs.question: The Tomb of Lord Cornwallis is situated at –
mcqs.explanation: Lord Cornwallis was the Governor-General of Bengal from 1786 to 1793 A.D. and again from 30 July, 1805 to 5 October, 1805. He is known in India as the introducer of the Permanent Settlement, the judicial code, and the Indian Civil Service. He died on 5 October, 1805 at Ghazipur (

mcqs.question: Who among the following Governor Generals of Bengal was associated with Third Anglo-Mysore War?
mcqs.explanation: Lord Cornwallis is associated with the Third Anglo-Mysore War (1790–1792 A.D.). In this war, Cornwallis himself took command of the army. During this war, Tipu entered into the Treaty of Seringapatam (1792 A.D.), according to which he had to surrender nearly half of his kingdom to the English and their allies (the Nizam and the Marathas).

mcqs.question: Subsidiary Alliance was implemented during the reign of –
mcqs.explanation: Wellesley did not invent the Subsidiary Alliance; this system already existed earlier. Probably Dupleix was the first European who rented out his army to Indian rulers. From the time of Clive, almost all Governor-Generals had adopted this system. Wellesley’s special contribution was only that he developed it and applied it in relation to all the native rulers who came into contact with him. Thus, the Subsidiary Alliance system was implemented during Wellesley’s period in order to establish British supremacy over the Indian states.

mcqs.question: The Subsidiary Alliance was not accepted by-
mcqs.explanation: Lord Wellesley (1798–1805 A.D.) used the Subsidiary Alliance system to bring Indian states within the British political sphere of influence. The states that accepted the Subsidiary Alliance were—Hyderabad (1798 and 1800 A.D.), Mysore (1799 A.D.), Tanjore (1799 A.D.), Awadh (1801 A.D.), the Peshwa (1802 A.D.), the Bhonsle ruler of Berar (1803 A.D.), Scindia (1804 A.D.), Holkar of Indore (1818 A.D.), Jodhpur, Jaipur, Macheri, Bundi, and Bharatpur. Therefore, none of the options given in the question is correct.

mcqs.question: Between whom was the ‘Treaty of Bassein ‘ signed in 1802 ?
mcqs.explanation: Peshwa Baji Rao II signed the ‘Treaty of Bassein’ with the British on 31 December, 1802. According to the treaty, Peshwa Baji Rao II accepted British protection. This was the first Subsidiary Alliance concluded by the Marathas with the English.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is not correctly matched?

options.c: Monopoly of East India – 1833 Company in India
options.d: Opening of trade in India – 1813 for British citizens and companies

mcqs.explanation: With the objective of establishing the supremacy of British rule in India, Wellesley began implementing the Subsidiary Alliance system in 1798 A.D. The other pairs in the question—Battle of Buxar–1764, monopoly of the East India Company–1833 (it was declared completely abolished by the Act of 1833), and opening of trade in India to British citizens and companies–1813—are correctly matched. Thus, the pair in option (b) is not correctly matched.

mcqs.question: Anglo-Nepal War took place during the reign of –
mcqs.explanation: The Anglo-Nepal War (1814–16) took place during the tenure of Lord Hastings as Governor-General (1813–23), and it ended with the Treaty of Sugauli. The Treaty of Sugauli was signed on 2 December, 1815, and was ratified on 4 March, 1816.

mcqs.question: Which of the following sites were obtained by the British East India Company under the Treaty of Sugauli in 1816 ? 1. Kathmandu 2. Shimla 3. Ranikhet 4. Nainital Select the correct answer from the code given below : Code :
mcqs.explanation: As a result of the Treaty of Sugauli (1816), Nepal ceded Kumaon, the eastern part of Garhwal, and some parts of the Terai to the British East India Company. The areas falling under Kumaon came under British rule. Kathmandu: It remained the capital of Nepal; under the treaty, there was only a provision for the appointment of a British Resident, and Kathmandu was not ceded to the British. Shimla: The treaty established British control over the hill belt in which Shimla is located; however, the actual transfer of Shimla town/station took place in 1830 from Keonthal/ Patiala. Ranikhet: Ranikhet is situated in the Kumaon region (present-day Uttarakhand). After the Treaty of Sugauli, Kumaon came under British control. Nainital: Nainital was also a part of Kumaon; when Kumaon came under British control, this region too came under Company rule. Note: In its preliminary answer key, UPPSC gave option (c) as the answer to this question, which is not correct.

mcqs.question: Which one of the following pairs is not correctly matched?
mcqs.explanation: The Third Anglo-Maratha War (1817–18) took place during the time of Lord Hastings, not during the time of Lord Cornwallis. Therefore, option (d) is not correctly matched. The Fourth Anglo-Mysore War (1799) took place during Lord Wellesley’s tenure, and the Anglo-Nepal War (1814– 16) took place during Lord Hastings’ tenure, whereas the Battle of Buxar (1764) was fought under the leadership of Hector Munro.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is not correctly matched?

options.d: Lord William - Seventeenth Regulation of 1829 Bentinck

mcqs.explanation: The Second Anglo-Maratha War took place between 1803 and 1805 during the tenure of Lord Wellesley. During Lord Hastings’ tenure, the Third and final Anglo-Maratha War (1817–1818) took place. After the defeat of the Marathas in the Third Anglo-Maratha War, Lord Hastings abolished the office of the Peshwa in 1818, and the entire territory of the Peshwa in western India was merged into the Bombay Presidency. Besides this, the Company established political control over Bundelkhand, Malwa, and the remaining parts of India over which the Peshwas had exercised dominance. The other three pairs are correctly matched.

mcqs.question: Sir Thomas Munro was Governor of Madras during years
mcqs.explanation: Sir Thomas Munro was the Governor of Madras from 1820 to 1827. Thomas Munro and Captain Reed are regarded as the pioneers of the Ryotwari system, which was introduced for land revenue collection in South India.

mcqs.question: On the basis of alleged maladministration which Governor-General had taken the administration of Mysore state?
mcqs.explanation: William Bentinck took over the administration of the princely state of Mysore in 1831 and of Coorg in 1834 (and the plains of Cachar in 1832) on the ground that there was allegedly extreme misgovernment and disorder there.

mcqs.question: Sati system was abolished by –
mcqs.explanation: Enlightened Indian reformers such as Raja Ram Mohan Roy inspired William Bentinck to declare the practice of Sati illegal. Many contemporary progressive newspapers supported him, and William Bentinck completely prohibited the practice of Sati by making a law. By Regulation XVII of December 1829, the burning of widows was declared illegal. Initially, this law was implemented only in the Bengal Presidency, and in 1830 it was extended to the Bombay and Madras Presidencies as well.

mcqs.question: Which Governor General had abolished slavery?
mcqs.explanation: In India, the then Governor-General Lord Ellenborough abolished slavery through Act V of 1843. Ellenborough’s tenure was from 1842 to 1844.

mcqs.question: The conquest of Sindh by British was completed during the period of –
mcqs.explanation: During the tenure of Governor-General Lord Ellenborough (1842–1844), Sind was completely annexed to the British Empire in 1843. This was a major outcome of the First Anglo-Afghan War.

mcqs.question: Awadh was annexed to British Empire in India by :

options.d: By declaring the State as maladministered

mcqs.explanation: Lord Dalhousie (1848–56) annexed Awadh to British rule on 13 February 1856 by accusing Nawab Wajid Ali Shah of maladministration. Apart from Awadh, the states annexed under Dalhousie’s Doctrine of Lapse were Satara (1848), Jaitpur and Sambalpur (1849), Baghat (1850), Udaipur (1852), Jhansi (1854), Nagpur (1854) and Karauli (1855).

mcqs.question: Which among the following was not one of those states which were annexed to the British Empire by Lord Dalhousie on the pretext of the ‘Doctrine of Lapse’?
mcqs.explanation: State Was it annexed under the Doctrine of Lapse? Satara Yes – in 1848, Dalhousie first applied it here. Jhansi Yes – in 1854; the state was seized after rejecting the claim of Rani Lakshmibai’s adopted son. Nagpur Yes – in 1854; it was annexed due to the absence of a natural heir in the Bhonsle dynasty. Carnatic No – the major state in the region was Mysore. After 1799 (after the death of Tipu), it remained under British protection and was not related to Dalhousie’s Doctrine of Lapse.

mcqs.question: Who had merged Sikkim in India?
mcqs.explanation: In history, Sikkim’s connection with India in this context can be seen on three occasions– 1. During the tenure of Lord Hastings, the Treaty of Titalia was concluded between Sikkim and British India on 10 February 1817. It mentioned the restoration of certain territories to Sikkim from Nepal, but there was no mention of the merger of any part of Sikkim into British India. 2. Darjeeling and some part of the Terai of Sikkim were annexed to British India in 1850 during the tenure of Lord Dalhousie. This was a partial annexation of Sikkim. 3. In 1975, Sikkim was fully merged into independent India. In the present question, the Commission determined its answer on the basis of the partial annexation of Sikkim into British India during Lord Dalhousie’s tenure. Therefore, the correct answer is option (c).

mcqs.question: Consider the following events and arrange them in chronological order: I. Merger of Sikkim II. Merger of Jhansi III. Merger of Punjab IV. Merger of Burma Select the correct answer from the code given below Code:
mcqs.explanation: The chronological order of annexation of the given states into British India was as follows– Punjab – 1849 Sikkim – 1850 Burma – 1853 Jhansi – 1854 Note: In 1850, only a part of Sikkim (Darjeeling and some part of the Terai) was annexed to British India. Pegu was annexed through the Second Anglo-Burmese War in 1853. Through the Third Anglo-Burmese War (1885), the whole of Burma was annexed to India. According to the options given in the above question, the correct answer (b) is obtained by considering the partial annexation of Sikkim (1850) and the annexation of Pegu in Burma.

mcqs.question: Who among the following was the British resident in Awadh at the time of its annexation into British Dominion?
mcqs.explanation: In 1854, James Outram was appointed the British Resident of Awadh in place of Sleeman. He stated that the administration of Awadh was highly corrupt and that the condition of the people was extremely miserable. Outram’s report became the basis for the annexation of Awadh in February 1856. At the time of the Revolt of 1857, the British Resident at Lucknow was Henry Lawrence, who was killed by the rebels.

mcqs.question: The first railway line was opened in India between –
mcqs.explanation: The first major step towards railway construction in India was taken by the British Governor-General Lord Dalhousie. The first railway line was laid in 1853 between Bombay and Thane during his tenure.

mcqs.question: In whose rule the Widow Remarriage Act was implemented in –
mcqs.explanation: As a result of the tireless efforts of Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar, the Widow Remarriage Act, 1856 was enacted on 26 July 1856 during the time of Lord Canning (28 February 1856– 21 March 1862). This Act had been drafted and introduced during the time of Lord Dalhousie. Under Act XV of 1856, widow remarriage was declared lawful, and the children born from such marriages were declared legitimate.

mcqs.question: Queen Victoria’s manifesto was read out in Allahabad on November 1, 1858 by –
mcqs.explanation: The most important result of the great Revolt of 1857 was the Queen’s Proclamation. It was read out on 1 November 1858 at the durbar held in Allahabad by Lord Canning, the first Viceroy of India.

mcqs.question: The right to adopt heir in place of own son was re- established by –
mcqs.explanation: The Queen’s Proclamation was issued on 1 November 1858 at Allahabad by Lord Canning. In it, the policy towards the Indian princely states was also broadly changed, and they were kept ready for use in any possible crisis of the British Empire. The policy of conquest and annexation was completely abandoned, and the rulers of princely states were permitted to adopt successors.

mcqs.question: Match List - I with List - II and select the correct answer using the code given below the lists. List - I List - II (Governor General/ (Important contribution/ Viceroy) work) A. Lord Dalhousie 1. Permanent settlement of Bengal B. Lord Curzon 2. Prohibition of Practice of Sati C. Lord William 3. Partition of Bengal Bentinck D. Lord Cornwallis 4. Doctrine of Lapse Code : A B C D
mcqs.explanation: The correct matching is as follows: Lord Dalhousie – Doctrine of Lapse Lord Curzon – Partition of Bengal Lord William Bentinck – Abolition of Sati Lord Cornwallis – Permanent Settlement of Bengal Therefore, the correct answer is option (d).

mcqs.question: Which one of the following is correctly matched?

options.d: Lord Canning - Foundation of Indian National Congress

mcqs.explanation: Lord Cornwallis introduced the Permanent Settlement system in 1793. The policy of Masterly Inactivity is associated with John Lawrence, the Subsidiary Alliance with Lord Wellesley, and the Doctrine of Lapse with Lord Dalhousie. The Indian National Congress was established in 1885 during the tenure of Lord Dufferin (1884–88).

mcqs.question: Which of the following is not correctly matched?
mcqs.explanation: The Anglo-Nepal War (1814–16) took place during the tenure of Lord Hastings. The other given pairs are correctly matched.

mcqs.question: Which one of the following is correctly matched?

options.d: Sir John Shore - Third Anglo- Maratha War

mcqs.explanation: The correct matching is as follows: Lord Ellenborough - Annexation of Sindh by the British in 1843 Lord Dalhousie - Annexation of Awadh in 1856 on charges of maladministration Lord Wellesley - Fourth Anglo-Mysore War (1799) Lord Hastings - Third Anglo-Maratha War (1817–18) Therefore, the pair in option (c) is correctly matched.

mcqs.question: Consider the following events and arrange them in correct chronological order. 1. Acquisition of Awadh by the British 2. Ilbert Bill Controversy 3. Indigo Revolt 4. Second Anglo-Afghan War Select the correct answer from the code given below : Code:
mcqs.explanation: The chronology of the given events is as follows: Annexation of Awadh – 1856 Indigo Revolt – 1859-60 Second Anglo-Afghan War – 1878-80 Ilbert Bill Controversy – 1883

mcqs.question: Which one of the following pairs is not correctly matched?

options.b: Lord Dufferin - Establishment of Indian National Congress
options.c: Lord William - Passing of the Charter Act, Bentinck 1833
options.d: Lord Lytton - Beginning of first Anglo- Afghan War

mcqs.explanation: The First Anglo-Afghan War took place between 1839 and 1842. During this period, the Governor-General of India was Auckland. During the tenure of Lord Lytton, the Second Anglo-Afghan War (1878–1880) took place. Thus, option (d) is not correctly matched, while the other three options are correctly matched.

mcqs.question: Who among the following is associated with the policy of ‘Masterly Inactivity’ :
mcqs.explanation: The policy of ‘Masterly Inactivity’ in the context of Anglo- Afghan relations began in the time of Lord Ellenborough and continued up to the tenure of Lord Northbrook. This policy is especially associated with John Lawrence because, during his viceroyalty (1864–1869), it was followed more clearly and its contours were more distinctly defined.

mcqs.question: The 1st census in India during the British period was held during the tenure of –
mcqs.explanation: The first census in British India was completed in 1872 during the tenure of Lord Mayo (1869–72), but the regular decennial census began in 1881 during the tenure of Lord Ripon.

mcqs.question: Which one of the following Viceroys of India was murdered by a convict in Andaman and Nicobar Island while he was on tour?
mcqs.explanation: Lord Mayo (1869–72) was assassinated by a convict during a visit to the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.

mcqs.question: Who had the longest tenure as the Viceroy of India ?
mcqs.explanation: Among the Viceroys mentioned in the question, Lord Curzon, who possessed the greatest knowledge of India, had the longest tenure. Lord Curzon – January, 1899 – November, 1905 = about 6 years 11 months Lord Dufferin – December, 1884 – December, 1888 = about 4 years Lord Hardinge – November, 1910 – April, 1916 = about 5 years 6 months Lord Mayo – January, 1869 – February, 1872 = about 3 years and 1 month

mcqs.question: Local Self-Government institutions in India were strengthened in 1882 by :
mcqs.explanation: The most important measure of Lord Ripon’s tenure was the Government Resolution on Local Self-Government (1882). Under this resolution, provision was made for the establishment of district boards, sub-divisional boards, taluka boards, or tehsil boards. Municipalities were established in towns. These local institutions were assigned definite functions and sources of revenue. In this context, Lord Ripon is called the father of modern local self- government in India.

mcqs.question: Which one of the following pairs is not correctly matched?
mcqs.explanation: Local self-government was associated not with Lord Lytton but with Lord Ripon. The other pairs given in the question are correctly matched.

mcqs.question: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer from the code given below : List- I List- II 1. Clive A. Removal of press restriction 2. Bentinck B. Partition of Bengal 3. Charles Metcalfe C. Dual Govt. in Bengal 4. Curzon D. English Education Code : 1 2 3 4
mcqs.explanation: Clive introduced the Dual Government system in Bengal in 1765. During Bentinck’s tenure, Macaulay laid the foundation of modern education through the medium of the English language. Charles Metcalfe removed restrictions on the press; therefore, he is called the ‘Liberator of the Press’. During Curzon’s tenure, Bengal was partitioned in 1905.

mcqs.question: Who remarked about the East India Company that "The Company is an anomaly but it is part of a system where everything is an anomaly"?
mcqs.explanation: Lord Thomas Babington Macaulay remarked about the policies of the East India Company that, “The Company is an anomaly, but it is a part of a system where everything is anomalous.”

mcqs.question: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below : List-I List-II I. Lord Dalhousie A.Prohibition of Sati II. Lord William Bentinck B. Local Self-Government III. Lord Ripon C. Division of Bengal IV. Lord Curzon D. Doctrine of Lapse Code : I II III IV
mcqs.explanation: The Doctrine of Lapse is associated with Dalhousie (1848– 1856). Through this doctrine, some important princely states such as Satara, Jaitpur, Sambalpur, Baghat, Udaipur, Jhansi, and Nagpur were annexed to the British Empire. William Bentinck abolished Sati by Regulation XVII of 1829. The most important measure during Lord Ripon’s tenure was the Government Resolution on Local Self-Government. Bengal was partitioned by Curzon in 1905.

mcqs.question: Which one of the following statements is not true?

options.a: The foundation of the system of civil administration, was firmly laid down by Warren Hastings on which the superstructure was raised by Cornwallis.
options.b: Clive was responsible for reforming the East India Company’s Civil and military services.
options.c: Lord William Bentinck was one of the greatest British rulers as he consolidated the British Empire in India
options.d: Lord Dalhousie added rich lemitones to the British Empire on the basis of the Doctrine of Lapse.

mcqs.explanation: Among the statements given in the question, the statement in option (c) is not correct, whereas the statements in the other options are correct. During the seven years of Lord William Bentinck’s rule (1828–35), the old policy of continuous wars and annexation was abandoned. In the history of India, Bentinck is remembered for his social and administrative reforms.

mcqs.question: The Archaeological Survey of India was established in the period of –
mcqs.explanation: Efforts relating to archaeological survey in India began with the establishment of the Asiatic Society at Calcutta by William Jones in 1784. In 1861, Lord Canning appointed Alexander Cunningham as the first Archaeological Surveyor of India, and in 1871 a separate government department for archaeological survey was created. During the tenure of Lord Curzon (1899–1905), in 1901, the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) was given an integrated and centralized form, and John Marshall was appointed Director-General.

mcqs.question: During the tenure of which Governor-General was the ‘Ancient Monuments Preservation Act’ passed -
mcqs.explanation: By the Ancient Monuments Preservation Act, 1904, Lord Curzon, for the first time in India, gave attention to the protection and repair of historical buildings and allocated 50,000 pounds for this purpose.

mcqs.question: Which statements is/are true regarding Lord Curzon? 1. Establishing the English Empire on granite rock. 2. Announcement of Calcutta Municipal Act. Select the correct answer the code given below : Code -
mcqs.explanation: The Calcutta Corporation Act, 1899, was enacted during the time of Lord Curzon; therefore, statement 2 is true. Although a direct reference to establishing the British Empire on a granite rock is not clearly found in the context of Lord Curzon, in 1904, in connection with Britain’s imperial mission, Curzon said, “To me the message is carved in granite, hewn from the rock of doom, that our work is righteous and shall endure.” On this basis, statement 1 may also be treated as true.

mcqs.question: Who compared Curzon’s administration in India to that of Aurangzeb?
mcqs.explanation: During his tenure as Viceroy (1899–1905), Lord Curzon tried to strengthen British rule in India while completely ignoring the aspirations of the Indian people. Gopal Krishna Gokhale compared Curzon’s administration with that of the Mughal Emperor Aurangzeb.

mcqs.question: With reference to the Civil Administration in 1905, which of the statements is/are correct? 1. Lord Curzon decided to rearrange the provincial boundaries. 2. A new province was constituted, called East Bengal and Assam. Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
mcqs.explanation: In 1905, Governor-General Lord Curzon decided to reorganize the provincial boundaries. He divided Bengal into two parts and created a new province called Eastern Bengal and Assam, while the western part consisted of Bengal, Bihar, Orissa and Chota Nagpur. In addition, he also made changes in the boundaries of Madras and the Central Provinces. Thus, both statements are correct.

mcqs.question: The strategy of ‘Divide and Rule’ was adopted by
mcqs.explanation: The strategy of ‘Divide and Rule’ was adopted by both Lord Curzon and Lord Minto. Under this policy, Minto encouraged the system of separate electorates. During the tenure of Lord Curzon, the British government adopted a policy that favoured Muslims and opposed Hindus. The partition of Bengal in 1905 became a symbol of this policy. The objective of the partition of Bengal was not administrative convenience, as was claimed, but two clear purposes—first, to drive a wedge between Hindus and Muslims, and second, to weaken the rising nationalist spirit of Bengal.
mcqs.chapter: Economic Impact of British Rule on India

mcqs.question: The transfer of the capital of British India from Calcutta to Delhi was affected during the period of-
mcqs.explanation: The capital of British India was shifted from Calcutta to Delhi during the viceroyalty of Lord Hardinge. In 1911, Viceroy Lord Hardinge invited King George V and Queen Mary to India and organized a grand Durbar at Delhi. It was in this Durbar that the Partition of Bengal was annulled and the transfer of the capital was announced.
mcqs.chapter: Economic Impact of British Rule on India

mcqs.question: Who among the following was the only Jewish Viceroy of India?
mcqs.explanation: Lord Reading (1921–1926) was the only Jewish Viceroy of India. During his tenure, the Chauri Chaura incident took place, the Swaraj Party was formed, and the Rowlatt Act was repealed.

mcqs.question: The Permanent Settlement was introduced by
mcqs.explanation: In 1793, Lord Cornwallis introduced the Permanent Settlement system of land revenue. It was also known by different names such as Istimrari, Jagirdari, Malguzari, and Biswedari. This system was implemented in Bengal, Bihar, Orissa, and the Benaras region of Uttar Pradesh. It covered about 19 percent of the total area of British India. Under this arrangement, a new class of zamindars was declared as landowners. They had to pay 10/11 of the land revenue to the Company and retain 1/11 for themselves. Under the Permanent Settlement, the zamindars were small capitalists (bhadra nawabs).
mcqs.chapter: Economic Impact of British Rule on India

mcqs.question: Sir Thomas Munro is associated with the land revenue settlement:
mcqs.explanation: The Ryotwari Settlement was a system introduced by the British in India for the collection of land revenue. Alexander Read first implemented the Ryotwari system in 1792 in the Baramahal region of Tamil Nadu in the Madras Presidency. Thomas Munro applied it in some areas in 1809. When he became the Governor of Madras in 1820, he extended it in Madras. Munro’s disciple Elphinstone introduced it in the Bombay Presidency. This system was implemented over about 51 percent of the total area of British India, including Madras, parts of Bombay, Eastern Bengal, Assam. Under this arrangement, the ryots were given ownership rights over the land, and they were directly responsible for paying land revenue. After 1836, improvements were made in this system by Wingate and Goldsmith.
mcqs.chapter: Economic Impact of British Rule on India

mcqs.question: Given below are two statements, one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R) : Assertion (A) : The British Government introduced different land revenue system in different part of India. Reason (R) : It led to create different classes in Indian peasantry. Select the correct answer from the codes given below. Codes :

options.a: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
options.b: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)

mcqs.explanation: The British Government introduced different land-revenue systems in different parts of India. These systems were the Permanent Settlement, the Ryotwari system, and the Mahalwari system. The Permanent Settlement was implemented in Bengal, Bihar, Odisha, and the Banaras region of Uttar Pradesh. It covered about 19 percent of the total area of British India. The Ryotwari system, covering about 51 percent of the area, was implemented in Madras, parts of Bombay, Eastern Bengal, Assam, and Coorg. The Mahalwari system, covering about 30 percent of the area, was implemented in the United Provinces, the Central Provinces, and Punjab, with some modifications. These separate land-revenue systems in different regions gave rise to different classes among Indian peasants. Therefore, both the Assertion and the Reason are true, and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
mcqs.chapter: Economic Impact of British Rule on India

mcqs.question: Which of the following pairs is not correctly matched?
mcqs.explanation: In the Bombay Presidency, the Ryotwari system was chiefly in force. The Taluqdari system was not recognized there as a distinct land-revenue system. Therefore, the pair given in option (d) is not correctly matched, whereas the other options are correctly matched. The Taluqdari system was mainly prevalent in the Awadh region.
mcqs.chapter: Economic Impact of British Rule on India

mcqs.question: When was the first tea company in Assam established?
mcqs.explanation: The first tea company in Assam was established in 1839. It was set up in England with a capital of Rs. 5 lakh, and its headquarters was located at Nazira in Assam. 'The Assam Company' is the oldest commercial tea company in India and continues to function even today.
mcqs.chapter: Economic Impact of British Rule on India

mcqs.question: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below the lists : List-I List-II A. Jajmani 1. North India B. Bara Balute 2. Karnataka C. Mirasi 3. Maharashtra D. Adade 4. Tamil Nadu Codes : A B C D
mcqs.explanation: The correct matching is as follows– Jajmani – North India Bara Balut – Maharashtra Mirasi – Tamil Nadu Adade – Karnataka
mcqs.chapter: Economic Impact of British Rule on India

mcqs.question: What is the total percentage of Central revenue spent on Military force in British India?
mcqs.explanation: Although the answer to such a question is somewhat debatable, many sources indicate that, on average, nearly 40 percent of the central revenue in British India was spent on the military.
mcqs.chapter: Economic Impact of British Rule on India

mcqs.question: Who is the exponent of the Theory of “Economic Drain” of India during the British Rule?
mcqs.explanation: Dadabhai Naoroji was one of the earliest and the most prominent exponent of the Drain of Wealth theory. Through his articles and books – 'England’s' Debt to India, 'Poverty' and Un-British Rule in India, 'The Wants and Means of India', and 'On the Commerce of India' – he explained the theory of the economic drain of India.
mcqs.chapter: Economic Impact of British Rule on India

mcqs.question: Consider the following statements and select the correct answer from the code given below the statements: Assertion (A) : Generally, India had a favourable balance of trade during the British rule. Reason (R) : The drain of wealth took the form of unrequired exports. Code :

options.a: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.b: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

mcqs.explanation: According to the nationalist interpretation, the drain of wealth meant the transfer of wealth, property, and goods from India to England without any equivalent economic, commercial, or material return to India. During the British period, India’s balance of trade was generally favourable because exports exceeded imports. The sources of the East India Company’s drain included profits from trade monopoly, salaries and pensions of Company employees, and dividends paid to its investors. The money sent by the Company to England later returned to India in the form of foreign loans and capital investment. However, this investment was meant not for the development of the country but for the maximum exploitation of Indian resources. After 1813, this economic drain assumed the form of unrequited exports. Before 1914, British capital investment in India was made mainly in such sectors as railways, roads, commercial shipping, mineral industries such as coal and gold, and financial institutions such as banks, insurance companies, and financial corporations. These served as complements to British industry and left no scope for Indian industrial development. Dadabhai Naoroji described the drain of wealth as the “evil of all evils” and regarded it as the chief cause of India’s poverty. Therefore, both (A) and (R) are correct, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
mcqs.chapter: Economic Impact of British Rule on India

mcqs.question: In which year the book 'Poverty and Unbritish Rule in India' was published?
mcqs.explanation: Dadabhai Naoroji propounded the theory of economic drain under British rule in his book 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India'. This book was published in 1901 in London by S. Sonnenschein.

mcqs.question: With reference to ‘deindustrialization’ which of the following statements is/are correct? 1. This process started in 1813. 2. Abolition of monopoly trade rights of East India Company aggravated the process. Select the correct answer from the codes given below:
mcqs.explanation: In India, the process of deindustrialization began with the Charter Act of 1813, which ended the Company’s monopoly over Indian trade. As a result, all British subjects got permission to trade with the East. This was done to expand the Industrial Revolution. Consequently, India became a market for British goods.
mcqs.chapter: Economic Impact of British Rule on India

mcqs.question: What was the main cause of 1857 revolt?
mcqs.explanation: The main cause of the Revolt of 1857 was the evil policies of the British Empire, due to which the long-suppressed rebellion finally erupted.

mcqs.question: With which uprising is Mangal Pandey associated?
mcqs.explanation: On 29 March 1857, at Barrackpore, the soldiers refused to use the greased cartridges, and a sepoy named Mangal Pandey attacked his adjutant.

mcqs.question: Mangal Pandey was the sepoy of –
mcqs.explanation: Mangal Pandey was a soldier (sepoy) in the 6th Company of the 34th Bengal Native Infantry.

mcqs.question: At the time of 1857 Revolt who was the British Commanding Officer at Barrackpore?
mcqs.explanation: In March 1857, at the time of the revolt of Mangal Pandey, a sepoy of the 34th Bengal Native Infantry, at Barrackpore, Lieutenant General Sir John Bennet Hearsey was the British commanding officer there.

mcqs.question: The first war of Independence (1857) started from:
mcqs.explanation: The Revolt of 1857 began from Meerut on 10 May 1857. The soldiers of the 3rd Cavalry Regiment there refused to use the greased cartridges and openly rebelled.

mcqs.question: The first event relating to the war of Independence of 1857 was –

options.a: Kanpur’s Revolt and taking over the leadership by Nana Saheb.
options.b: Begum Hazrat Mahal’s leadership of Oudh.
options.c: Marching of sepoys to Delhi’s Red Fort.

mcqs.explanation: On 11 May 1857, a contingent of sepoys that had arrived in Delhi from Meerut appealed to Mughal Emperor Bahadur Shah II to accept their leadership. Thus, among the given options, the soldiers reaching the Red Fort in Delhi was the first event. Nana Sahib led the revolt at Kanpur on 5 June 1857. Begum Hazrat Mahal and her son Birjis Qadir led the revolt of Awadh (Lucknow), which began on 30 May/4 June 1857. Rani Lakshmibai of Jhansi joined the revolt in June 1857 and was martyred on 17 June 1858.

mcqs.question: Which one of the following (Place of the revolt of 1857- Start of rebellion) is not correctly matched?
mcqs.explanation: The correct matching of the places of the Revolt of 1857 and the dates of the beginning of the revolt is as follows– Lucknow – 30 May/4 June, 1857 Jhansi – June, 1857 Meerut – 10 May, 1857 Barrackpore – 29 March, 1857 Note: In many reference books and official websites, the date of the beginning of the Revolt of 1857 in Lucknow is given as 4 June 1857, whereas in the NCERT Class 12 book, this date is given as 30 May 1857. In its answer key, UPPSC treated option (b) as the correct answer.

mcqs.question: Who among the following was bestowed with the title of Saheb-e-Alam Bahadur by Bahadur Shah during the uprising of 1857?
mcqs.explanation: During the Revolt of 1857, Bahadur Shah conferred the title of ‘Sahib-e-Alam Bahadur’ on Bakht Khan. Bakht Khan was a Pashtun. In the East India Company, he held the rank of Subedar and, on behalf of the Company, he had participated in the First Anglo-Afghan War. Bahadur Shah declared his eldest son, Mirza Mughal, as the commander- in-chief, but the real leadership of the revolt remained in the hands of Bakht Khan.

mcqs.question: Which one of the following centres of the uprising of 1857 was recaptured by the English?
mcqs.explanation: Among the centres of the Revolt of 1857 mentioned above, Delhi was the first to be recaptured by the British. After a siege of three months, Delhi was recaptured by the British on 20 September 1857.

mcqs.question: Lord Dalhousie recognised the adopted son of Rani Lakshmi Bai as the heir apparent. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
mcqs.explanation: In 1857–58, the revolt at Jagdishpur in Bihar was led by the local zamindar, Kunwar Singh. Therefore, statement 1 is correct. According to Lord Dalhousie’s Doctrine of Lapse, if an Indian ruler died without a natural son, the state was annexed by the British East India Company. When Raja Gangadhar Rao of Jhansi died in 1853 without a natural heir, Rani Lakshmibai adopted Damodar Rao as her son and declared him the heir to Jhansi, but Dalhousie refused to recognize him. Under the Doctrine of Lapse, Jhansi was annexed to the British Empire in 1854. Therefore, statement 2 is incorrect.

mcqs.question: The birthplace of Maharani Laxmi Bai, the heroine of the 1857 freedom struggle, is:
mcqs.explanation: Rani Lakshmibai (original name Manikarnika) was born on 19 November 1835 in Golghar, which is now in Varanasi.

mcqs.question: Who among the following was the leader of the revolt during 1857 at Bareilly?
mcqs.explanation: At Bareilly, Khan Bahadur Khan, the heir of the former rulers of Rohilkhand, led the revolt of 1857. As soon as the wave of revolt spread, he took over the administration himself and organized nearly 40,000 soldiers, thus building a strong force and giving the British a tough fight. Mughal Emperor Bahadur Shah II appointed him as Viceroy.

mcqs.question: Who amongst the following was the leader of the 1857 uprising at Allahabad?
mcqs.explanation: In Allahabad, the rebels in the Revolt of 1857 were led by Maulvi Liaqat Ali. Later, the revolt there was suppressed by General Neill.

mcqs.question: The largest number of soldiers participated in the Struggle of 1857 came from –
mcqs.explanation: In the Revolt of 1857, the largest number of sepoys came from Awadh. In fact, at that time there was hardly any family in Awadh that did not have at least one member in the army. About 75,000 soldiers were in the army from Awadh alone.

mcqs.question: Who was ‘commander-in-chief’ of Nana saheb?
mcqs.explanation: At Kanpur, on 5 June 1857, Nana Sahib was proclaimed Peshwa and independence was declared. Nana Sahib received great assistance from Tatya Tope, who was his Commander-in-Chief.

mcqs.question: The real name of which one of the following leaders of 1857 was ‘Ram Chandra Pandurang’?
mcqs.explanation: Tatya Tope (1814–1859 A.D.) was also known as Ramchandra Pandurang. He was one of the major leaders of the Revolt of 1857.

mcqs.question: Who among the following was the leader of the revolution of 1857 in Assam?
mcqs.explanation: During the Revolt of 1857 in Assam, Diwan Maniram Dutt started the uprising by declaring Kandapeshwar Singh, the grandson of the last king, as king. However, the revolt was soon suppressed and Maniram was hanged.

mcqs.question: Who among the following was not related to the Revolt of 1857?
mcqs.explanation: Udham Singh was not associated with the Revolt of 1857. He was a revolutionary from Punjab. To avenge the Jallianwala Bagh massacre, he killed Michael O’Dwyer, the former Lieutenant Governor of Punjab, in London in March 1940. For this act, he was arrested and sentenced to death. Begum Hazrat Mahal led the revolt in Lucknow, Kunwar Singh in Bihar, and Maulvi Ahmadullah in Faizabad.

mcqs.question: The educated middle class in India:

options.c: Remained neutral to the revolt of 1857

mcqs.explanation: The educated class showed no or very little interest in the Revolt of 1857, which was one of the major reasons for the failure of this great struggle. The manner in which the rebels used superstitions or opposed progressive social measures made educated Indians keep away from them. Thus, the educated middle class in India maintained a kind of neutrality towards the Revolt of 1857.

mcqs.question: The original residence of Eminent Urdu Poet Mirza Ghalib was?
mcqs.explanation: The Urdu poet Mirza Ghalib was born on 27 December 1797 in Agra and died on 15 February 1869 in Delhi. He witnessed the Revolt of 1857 with his own eyes.

mcqs.question: Match List I with the List II and select the correct answer by using the code given below : List-I List-II A. Jhansi 1. Maulvi Ahmad Shah B. Lucknow 2. Azimullah Khan C. Kanpur 3. Begum Hazrat Mahal D. Faizabad 4. Rani Laxmibai Code : A B C D
mcqs.explanation: In the Revolt of 1857, Rani Lakshmibai led the revolt in Jhansi, Begum Hazrat Mahal in Lucknow, Azimullah Khan in Kanpur and Fatehpur, and Maulvi Ahmad Shah (Maulvi Ahmadullah Shah) in Faizabad.

mcqs.question: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below the lists: List-I List-II (Name of the (Place) Revolutionaries) A. Nana Saheb 1. Delhi B. Nawab Hamid Ali Khan 2. Kanpur C. Moulvi Ahmed Ullah 3. Lucknow D. Mani Ram Diwan 4. Assam Code : A B C D
mcqs.explanation: Revolutionary Place Nana Saheb – Kanpur Nawab Hamid Ali Khan – Delhi Maulvi Ahmadullah – Lucknow Maniram Diwan – Assam

mcqs.question: Who was the Governor-General of India during the revolt of 1857?
mcqs.explanation: At the time of the Revolt of 1857, Lord Canning was the Governor-General of India. Lord Canning was the last Governor-General of India appointed by the Company (1856–58 A.D.) and the first Viceroy of India appointed under the British Crown (1858-62 A.D.).

mcqs.question: Who made Allahabad the emergency headquarters in 1857?
mcqs.explanation: During the Revolt of 1857, the then Governor-General, Lord Canning, made Allahabad the emergency headquarters.

mcqs.question: Who was the British Prime minister during the revolt of 1857 ?
mcqs.explanation: At the time of the Revolt of 1857 in India, Viscount Palmerston (Henry John Temple, 3rd Viscount Palmerston) was the Prime Minister of Britain. His tenure lasted from 1855 to 1858 A.D. and again from 1859 to 1865 A.D.

mcqs.question: Whose name, amongst the following is not associated with the Revolt of 1857?
mcqs.explanation: None of the names given in the options is associated with the Revolt of 1857.

mcqs.question: The first freedom struggle of 1857 failed because –

options.a: There was lack of the unity of purpose in Indian sepoys
options.c: British soldiers were better equipped and organised rather than Indians

mcqs.explanation: Whatever may have been the reasons for the lack of unity among Indians during the revolt, it proved fatal for the rebellion. This was not the only weakness that undermined the objective of the rebels. The Indian sepoys were brave and selfless, but they lacked discipline and unity. The armies of Bombay and Madras remained loyal to the British. The feudal elements of Awadh, Rohilkhand, and other parts of northern India led the revolt, but, on the other hand, other feudal forces, such as the rulers of Patiala, Jind, Gwalior, and Hyderabad, helped in suppressing it. From the point of view of strategy and military skill too, the British forces were far ahead of the Indian rebels. They were much better equipped than the Indian sepoys. Thus, all of the above reasons were responsible for the failure of the Revolt of 1857.

mcqs.question: Which among the following British officers lost their lives at Lucknow? 1. General John Nicholson 2. General Neil 3. Major Havelock 4. Sir Henry Lawrence Select the correct answer from the code given below –
mcqs.explanation: On 14 September 1857, British General John Nicholson was wounded during the British recapture of Delhi, and he died on 23 September 1857. During the Revolt of 1857 in Lucknow, Sir Henry Lawrence, Major General Havelock, and General Neill died while defending the British Residency.

mcqs.question: Who termed the uprising of 1857 as the first war of independence?
mcqs.explanation: V.D. Savarkar, in his book 'The Indian War of Independence 1857', described the Revolt of 1857 as a well-planned war of independence. He called it the first war of independence.

mcqs.question: The official historian of Indian Freedom struggle was:
mcqs.explanation: Surendra Nath Sen (S.N. Sen) was the official historian of the freedom movement of 1857. His book 'Eighteen Fifty- Seven' was published in 1957.

mcqs.question: The first Indian to write in Indian language on the causes of the uprising of 1857 was.
mcqs.explanation: The book 'Asbab-e-Baghawat-e-Hind', written by Sir Syed Ahmad Khan, was published in 1859, in which the causes of the Revolt of 1857 were discussed.

mcqs.question: The statement “the so-called first national war of independence was neither first, nor national, nor a war of independence’ is associated with
mcqs.explanation: R.C. Majumdar independently published his book 'The Sepoy Mutiny and the Revolt of 1857' in 1957. It was Majumdar who said about the Revolt of 1857 that “the so- called First War of National Independence was neither the first, nor national, nor a war of independence.”

mcqs.question: Which one of the following conceptions is true about the Revolt of 1857?

options.a: Indian historians have described it as an Indian mutiny.
options.b: British historians have described it as a war of independence.
options.c: It gave a death blow to the system of East India Company’s rule in India
options.d: It was for the improvement of the administrative machinery in India

mcqs.explanation: As a result of the Revolt of 1857, the reins of administration in India passed from the hands of the Company to the British Crown, and the system of governance was also radically transformed. Therefore, in the context of the Revolt of 1857, only option (c) is correct, while the other statements are incorrect.

mcqs.question: Indians were assured of many things in the declaration by Queen Victoria in 1858. Which among the following assurances was fulfilled by the British Government:

options.a: Policy of annexation will be abandoned
options.b: ‘status quo’ of the native rulers would be maintained
options.c: Equal treatment would be given to all subjects, Indians, and Europeans
options.d: There would be no interference in the social and religious beliefs of the Indians

mcqs.explanation: The most important result of the Revolt of 1857 was Queen Victoria’s Proclamation. This proclamation was announced by Lord Canning at the Allahabad Durbar held on 1 November 1858. Through it, Company rule in India was ended and the administration of India was brought directly under the Crown. This proclamation included a halt to the expansion of the British Empire in India, non-interference in people’s religious matters, and equal legal protection for all. The policy of conquest and annexation towards the Indian princely states was abandoned, and the government granted the rulers the right of adoption; however, the other assurances could not be fulfilled by British rule.

mcqs.question: Match List-I with List-II and choose the correct answer using the codes given below the lists: List-I List-II (Revolt) (Leader) A. Paika Revolt 1. Edachena Kungan B. Bareilly Revolt 2. Radharam C. Malabar Revolt 3. Mufti Muhammad Aiwaz D. Sylhet Revolt 4. Jagabandhu Bidyadhar Mahapatra Codes: A B C D
mcqs.explanation: Bakshi Jagabandhu was the leader of the Paika Revolt of 1817, which took place in Khordha in present-day Odisha. He was born at Rorunga near Puri, and his real name was Jagabandhu Vidyadhar Mahapatra Bhramarbar Ray. The Bareilly Revolt of 1816 took place against the new police tax, and it was led by the religious leader Mufti Mohammad Aiwaz. Edachana Kungan Nair was the military commander of the Nair army of Kerala Varma Pazhassiraja in Wayanad during 1797–1805, and he revolted against British colonial oppression; this revolt is known as the Malabar Revolt. The Sylhet Revolt of 1786, also known as the Chargola Revolt and the Pratapgarh Revolt, was an uprising against British rule led by Radharam, the zamindar of Chargola.

mcqs.question: Who was the author of the play ‘Nil Darpan’?
mcqs.explanation: Soon after the Revolt of 1857, the Indigo Revolt (1859–60) took place in Bengal against the oppression of the European indigo planters. The atrocities of the indigo planters were vividly depicted by Dinabandhu Mitra in his play 'Nil Darpan'.

mcqs.question: The theme of the Bankimchandra Chatterjee's famous novel Anandmath is based on:
mcqs.explanation: The song Vande Mataram has been taken from Bankim Chandra Chatterjee’s famous work Anandamath. The plot of this novel is based on the Sanyasi Revolt.

mcqs.question: Which one of the following pairs is not correctly matched? Revolt Year
mcqs.explanation: The correct matching is as follows– Revolt Year Pabna Revolt - 1873-76 Deccan Peasant Revolt - 1875 Sanyasi Revolt - 1763-1800 Kol Revolt - 1831-32

mcqs.question: Consider the following revolts and arrange them in correct chronological order. 1. Pabna 2. Indigo 3. Kuka 4. Sanyasi Select the correct answer from the code given below : Code :
mcqs.explanation: The chronology of these revolts is as follows : Sanyasi Revolt (Bengal): approximately 1763–1800. Indigo Revolt (Bengal): a widespread peasant movement against the forced cultivation of indigo in 1859–60. Kuka (Namdhari) Revolt (Punjab): the major incidents of armed conflict and severe repression in the Namdhari/Kuka movement took place in 1871–72. Pabna Peasant Movement (Bengal): this movement was carried on mainly during 1873–76 by peasants against the oppression of zamindars, illegal cesses, forced levies, and enhancement of rent. Therefore, the correct chronological order is given in option (d).

mcqs.question: Chief centre of Wahabi Movement during 19th century was:
mcqs.explanation: The most organized and serious challenge to British supremacy came from the Wahabi Movement. Syed Ahmad Barelvi of Rae Bareli was the pioneer of this movement in India. He was influenced by Abdul Wahab of Arabia, but an even greater influence on him was that of Shah Waliullah, a saint of Delhi. Due to the efforts of Syed Ahmad Barelvi, the ideas of this movement soon spread to Kabul, the North-West Frontier Province, Bengal, Bihar, the Central Provinces, etc. For some time, his followers captured Peshawar in 1830 and issued coins in his name, but he was killed the following year in the Battle of Balakot. After the death of Syed Ahmad Barelvi, Patna became the centre of this movement. During this period, the movement was led by Maulvi Qasim, Vilayat Ali, Inayat Ali, Ahmadullah, etc. Besides Patna, branches of this movement were also established in Hyderabad, Madras, Bengal, the United Provinces, and Bombay. The Wahabis made a significant contribution to the spread of anti-British feeling during the Revolt of 1857.

mcqs.question: Kuka Movement was founded in
mcqs.explanation: The Kuka Movement began in western Punjab in the 1840s under Bhagat Jawaharmal, who was mainly known as Sian Sahib. The objective was to remove the evils and superstitions prevalent in Sikhism and to purify the religion. However, later it developed into a political movement under the leadership of Ram Singh. In 1872, the leader of this movement, Ram Singh, was deported to Rangoon, where he died in 1885.

mcqs.question: The Pagalpanthi rebellion was indeed a rebellion of :
mcqs.explanation: Pagalpanth was a semi-religious sect. It was actually a revolt of the Garo tribe, launched by Karam Shah of northern Bengal. Titu, the son and successor of Karam Shah, was inspired by both religious and political motives. He organized a movement against the oppression of tenants by zamindars. In 1825, Titu captured Sherpur and set himself up as king.

mcqs.question: Who among the following was the leader of the Farazi rebellion:
mcqs.explanation: The Faraizis were followers of the sect started by Haji Shariatullah of Faridpur in Bengal. They advocated major religious, social, and political changes. Shariatullah’s son, Dadu Miyan/Dudu Miyan, planned to drive the British out of Bengal. The Faraizi Movement continued from 1818 to 1862; in the end, the followers of this sect joined the Wahabi group.

mcqs.question: Velu Thampi led a rebellion against the British in
mcqs.explanation: In 1805, Wellesley compelled the Maharaja of Travancore (Kerala) to accept a Subsidiary Alliance. The Maharaja was dissatisfied with the terms of the treaty and therefore delayed payment of the subsidy due under the alliance, with the arrears continuing to accumulate. The behaviour of the British Resident was also highly arrogant. As a result, the Diwan, Velu Thampi, revolted, and the Nair Battalion supported him. The British had to send a large army to suppress this revolt.

mcqs.question: Which of the following places was the centre of the Gadakari rebellion:
mcqs.explanation: The Gadkaris were hereditary employees who served in the forts of the Marathas. In 1844, they revolted in Kolhapur against arbitrary land revenue collection, their removal from service in the Maratha army, and the transfer of their lands to the supervision of mamlatdars. The government had to make considerable efforts to suppress this revolt.

mcqs.question: There was a time when Santhals enjoyed full sovereignty over the area of Ganga valley near Muzaffarpur. Codes:
mcqs.explanation: In July 1855, the Santhals raised the banner of revolt. Major Burrough from Calcutta and a military detachment from Purnea were sent to suppress them, but they were defeated by the Santhals at the field of Pir Painti near Bhagalpur. Later, the revolt was suppressed by Captain Alexander. Godda is now a district in the Santhal Pargana Division of Jharkhand. Gokko was an important leader from this area.
