The moneylender Din Dayal Rai was also among the exploiters. The Santhals did not have dominance over the Gangetic valley region. This revolt spread from Bhagalpur to Burdwan (modern Bardhaman).

mcqs.question: Which one of the following uprisings occurred in Maharastra?
mcqs.explanation: Bhil Revolt – The Bhils, a tribal community, lived in Khandesh on the western side, which is now part of Maharashtra. From 1818 to 1831, they revolted against their new rulers, the British. In 1825, the Bhils revolted under the leadership of Sevaram. Kol Revolt – This revolt spread across Ranchi, Singhbhum, Hazaribagh, Palamu, and the western parts of Manbhum. Rampa Revolt – This revolt took place in the hilly Rampa region situated to the north of the Godavari district in Andhra Pradesh. This tribal revolt was directed against exploitation by moneylenders and against forest laws. Santhal Revolt – This revolt, which took place in 1855–56, was mainly centred in the region between Bhagalpur and Rajmahal.

mcqs.question: Who was the leader of Munda rebellion?
mcqs.explanation: Birsa Munda, the leader of the Munda Revolt, was known as Dharti Aba (Father of the World), and his revolt is known as ‘Ulgulan’ (the Great Revolt or Great Upheaval). The Munda Revolt began in opposition to the change from the traditional collective land system, known as Khuntkatti or Mundari, to a zamindari or individually held land system. Later, Birsa gave it the form of a religious and political movement. The revolt of the Munda tribals took place between 1899 and 1900.

mcqs.question: Match List -I with List - II and select correct answer from the code given below the lists. List–I List-II (Revolt/Movement) (Year) A. Tebhaga Movement 1. 1859-60 B. Mopla Rebellion 2. 1879-80 C. Pabana Peasant Revolt 3. 1921 D. Bengal Indigo Revolt 4. 1946-47 Codes : A B C D
mcqs.explanation: The correct matching is as follows— Tebhaga Movement – 1946-47 Moplah Revolt – 1921 Pabna Peasant Revolt – 1873-76 Bengal Indigo Revolt – 1859-60 Note: In this question, the year of the Pabna Peasant Revolt has been given as 1879-80, which is incorrect. The matching of the other three is correct. Therefore, the nearest correct answer may be taken as option (d).

mcqs.question: Match List- I with List- II and select the correct answer using the code given below the lists : List- I (Movement) List- II (Year) A. Pabana Rebellion 1. 1855-56 B. Eka Movement 2. 1873-85 C. Santhal Rebellion 3. 1922 D. Tana Bhagal Movement 4. 1914 Code : A B C D
mcqs.explanation: The correct matching of the above movements and their years is as follows– Pabna Revolt – 1873-85 Eka Movement – 1922 Santhal Revolt – 1855-56 Tana Bhagat Movement – 1914 Note: In 1885, the Bengal Tenancy Act clearly defined the rights of peasants over land, which was the main demand of the Pabna Movement. The movement remained intense from 1873 to 1876. Thereafter, it continued only as a legal dispute.

mcqs.question: Who started the Eka movement?

options.d: Farmers of Hardoi, Barabanki and other places of Uttar Pradesh

mcqs.explanation: The Eka Movement (1921-22) was started by peasants in the districts of Hardoi, Bahraich, Sitapur, etc. in Uttar Pradesh. The main issue of this movement was the collection of rent at 50 percent above the fixed rate. This movement was led by Madari Pasi, a leader from a backward caste community.

mcqs.question: Match the List-I with List-II and select the correct answer from the codes given below: List–I List-II A. Rampa Rebellion 1. 1859-60 B. Pabana Peasant Revolt 2. 1879-80 C. Bengal Indigo Revolt 3. 1860-63 D. Jaintia Rebellion 4. 1873-76 Codes : A B C D
mcqs.explanation: The correct matching is as follows– Bengal Indigo Revolt – 1859-60 Pabna Peasant Revolt – 1873-76 Rampa Revolt – 1879-80 Jaintia Revolt – 1860-63

mcqs.question: The ‘Moplah Revolt’ of 1921 took place in :
mcqs.explanation: The Muslim tenants (Kanamdars) and cultivators (Verumpattamdars) of South Malabar (Kerala) were called Moplahs. Here, the landlords belonged to the upper-caste Hindu communities, namely the Nambudiris and the Nayars. There were two causes behind the Moplah Revolt of 1921– first, the oppression by landlords, and second, the policies of the British government opposed to the Khilafat movement.

mcqs.question: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer by using the code given below the lists : List-I List-II (Events) (Dates) A. Barrackpur Mutiny 1. July, 1806 B. Berhampur Revolt 2. November, 1824 C. Santhal Revolt 3. 1855-56 D. Vellore Mutiny 4. February, 1857 Code : A B C D
mcqs.explanation: The revolt at Barrackpore took place in November, 1824. The revolt at Berhampore took place in February, 1857. The Santhal Revolt took place in 1855-56 under the leadership of Sidho and Kanhu. In 1806, the soldiers revolted at Vellore due to interference in their social and religious customs and raised the flag of the King of Mysore.

mcqs.question: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer from the codes given below : List-I List-II (Rebellion) (Year A.D.) A. Ahom i. 1855-56 B. Kol ii. 1828 C. Santhal iii. 1921 D. Moplah iv. 1831-32 Codes : A B C D
mcqs.explanation: The correct matching is as follows– Revolt Year (A.D.) Ahom – 1828 Kol – 1831-32 Santhal – 1855-56 Moplah – 1921

mcqs.question: Which of the following is not correctly matched?
mcqs.explanation: The Moplah Rebellion was launched by the Moplahs in the Malabar region of Kerala in 1921. The Kuka Rebellion began in Punjab in the 1840s under the leadership of Bhagat Jawahar Mal. The Koli Rebellion took place in Maharashtra during 1784–1785. The Chuar revolt of Midnapore (West Bengal) against British rule took place in 1768.

mcqs.question: Which one of the following pairs is not correctly matched?
mcqs.explanation: The Munda Rebellion took place in 1899–1900 in the southern parts of Ranchi. Its leader was Birsa Munda. The Santhal Rebellion took place in 1855–56. Its leaders were Sidho and Kanhu. The Ahom Rebellion began in 1828. Its leader was Gomdhar Kunwar. The Tana Bhagat Movement began in 1914 among the Oraon tribals of Chotanagpur. Its leaders included Jatra Bhagat, Balram Bhagat, and Devmenia Bhagat.

mcqs.question: Tripura Choose the right answer from this code : Code : A B C D
mcqs.explanation: The Kuki Rebellion (1917–19) took place in Manipur and Tripura; the Kuka Rebellion (1840–72) in Punjab; the Pabna Rebellion (1873–76) in Bengal; and the Birsa Munda Rebellion (1899–1900) in Bihar (present-day Jharkhand).

mcqs.question: Which of the above pairs is not correctly matched? Rebellion Year
mcqs.explanation: Under the leadership of Gomdhar Kunwar, the Ahom Rebellion began in 1828, but it was suppressed by the East India Company. Under the leadership of Tirot Singh, the Garo, Khasi, and Singhpo people of the Jaintia and Garo Hills took part in the Khasi Rebellion (1829–1833). In the Chotanagpur region, the Kol Rebellion was led in 1831–32 by Buddhu or Budho Bhagat. The Santhal Rebellion of 1855–56 was a famous tribal uprising led by four brothers— Sidhu, Kanhu, Chand, and Bhairav. Therefore, among the given pairs, option (d) is not correctly matched.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched ? (Revolts) (Years)
mcqs.explanation: The Kuka Movement began in the 1840s under Bhagat Jawahar Mal. Its objective was to purify the Sikh religion by removing the evils and superstitions prevalent within it, whereas the Kuki Rebellion began in 1917. This rebellion was directed against the British labour recruitment drive under the Labour Corps scheme. This movement continued until March 1919.

mcqs.question: The people known as 'Kallar' in the context of the rebellions in British India belonged to which of the following regions?
mcqs.explanation: The ‘Kallar’ were a tribal community of South India. In British India, the Kallar tribe revolted against the British. This tribe belonged to Madurai and the surrounding region of South India.

mcqs.question: Where was the first Madarsa set up by British in India?
mcqs.explanation: In 1780, Warren Hastings established a Madrasa in Calcutta.
mcqs.chapter: Development of Education in Modern India

mcqs.question: The Asiatic Society of Bengal was founded by
mcqs.explanation: In 1784, Sir William Jones, an associate of Warren Hastings, founded the ‘Asiatic Society of Bengal’ for the study of the social and natural history of Asia, archaeology, art, science, and literature. In 1791, as a result of the efforts of Jonathan Duncan, the British Resident at Banaras, the first Sanskrit College was opened at Banaras.
mcqs.chapter: Development of Education in Modern India

mcqs.question: Given below are two statements, one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R). Assertion (A) : The Asiatic Society of Bengal was established in the period of Warren Hastings and he modestly declined the offer of Presidentship of the learned body in favour of Sir William Jones. Reason (R) : Warren Hastings was himself a great scholar and an ardent orientalist who used to encourage the study of Sanskrit, Persian and Arabic. Select the correct answer from the codes given below. Codes :

options.a: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
options.b: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not a correct explanation of (A)

mcqs.explanation: Warren Hastings was the Governor-General of Bengal during 1774–85. He was himself an eminent scholar and a strong supporter of Oriental learning, who encouraged the study of Sanskrit, Persian, and Arabic. It was with his cooperation and support that the Asiatic Society of Bengal was established in 1784. However, he declined the proposal to accept the presidency of this institution in favour of Sir William Jones. Charles Wilkins, Nathaniel Halhed, Jonathan Duncan, and others contributed to the study of Oriental learning under the patronage and support of Warren Hastings. The preface to the English translation of the 'Bhagavad Gita' by Charles Wilkins was also written by Warren Hastings. According to the question, the statement mentions two things— (1) the establishment of the Asiatic Society, and (2) Warren Hastings declining to accept its presidency in favour of William Jones. The reason describes his own scholarship and his encouragement of the study of Oriental learning. Here, his encouragement of Oriental learning confirms that it was the reason behind both parts of the statement. Thus, it is clear that both the statement and the reason are correct, and the reason is the correct explanation of the statement. The Commission had given option (b) as the answer to this question, which is not appropriate. The correct answer should be option (a).
mcqs.chapter: Development of Education in Modern India

mcqs.question: Who among the following was offered membership of the Royal Asiatic Society of Paris?
mcqs.explanation: Among the persons given in the question, Michael Madhusudan Dutt was granted membership of the Royal Asiatic Society.
mcqs.chapter: Development of Education in Modern India

mcqs.question: Who among the following was the first to translate Kalidasa’s famous work ‘Shakuntala’ into English?
mcqs.explanation: Sir William Jones translated Kalidasa’s 'Abhijnanashakun- talam' into English in 1789, and five editions of this translation were published.
mcqs.chapter: Development of Education in Modern India

mcqs.question: Which Act of British Government granted Rs. One lakh for education in India for the first time?
mcqs.explanation: Under the Charter Act of 1813, the Company for the first time assumed governmental responsibility for education. This Act made provision for spending one lakh rupees annually on education.
mcqs.chapter: Development of Education in Modern India

mcqs.question: In the Hunter Commission report, special emphasis was laid on the development of:
mcqs.explanation: To review the progress made in the field of education after 1854, Lord Ripon appointed the first Indian Education Commission in 1882 under the chairmanship of W.W. Hunter. The report of this commission laid special emphasis on the improvement and development of primary education.
mcqs.chapter: Development of Education in Modern India

mcqs.question: Sadler Commission was related to:
mcqs.explanation: The Sadler Commission was related to education. In 1917, the government appointed a commission to study the problems and prospects of Calcutta University and to submit a report. Dr. M.E. Sadler, the Vice-Chancellor of Leeds University, was appointed its Chairman. The Commission was of the view that if university education was to be improved, reform in secondary education was essential.
mcqs.chapter: Development of Education in Modern India

mcqs.question: Arrange the following events in their chronological order and select the correct answer from the codes given below: A. Hunter Commission B. Sadler Commission C. Wood’s Despatch D. Sargeant Plan Codes :
mcqs.explanation: Wood’s Despatch was issued on 19 July 1854 by Charles Wood, the President of the Board of Control. The Hunter Commission was appointed in 1882 during the tenure of Lord Ripon (1880–1884). The Sadler Commission was constituted in 1917 under the chairmanship of Dr. M.E. Sadler to study the problems of Calcutta University. The Sargent Plan was put forward in 1944 by the Central Advisory Board of Education. At that time, John Sargent was serving as the Educational Adviser to the Government of British India, and this “National Education Plan” was named after him. Therefore, option (d) is the correct answer.
mcqs.chapter: Development of Education in Modern India

mcqs.question: Lord Macaulay was related to:
mcqs.explanation: In order to settle the language controversy in the Indian education system, William Bentinck asked Lord Macaulay, the Law Member of his Council, to give his opinion on the issue. Macaulay supported English as the medium of education in India.
mcqs.chapter: Development of Education in Modern India

mcqs.question: The propounder of “Filtration Theory” in India’s education policy was :
mcqs.explanation: During the colonial period in India, “the theory of downward filtration” was related to education. According to this theory, education should be given first to the upper classes of society, from whom its benefits would gradually filter down to the common people. Macaulay, the propounder of this theory, believed that with limited resources it was impossible to educate the entire population.
mcqs.chapter: Development of Education in Modern India

mcqs.question: In whose reign was English Education introduced in India?
mcqs.explanation: During the tenure of Governor-General Lord William Cavendish Bentinck (1828–35), Macaulay’s proposal was approved on 7 March 1835, and English was made the medium of higher education in India. In India, the supporters of English education were led by Munro and Elphinstone, whereas H.T. Prinsep led the supporters of Orientalist education.
mcqs.chapter: Development of Education in Modern India

mcqs.question: The establishment of the first Women’s University in Mumbai was the result of the effort of
mcqs.source: U.P. P.C.S. (Mains) 2002; U.P. P.S.C. (GIC) 2010 U.P. U.D.A./L.D.A. (Pre) 2006
mcqs.explanation: It was through the persistent efforts of D.K. Karve that the first women’s university was established in 1916. He was a social reformer from Maharashtra.
mcqs.chapter: Development of Education in Modern India

mcqs.question: Who was associated with the formation of the Deccan Educational Society?
mcqs.explanation: The background to the Deccan Education Society began in Pune in 1880 with the establishment of the New English School, and the Deccan Education Society was formally constituted in 1884. Among its principal founders were V.K. Chiplunkar, B.G. Tilak, M.B. Namjoshi, and Gopal Ganesh Agarkar. Justice Ranade was not a founder of this society; rather, he was one of its five patrons.
mcqs.chapter: Development of Education in Modern India

mcqs.question: Which of the following was established first?
mcqs.explanation: Raja Rammohan Roy was among the earliest advocates of modern education. In 1817, he, along with David Hare and Alexander Duff, established the famous Hindu College at Calcutta. Mayo College was established in 1875 at Ajmer; the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College was originally founded as Madrasatul Uloom at Aligarh in 1875 and was transformed into the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College in 1877; and Delhi College was established in 1824.
mcqs.chapter: Development of Education in Modern India

mcqs.question: Which one of the following statements is not correct about William A.J. Archbold?

options.a: He was the Principal of Government College, Dacca.
options.b: He was the Principal of Lahore College, Lahore.
options.c: He was the Principal of MAO College, Aligarh.
options.d: He was the Principal of the Muir Central College, Allahabad

mcqs.explanation: William Arthur Jobson Archbold (1865–1947) was a distinguished historian and academic administrator. He served as the Principal of the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental (M.A.O.) College, Aligarh, from 1905 to 1909. While serving in this position, he also played an important role in organizing the meeting held at Simla in 1906 between Viceroy Lord Minto II and the Muslim deputation. After resigning from the post of Principal of M.A.O. College, he also served as the Principal of Government College, Dacca, and Muir Central College, Allahabad (present-day Prayagraj). William A.J. Archbold did not serve as the Principal of Lahore College, Lahore. Therefore, statement (b) is not correct.
mcqs.chapter: Development of Education in Modern India

mcqs.question: With reference to the Fort William College Calcutta. Which of the statement/s is/are correct? 1. It was founded on 10th June, 1800 A.D. within the Fort William Complex in Calcutta. 2. The main purpose of establishing this college, was to teach Indian languages to British officers. Select the correct answer using the code given below : Code -
mcqs.explanation: Fort William College was established at Calcutta on 10 July, 1800 by Wellesley, the then Governor-General of the East India Company. The main objective of establishing this college was to impart education in Indian languages, especially Persian and Hindustani, to British civil servants for administrative purposes in India.
mcqs.chapter: Development of Education in Modern India

mcqs.question: Who one of the following had vigorously advocated for religious education in the Indian universities?
mcqs.explanation: Madan Mohan Malaviya strongly advocated religious education in Indian universities. He was a leading nationalist and patriot.
mcqs.chapter: Development of Press in Modern India

mcqs.question: Who established the Central Hindu College in Banaras, which later emerged as the focal point of Banaras Hindu University?
mcqs.explanation: The Central Hindu College was established at Varanasi on 7 July, 1898 by Annie Besant. Later, when Banaras Hindu University (BHU) was established in 1916 with the cooperation of Annie Besant and the efforts of Madan Mohan Malaviya, this college was incorporated into the newly formed university in 1917. At present, this institution functions as a constituent institution of BHU.
mcqs.chapter: Development of Education in Modern India

mcqs.question: Who among the following laid the foundation stone of Banaras Hindu University:
mcqs.explanation: The foundation stone of Banaras Hindu University was laid on 4 February, 1916, on the day of Vasant Panchami, by the then Viceroy, Lord Hardinge.
mcqs.chapter: Development of Education in Modern India

mcqs.question: Which one of the following was the first to be declared as Central University?
mcqs.explanation: Among the universities given, Banaras Hindu University, Varanasi, was the first to be granted the status of a Central University. The credit for its establishment in 1916 goes to Mahamana Madan Mohan Malaviya.
mcqs.chapter: Development of Education in Modern India

mcqs.question: The first newspaper in India was –
mcqs.explanation: The first newspaper published in India was 'The Bengal Gazette'. Initially, William Bolts attempted to publish a newspaper, but the East India Company sent him back to England. In 1780, James Augustus Hicky began publishing a newspaper titled 'The Bengal Gazette'.
mcqs.chapter: Development of Press in Modern India

mcqs.question: Who among the following had primarily implemented the Press Censorship?
mcqs.explanation: Lord Wellesley introduced press censorship in 1799 and imposed wartime censorship on newspapers. According to this—
mcqs.chapter: Development of Press in Modern India

mcqs.question: Who among the following introduced the Vernacular Press Act?
mcqs.explanation: The Vernacular Press Act was passed in 1878 during the tenure of Lord Lytton (1876–1880 A.D.). This Act was called the “Gagging Act.” Lord Ripon repealed the Vernacular Press Act, or the Native Language Press Act, in 1882 and granted newspapers published in Indian languages the same freedom as English-language newspapers.
mcqs.chapter: Development of Press in Modern India

mcqs.question: Who was the first Indian to go to jail in performance of his duty as a journalist:
mcqs.explanation: According to historian Dhananjay Keer’s book 'Lokmanya Tilak–Father of the Indian Freedom Struggle', Bal Gangadhar Tilak and Gopal Ganesh Agarkar were confined in Dongri Jail, Bombay (Mumbai), on 17 July 1882 to serve four months’ imprisonment for their journalistic writings in the newspapers 'Maratha' and 'Kesari'. This was the first occasion on which any Indian was sentenced to imprisonment while performing his duties as a journalist. However, Bipin Chandra and others, in the English edition of their book 'India’s Struggle for Independence', have stated that Surendranath Banerjee was the first Indian to be imprisoned for discharging his duties as a journalist. But Banerjee received this punishment on 2 April 1883 for his editorial published in 'The Bengalee'. Thus, chronologically, Bal Gangadhar Tilak and Gopal Ganesh Agarkar were the first Indians to go to jail for discharging journalistic duties.
mcqs.chapter: Development of Press in Modern India

mcqs.question: Given below are two statements, in which one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R): Assertion (A): Raja Ram Mohan Roy was the Editor of "sambad Kaumudi", a Bengali weekly. Reason (R) : His articles condemning the custom of widow burning were published in it. Select the correct answer using the code given below: Code -

options.a: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is correct explanation of (A).
options.c: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not correct explanation of (A).

mcqs.explanation: In 1821, Raja Rammohan Roy started the Bengali weekly newspaper 'Sambad Kaumudi'. Interestingly, Raja Rammohan Roy’s name did not appear in the credits of this newspaper. Instead, the newspaper was officially edited by Bhabanicharan Bandyopadhyay and others. This newspaper was not only at the forefront of the movement against 'sati', but it also supported several other progressive values. Raja Rammohan Roy’s articles condemning 'sati' were published in it.
mcqs.chapter: Development of Press in Modern India

mcqs.question: Persian Weekly ‘Miratul Akhbar’ was Published by:
mcqs.explanation: Raja Rammohan Roy propagated his ideas through the press. In December 1821, he began publishing the Bengali weekly 'Sambad Kaumudi'. A year later, he started publishing another weekly newspaper in Persian, 'Mirat-ul-Akhbar'.
mcqs.chapter: Development of Press in Modern India

mcqs.question: From where the ‘Indian Mirror’ newspaper was published in 1880?
mcqs.explanation: The newspaper 'Indian Mirror' was published from Calcutta (Bengal). 'Indian Mirror' was founded in 1861 by Debendranath Tagore and Manmohan Ghosh. Keshab Chandra Sen and Narendra Nath Sen were associated with its editorial section. It was a daily newspaper.
mcqs.chapter: Development of Press in Modern India

mcqs.question: In which one of the following languages was the first issue of the Journal Gadar published?
mcqs.explanation: The first issue of the Ghadar newspaper was published on 1 November 1913, and it was published in Urdu. From 9 December 1913, it also began to appear in Gurmukhi. This weekly newspaper was also published in Marathi, Hindi, English, and Gujarati. One issue was also published in Pashto.
mcqs.chapter: Development of Press in Modern India

mcqs.question: Which newspaper was started by Lokmanya Bal Gangadhar Tilak to serve the cause of India’s freedom struggle?
mcqs.explanation: In 1881, Lokmanya Bal Gangadhar Tilak started two important newspapers from Bombay, namely Kesari and Maratha, for the service of the Indian freedom struggle.
mcqs.chapter: Development of Press in Modern India

mcqs.question: Which one of the popular magazines of the revolutionary period criticized the Congress for various reasons?
mcqs.explanation: Bangavasi, Kaal, and Kesari were supporters of the revolutionary movement and critics of the moderate policies of the Congress.
mcqs.chapter: Development of Press in Modern India

mcqs.question: Kaal Choose the correct answer from the code given below: Code :
mcqs.explanation: All the three newspapers—Sandhya, Yugantar, and Kaal— advocated revolutionary militant activities during the freedom struggle.
mcqs.chapter: Development of Press in Modern India

mcqs.question: The first editor of the journal ‘Indian Opinion’ was :
mcqs.explanation: Indian Opinion was a journal started by Mahatma Gandhi in South Africa in 1903, and its first editor was Mansukhlal Nazar. He was the secretary of the Natal Congress. This journal was published in Gujarati, Hindi, Tamil, and English.
mcqs.chapter: Development of Press in Modern India

mcqs.question: The ‘Young India’ was started as a weekly by:
mcqs.explanation: Under the supervision of Mahatma Gandhi, Young India was initially published from Bombay as a fortnightly from 7 May 1919. In its early issues, Jamnadas Dwarkadas and Shankarlal Banker were its editors. From 8 October 1919, Mahatma Gandhi became its editor, and it began to be published from Ahmedabad as a weekly. Jamnadas Dwarkadas and Shankarlal Banker were members of Annie Besant’s Home Rule League.
mcqs.chapter: Development of Press in Modern India

mcqs.question: The first Hindi Newspaper ‘Udant Martand’ (30th May, 1826) was published from –
mcqs.explanation: Udant Martand was the first Hindi newspaper. Its publication began on 30 May 1826 from Calcutta as a weekly newspaper. Its publisher and editor was Pandit Jugal Kishore Shukla.
mcqs.chapter: Development of Press in Modern India

mcqs.question: The first newspaper published by the Indians in the English language was:
mcqs.explanation: The first newspaper published in English by an Indian was Gangadhar Bhattacharya’s weekly Bengal Gazette. Among the given options, Hindu Patriot was the first newspaper published in English by Indians. It was started in 1853. The first editor of this newspaper was Girish Chandra Ghosh (1853–55). Harish Chandra Mukherjee (1855–61) and Krishnadas Pal (1861–1884) also served as editors of this newspaper.
mcqs.chapter: Development of Press in Modern India

mcqs.question: Who affiliated himself with the English journal ‘Vande Matram’?
mcqs.explanation: Aurobindo Ghosh was associated with the English weekly Vande Mataram as its editor.
mcqs.chapter: Development of Press in Modern India

mcqs.question: The ‘Swadesh Vahini’ was edited by –
mcqs.explanation: K. Ramakrishna Pillai was the editor of ‘Swadeshvahini’, also known as ‘Swadeshabhimani’.
mcqs.chapter: Development of Press in Modern India

mcqs.question: The English newspaper ‘Independent’ was associated to-
mcqs.explanation: Motilal Nehru started the English newspaper ‘Independent’ while advocating self-government for India.
mcqs.chapter: Development of Press in Modern India

mcqs.question: The first issue of a weekly paper ‘Harijan’ started by Gandhiji was published on February 11, 1933 from which of the following cities?
mcqs.explanation: The first issue of the weekly ‘Harijan’, started by Gandhiji, was published on 11 February 1933 from Poona (now Pune, Maharashtra). At that time, Mahatma Gandhi was in Yeravda Jail, Pune. The editor of this paper was R.V. Shastri.
mcqs.chapter: Development of Press in Modern India

mcqs.question: The Marathi fortnightly ‘Bahishkrit Bharat’ was started by:
mcqs.explanation: B.R. Ambedkar started the Marathi fortnightly ‘Bahishkrit Bharat’ from Bombay in 1927.
mcqs.chapter: Development of Press in Modern India

mcqs.question: Which Urdu newspaper was started by Lajpat Rai from Lahore in 1920?
mcqs.explanation: Lala Lajpat Rai started an Urdu daily, Vande Mataram, and an English weekly, 'The People', from Lahore.
mcqs.chapter: Development of Press in Modern India

mcqs.question: Match list-I with List-II and select the correct answer from the codes given below: List-I List-II (Newspapers) (Editors) A. Hindu 1. Dadabhai Nauroji B. Sudharak 2. Gopal Krishna Gokhale C. Voice of India 3. G. Subramaniya Iyer D. Bengalee 4. Surendra Nath Banerjee Code: A B C D
mcqs.explanation: The editor of 'The Hindu' was G. Subrahmanyam Aiyar, and the moderate leader Gopal Krishna Gokhale was the editor of the newspaper 'Sudharak'. Dadabhai Naoroji was the editor of 'Voice of India', and S.N. Banerjee was the editor of 'Bengali'.
mcqs.chapter: Development of Press in Modern India

mcqs.explanation: 'New India' and 'The Commonweal' were newspapers started by Annie Besant. 'Bombay Chronicle' was started by Pherozeshah Mehta, Searchlight by Sachchidanand Sinha, and 'Leader' by Madan Mohan Malaviya.

mcqs.question: Who among the following had launched the paper ‘Qaumi Awaz’?
mcqs.explanation: The Urdu newspaper Qaumi Awaz was started from Lucknow in 1945 by Jawaharlal Nehru and Rafi Ahmad Kidwai. Its editor was Hayatullah Ansari.

mcqs.explanation: The newspaper 'Rast Goftar' is associated with Dadabhai Naoroji. mcqs.explanation: 'Bombay Chronicle' was an English-language newspaper started by Sir Pherozeshah Mehta. This newspaper was published from Bombay (present-day Mumbai).

mcqs.explanation: ‘The Commonweal’ and ‘New India’ were the newspapers brought out by Annie Besant.
mcqs.chapter: Development of Press in Modern India

mcqs.question: To whom Commonweal is related?
mcqs.explanation: ‘The Commonweal’ was an English journal published from Madras, of which Annie Besant was the editor.
mcqs.chapter: Development of Press in Modern India

mcqs.chapter: Development of Press in Modern India

mcqs.question: Who was the editor of the revolutionary paper ‘Vande Mataram’?
mcqs.explanation: The newspaper ‘Vande Mataram’ was first published from Calcutta on 6 August 1906. From 6 August to 15 October 1906, Bipin Chandra Pal was its editor. From 24 October 1906 to 27 May 1907, Aurobindo Ghosh was its editor. At that time, the paper was published daily, but from 2 June 1907, its weekly publication also began. From 28 May to 22 December 1907, under the editorship of Aurobindo Ghosh, both the daily and weekly editions of the paper continued to be published. However, later the publication of this newspaper was discontinued. Again, on 10 September 1909, the first paper under the name ‘Vande Mataram’ was published from Paris, whose editor was Lala Hardayal. The publication and distribution of this paper were handled by Madame Bhikaji Cama.
mcqs.chapter: Development of Press in Modern India

mcqs.question: Who among the following great men is called the ‘Father of Indian Renaissance’?
mcqs.explanation: Raja Rammohan Roy has been called the ‘Father of Indian Renaissance’, the ‘Prophet of Indian Nationalism’, the ‘Bridge between the Past and the Future’, the ‘Father of Indian Nationalism’, the ‘Father of Modern India’, the ‘First Modern Man’, and the ‘Herald of a New Age’.

mcqs.question: The First Society founded by Raja Ram Mohan Roy was:
mcqs.explanation: In order to propagate the monotheistic doctrine of Hinduism, Raja Rammohan Roy, with the help of his young supporters, founded the ‘Atmiya Sabha’ in 1815. This was the first organization established by Raja Rammohan Roy.
mcqs.chapter: Development of Press in Modern India

mcqs.question: In 1809, Raja Ram Mohan Roy wrote his famous book "Gift to Monotheists" in which of the following languages?
mcqs.explanation: In 1809, Raja Rammohan Roy wrote his famous book ‘Gift to Monotheists’ (Tuhfat-ul-Muwahhidin) in Persian language.
mcqs.chapter: Development of Press in Modern India

mcqs.question: Who gave Ram Mohan Roy the title of ‘Raja’?
mcqs.explanation: The Mughal Emperor Akbar II conferred the title of ‘Raja’ on Rammohan Roy and sent him in 1830 as his envoy to the court of the then British monarch William IV. Roy had to negotiate in England for an increase in the pension granted to Mughal Emperor Akbar II. Raja Rammohan Roy died on 27 September 1833 at Bristol in England, where his memorial stands.
mcqs.chapter: Development of Press in Modern India

mcqs.question: The Bengali leader who opposed socio-religious reforms and supported orthodoxy was
mcqs.explanation: Raja Radhakanta Deb founded the ‘Dharma Sabha’ in Bengal in 1830 and opposed socio-religious reforms while supporting orthodoxy.
mcqs.chapter: Development of Press in Modern India

mcqs.question: The founder of ‘Bhartiya Brahmo Samaj’ was :
mcqs.source: U.P. U.D.A./L.D.A. (Spl) (Pre) 2010 U.P. U.D.A./L.D.A. (Spl) (Mains) 2010 U.P. P.C.S. (Spl) (Mains) 2008
mcqs.explanation: Keshab Chandra Sen was the founder of the Indian Brahmo Samaj. In 1865, Debendranath Tagore removed him from the position of Acharya. As a result, Keshab Chandra Sen separated from the original Brahmo Samaj, and the original branch under Debendranath Tagore came to be known as the ‘Adi Brahmo Samaj’. The group led by Keshab Chandra Sen called itself the ‘Indian Brahmo Samaj’ or ‘Brahmo Samaj of India’ (Navavidhan). In 1878, this group again split when Anand Mohan Bose and Shibnath Shastri founded the ‘Sadharan Brahmo Samaj’ in protest against the marriage of Keshab Chandra Sen’s 13-year-old daughter to the Maharaja of Cooch Behar.

mcqs.question: The Brahmo Samaj is based on the principle of :
mcqs.explanation: In 1828, Raja Rammohan Roy laid the foundation of the Brahmo Samaj. The objective of the Brahmo Samaj was the worship of one God, opposition to idol worship, and rejection of the doctrine of incarnation. The Brahmo Samaj emphasized the worship of a universal God.

mcqs.question: Which of the following were not protested by Raja Ram Mohan Roy?
mcqs.explanation: In the field of education, Raja Rammohan Roy was a supporter of English education. According to him, only a liberal Western education could remove us from the darkness of ignorance and enable Indians to participate in the administration of the country. He opposed child marriage, the practice of Sati, idol worship, etc.

mcqs.question: Which of the above following was started in opposition to the religious/social ideas of Ram Mohan Roy?
mcqs.explanation: In opposition to the religious and social ideas of Rammohan Roy, Bhawani Charan Bandyopadhyay started ‘Samachar Chandrika’ in 1822. Earlier, he had been the editor of ‘Sambad Kaumudi’.

mcqs.question: Vivekanand attended the ‘Parliament of the World’s Religions’ held at Chicago in
mcqs.explanation: The credit for giving concrete shape to the interpretation of the teachings of Ramakrishna Paramhansa goes to Swami Vivekananda (1863–1902 A.D.). He explained these teachings in simple language. Swami Vivekananda emerged as a preacher of Neo-Hinduism. In 1893, he went to Chicago, where he delivered his famous speech at the ‘Parliament of Religions’ (World Parliament of Religions). Through this speech, he presented the greatness of Indian culture before the Western world in a highly effective manner. In the latter half of the nineteenth century, Swami Vivekananda was one of the best representatives of Neo-Hinduism.

mcqs.question: Who among the following famous reformers wrote the books Jnyana Yoga, Karma Yoga, and Raja Yoga?
mcqs.explanation: Swami Vivekananda wrote the books Jnanayoga, Karmayoga and Rajayoga.

mcqs.question: Who was the founder of Ram Krishna Mission?
mcqs.explanation: The Ramakrishna Mission was founded by Swami Vivekananda in 1897 A.D. (It was formally registered in 1909 under the Societies Registration Act). The headquarters of the Ramakrishna Mission was established at Belur near Calcutta.

mcqs.question: “I have no time to think about God because a lot of work has to be done on this earth” whose statement is above ?
mcqs.explanation: When asked whether God exists or not, Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar replied, “I have no time to think about God, because there is still much work to be done on this earth.”

mcqs.question: The year Arya Samaj founded :
mcqs.explanation: Dayananda Saraswati (Moolshankar) founded the Arya Samaj in Bombay in April 1875 A.D. Its main objective was to re-establish the ancient Vedic religion in its pure form. Giving the slogan “Back to the Vedas,” he said that “the Vedas are the source of all knowledge.” He is credited with the revival of the Vedas in India. The Arya Samaj movement spread mainly as a reaction to Western influences. In 1877, the headquarters of the Arya Samaj was established at Lahore, after which the Arya Samaj gained wider publicity.

mcqs.question: Who among the following is known as ‘Martin Luther of India’?
mcqs.explanation: Swami Dayananda Saraswati is called the ‘Martin Luther of India’ because of his religious reform efforts.

mcqs.question: ‘Satyarth Prakash’ was written by –
mcqs.explanation: The ideas of Swami Dayananda are presented in his famous book ‘Satyarth Prakash’. His other major works include Pakhanda Khandan, Vedabhashya Bhumika, Rigveda Bhashya, Advaita Mat Khandan, Panch Mahayajna Vidhi and Vallabhacharya Mat Khandan.

mcqs.question: Which among the following organizations supported Shuddhi movement?
mcqs.explanation: The Arya Samaj, founded by Swami Dayananda Saraswati in Bombay in 1875 A.D., supported the Shuddhi Movement for bringing converted Hindus back into Hinduism.

mcqs.question: Given below are two statements, one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R). Assertion (A) : The Arya Samaj Movement gave self- confidence and self-reliance to the Hindus. Reason (R) : The Arya Samaj Movement undermined the belief in superiority of White Race. Choose the correct answer from the codes given below: Codes:

options.a: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct expla nation of (A)
options.b: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)

mcqs.explanation: The Arya Samaj was founded by Dayananda Saraswati (Moolshankar) in Bombay in April 1875. Its main objective was to re-establish the ancient Vedic religion in its pure form and to unite India religiously, socially and politically, while also generating self-confidence and self-reliance among Hindus. The Arya Samaj accepted the principle of Hindu cultural superiority and rejected the doctrine of white superiority. Thus, both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct, and Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

mcqs.question: Who was the founder of ‘Prarthana Samaj’?
mcqs.explanation: Prarthana Samaj was founded in 1867 in Bombay by Atmaram Pandurang under the inspiration of Acharya Keshab Chandra Sen. Mahadev Govind Ranade joined this institution in 1869 and became its principal leader. The main objectives of this institution were to oppose the caste system, raise the age of marriage for men and women, encourage widow remarriage, and promote women’s education. Ranade continued this social reform movement successfully until the end of the nineteenth century.

mcqs.question: Who was the founder of ‘Satyashodhak Samaj’ having its primary emphasis on the seeking of truth?
mcqs.explanation: The Satyashodhak Samaj was founded by Jyotiba Phule in 1873. He led a powerful non-Brahmin movement. Through his book ‘Gulamgiri’ and his organization ‘Satyashodhak Samaj’, he worked to secure justice for Dalits and the underprivileged sections of society.

mcqs.question: Jyotiba Phule was associated with
mcqs.explanation: Jyotiba Phule was associated with the anti-caste movement. Mahatma Jyotiba Phule was among the first persons in Maharashtra to begin work for the uplift of the untouchables and for women’s education. To secure justice for Dalits and the underprivileged sections, he founded the ‘Satyashodhak Samaj’.

mcqs.question: Who among the following was the founder of ‘Dev Samaj’?
mcqs.explanation: ‘Dev Samaj’ was founded in 1887 at Lahore by Shivnarayan Agnihotri. He had earlier been a follower of the Brahmo Samaj. The teachings of this society are compiled in a book titled ‘Devshastra’.

mcqs.question: Who was the founder of Radha Swami Satsang?
mcqs.explanation: The Radhaswami Satsang movement was founded in 1861 by Tulsiram, a merchant or banker from Agra, who was popularly known as Shivdayal Sahib or Swamiji Maharaj. Followers of the Radhaswami faith believe in one God, the importance of the Guru, the company of saints (satsang), and a simple social way of life.

mcqs.question: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
mcqs.explanation: The correct matching is as follows– Bharat Dharma Mahamandal – Haridwar Dev Samaj – Lahore Radhaswami Satsang – Agra Sanatan Dharma Rakshini Sabha – Calcutta

mcqs.question: Who was known by the nickname “Lokahitvadi”?
mcqs.explanation: Gopal Hari Deshmukh (1823–92 A.D.), the noted social reformer of Maharashtra, was popularly known as ‘Lokhitwadi’.

mcqs.question: The campaign for widow remarriage in Maharashtra was led by :
mcqs.explanation: The first campaign for widow remarriage in Maharashtra was led by Vishnu Parshuram Pandit (Vishnu Shastri). In 1850, he founded the ‘Widow Remarriage Association’. B.M. Malabari is famous for his efforts to bring about the legal abolition of child marriage and for advocating women’s rights.

mcqs.question: Which of the following Act was passed in 1856? (i) Religious Disabilities Act (ii) Sati Prohibition Act (iii) Hindu Widow Remarriage Act (iv) Policy of Annexation Choose the correct option from the codes given below:
mcqs.explanation: No law by the name of the Religious Disabilities Act was passed in British India. The Caste Disabilities Act was passed in 1850. The Hindu Widow Remarriage Act, 1856 legalized the remarriage of widows. The Sati Prohibition Regulation was enacted in 1829 during the time of Lord William Bentinck, whereas the Doctrine of Lapse was introduced by Dalhousie in 1848.

mcqs.question: The name of D.K. Karve of Western India figures in the context of which of the following?
mcqs.explanation: D.K. Karve was a famous social reformer. He made significant contributions in the fields of widow remarriage and women’s education. Along with Ranade, he worked for the widow remarriage movement and established the ‘Widow Ashram Association’ to provide education to widows. The objective of this ashram was to make widows self-reliant by training them as teachers, nurses, or midwives. D.K. Karve was the secretary of the Widow Remarriage Association. He also established the first women’s university in Bombay in 1916.

mcqs.question: Who among the following prominently fought for and got widow remarriage legalized ?
mcqs.explanation: Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar, the Principal of Sanskrit College, Calcutta, struggled tirelessly for widow remarriage. He tried to prove that widow remarriage was recognized in the Vedas. As a result of his efforts, the Hindu Widow Remarriage Act was passed on 26 July 1856.

mcqs.question: What did the Act V of 1843 make illegal?
mcqs.explanation: During the tenure of Lord Ellenborough, Act V of 1843 declared slavery illegal. A clause had already been added to the Charter Act of 1833 stating that slavery should be abolished as early as possible. Finally, in 1843, slavery was declared illegal throughout India, and all slaves were freed without any compensation being given to their owners.

mcqs.question: Who among the following had played an important role in passing the Native Marriage Act of 1872?
mcqs.explanation: Keshab Chandra Sen played an important role in getting the Native (Civil) Marriage Act passed in 1872. Under this Act, the minimum age for marriage was fixed at 14 years for girls and 18 years for boys. It was also called the Brahmo Marriage Act.

mcqs.question: The Act was supported by the extremist wing led by Bal Gangadhar Tilak. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Behramji M. Malabari was one of the greatest Parsi social reformers of the 19th century. Although he was born in Baroda (Gujarat), Bombay later became his main field of work. He tried to create public awareness for improving the condition of women, opposing child marriage, and supporting widow remarriage. The Age of Consent Act, 1891 was passed due to his efforts. Bal Gangadhar Tilak opposed this Act.

mcqs.question: Consider the following passage: “Born in 1853 he was a Parsi from Western India. He was the editor of “Indian Spectator” and “Voice of India.” He was a social reformer and was the chief crusader for the Age of Consent Act 1891. Who is being described in the above paragraph?
mcqs.explanation: Behramji Malabari was a Parsi and a social reformer. He edited 'Indian Spectator' and 'Voice of India'. As a result of his efforts, the Age of Consent Act, 1891 was passed. By this Act, the age of consent for girls was raised to 12 years. Bal Gangadhar Tilak opposed this Act.

mcqs.question: What was the minimum marriageable age fixed under Sharda Act for boys and girls?
mcqs.explanation: In 1929, due to the efforts of Judge Har Bilas Sarda, a law prohibiting child marriage was enacted. It came to be known as the Sharda Act after his name. Under this Act, the minimum age for marriage was fixed at 14 years for girls and 18 years for boys.

mcqs.question: The success of the Theosophical Society in India was mainly due to –
mcqs.explanation: In 1879, Colonel Olcott and Madam Blavatsky came to India and established the headquarters of the Theosophical Society near Adyar in Madras. In 1889, Mrs. Annie Besant became a member of this Society, and after coming to India in 1893, she played the most active role in it. Mrs. Annie Besant regarded ancient Hinduism as one of the most profound and spiritual religions of the world. Theosophy supported the spiritual philosophy of Hinduism, the doctrine of karma, and the doctrine of rebirth. For this reason, Annie Besant was able to win Indian support for it, which was the main reason for its success.

mcqs.question: Which one of the following pairs is not correctly matched?

options.a: Raja Ram Mohan Roy - Brahmo Samaj

mcqs.explanation: Raja Rammohan Roy founded the Brahmo Samaj, Swami Dayanand Saraswati founded the Arya Samaj, and Swami Vivekananda founded the Ramakrishna Mission. Mahadev Govind Ranade was not associated with the Theosophical Society; rather, he was associated with the Prarthana Samaj (founded by Atmaram Pandurang). Annie Besant was associated with the Theosophical Society.

mcqs.question: Which one of the following is not correctly matched?

options.c: Brahmo Samaj of India - Keshav Chandra Sen

mcqs.explanation: The Atmiya Sabha was founded in 1815 by Raja Rammohan Roy. The Prarthana Samaj was founded in 1867 by Dr. Atmaram Pandurang. Two years later, R.G. Bhandarkar and Mahadev Govind Ranade also joined it. In 1866, the Brahmo Samaj split. Under the leadership of Debendranath Tagore, the Adi Brahmo Samaj was formed, and under the leadership of Keshab Chandra Sen, the Indian Brahmo Samaj was established. Tulsi Ram (Shiv Dayal Sahib) was associated with the Radhaswami Satsang.

mcqs.question: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer by using the codes given below the lists: List-I List-II A. Brahmo Samaj 1. Mumbai B. Manav Dharma Sabha 2. Surat C. Arya Samaj 3. Kolkata D. Nadwah-ul-Ulama 4. Lucknow Code : A B C D
mcqs.explanation: The correct matching is as follows— Brahmo Samaj – Calcutta Manav Dharma Sabha – Surat Arya Samaj – Bombay Nadwa-ul-Ulama – Lucknow

mcqs.question: Which one of the following social reformers strongly opposed Jury Act of 1826’?
mcqs.explanation: The Jury Act was passed in 1826. Under it, discrimination in courts on a religious basis began. According to its provisions, cases relating to Hindus and Muslims could be heard by European or Indian Christian judges, but no Hindu or Muslim judge could hear the case of any Christian, whether European or Indian. Raja Rammohan Roy strongly opposed this discrimination.

mcqs.question: Which one of the following is correctly matched?

options.a: Brahmo Samaj of India - Raja Ram Mohan Roy
options.d: The Servants of India - Gopal Krishna Gokhale Society

mcqs.source: U.P.P.C.S. (Spl) (Mains) 2004; U.P. Lower Sub. (Pre) 2015 U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 1990, 1993; U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2016
mcqs.explanation: Gopal Krishna Gokhale, a disciple of Ranade, founded the Servants of India Society in 1905. Debendranath Tagore founded the Tattvabodhini Sabha in 1839. In 1866, Keshab Chandra Sen separated from the original Brahmo Samaj and organized a new branch, which he called the Indian Brahmo Samaj. The founder of the Satyashodhak Samaj was Jyotiba Phule, who wrote the book Gulamgiri.

mcqs.question: Who was the founder of Bahujan Samaj?
mcqs.explanation: After 1910, inspired by the ideas of Jyotiba Phule, Mukundrao Patil and Shankarrao Jadhav founded the anti- Brahmin and strongly anti-Congress Bahujan Samaj. Shahu Maharaj of Kolhapur supported this movement because of disputes with Brahmin courtiers.

mcqs.question: Who said that “If God is put up with untouchability, I will not call him God.”
mcqs.explanation: At a conference held for the abolition of untouchability, Tilak said, “If God tolerates untouchability, I will not call him God.”

mcqs.question: Said that Brahmovad should be made the religion of the world. B. Keshav Chandra Sen 2. Identified Hinduism with religion instituted in Vedas. C Dayanand Saraswati 3. Emphasized that there are several ways to reach God. D. Ramakrishna 4. Purest form of Hinduism Paramhansa is contained in Upanishads Code : A B C D
mcqs.explanation: Raja Rammohan Roy, the founder of the Brahmo Samaj, reinterpreted the principles of Hinduism and found sufficient support for his reforms in the Upanishads. Swami Dayanand Saraswati believed in the pure Vedic tradition and gave the slogan, “Back to the Vedas.” Keshab Chandra Sen called for Brahmoism to be made a universal religion. Ramakrishna Paramhansa emphasized that there may be many paths to reach God.

mcqs.question: Which one of the following is not correctly matched:

options.c: Raja Ram Mohan Roy – Adi Brahmo Samaj

mcqs.explanation: Raja Rammohan Roy founded the Brahmo Samaj in 1828. Later, under Debendranath Tagore, it came to be known as the Adi Brahmo Samaj. Owing to ideological differences between Keshab Chandra Sen and Debendranath Tagore, Keshab Chandra Sen founded a new organization in 1866 under the name Indian Brahmo Samaj. After that, Debendranath Tagore’s Brahmo Samaj came to be known as the Adi Brahmo Samaj. The other three pairs are correctly matched.

Establishment of Girls School in Calcutta B. J. E. D. Bethune 2. Secretary, Widow Re- marriage Association C. Ishwar Chandra 3. Starting a crusade Vidyasagar against child marriage D. B. M. Malabari 4. Principal of Sanskrit College in Calcutta Code : A B C D
mcqs.explanation: The correct matching is as follows– Person Related work/post D.K. Karve – Widow Remarriage Association J.E.D. Bethune – Establishment of a girls’ school in Calcutta Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar – Principal of Sanskrit College, Calcutta B.M. Malabari – Beginning the campaign against child marriage

mcqs.question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? Organisation Person

options.a: Young Bengal Movement - Henry Vivian Derozeo
options.d: United Indian Patriotic - Syed Ahmad Khan Association

mcqs.explanation: The Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha was founded by Babasaheb Bhimrao Ambedkar. The remaining options are correctly matched.

mcqs.question: Who among the following social reformers was known for proficiency in the Sanskrit language?
mcqs.explanation: Dayanand Saraswati, Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar, and Raja Rammohan Roy made tireless efforts for religious and social reform in India during British rule. All three were proficient in Sanskrit and criticized the evils prevalent in Hindu religion and society.

mcqs.question: ‘Dar-ul-Ulum was established by –
mcqs.explanation: In 1893, Nadwat-ul-Ulama was formed at Kanpur under the presidency of Maulana Lutfullah Sahib of Aligarh, and Maulana Shibli Nomani was among its founders. In 1898, ‘Dar-ul-Uloom’ (Dar-ul-Uloom Nadwat-ul-Ulama) was established at Lucknow by Nadwat-ul-Ulama on the advice of Maulana Shibli Nomani. He was also a leading teacher of this Dar-ul-Uloom.

mcqs.question: The Deoband Movement in U.P. (United Province) started in the year
mcqs.explanation: The Deoband Movement began in 1866 with the establishment of Dar-ul-Uloom at Deoband,

mcqs.question: The Tarkeshwar Movement of 1924 in Bengal was against:
mcqs.explanation: In 1924, the Tarakeshwar Movement was launched in Bengal against the corrupt mahant of the Tarakeshwar Shiva temple. The mahant was accused of having an illicit relationship with a woman and of misusing temple funds.

mcqs.question: ‘Hali System’ concerned :
mcqs.explanation: The ‘Hali system’ was related to bonded labour and bonded labourers. Under this system, in the Bardoli region, people of the Kaliparaj tribe had to work as hereditary labourers in the houses of upper castes.

mcqs.question: Given below are two statements, in which one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R): Assertion (A): The Bengal British Indian Society was founded in 1843 as a result of George Thompson's efforts. Reason (R) : George Thompson was brought out from England by Dwarkanath Tagore to organise the political movement. Select the correct answer using the code given below: Code -

options.a: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not correct explanation of (A).
options.c: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is correct explanation of (A).

mcqs.explanation: The Bengal British Indian Society was established in 1843 in Calcutta. Its establishment was the result of the efforts of George Thompson. He was its president. Dwarkanath Tagore had brought George Thompson from England to India to organize liberal politics in Bengal. Therefore, both the statement and the reason are correct, and the reason is the correct explanation of the statement.

mcqs.question: Who amongst the following was the founder of ‘Indian Association’
mcqs.explanation: On 26 July 1876, Surendranath Banerjee, with the cooperation of Anand Mohan Bose, founded the ‘Indian Association’ or ‘Bharat Sangh’ in Calcutta. It was one of the most prominent and important political organizations of that time and enjoyed the status of an all-India organization even before the Congress. This association carried on movements on issues such as the demand for reform in the Civil Services examination system and the Ilbert Bill controversy. In the Indian Association, the middle class was given prominence over the zamindars.

mcqs.question: Name the organization formed by Surendranath Banerjee which merged with the Indian National Congress in 1886:
mcqs.explanation: In December 1883, the Indian Association organized the Indian National Conference. At the time of the establishment of the Indian National Congress, the second session of the Indian Association, under the presidency of Surendranath Banerjee, was held in Calcutta as the Indian National Conference. It appears that both movements were simultaneous and independent, and that before their sessions neither of the two sets of organizers had any knowledge of the other; this came to be known only just before the sessions. Both organizations were conceived on the same lines and adopted the same type of programme. It was clearly undesirable that two such organizations should work independently in two different parts of India. Therefore, after 1886, the Indian National Conference was no longer held. The Indian Association was never merged into the Congress. Since the Indian National Conference was not held after 1886, option (d) may be treated as the correct answer.

mcqs.question: Who amongst the following was one of the founders of the Bombay Presidency Association in 1885?
mcqs.explanation: In 1885, the Bombay Presidency Association was founded through the efforts of Pherozeshah Mehta, Badruddin Tyabji and K.T. Telang. Its objective was to propagate political ideas among the people.

mcqs.question: Consider the following events and arrange them in chronological order : 1. East India Association 2. National Indian Association 3. Indian Society 4. Indian Association Select the correct answer from the codes given below:
mcqs.explanation: Organizations (Year Founder of Establishment) East India Association (1866) – Dadabhai Naoroji National Indian Association (1870) – Mary Carpenter Indian Society (1872) – Anand Mohan Bose Indian Association (1876) – Surendranath Banerjee and Anand Mohan Bose Therefore, the correct chronological order of the organizations mentioned in the question is given in option (d). In some sources, the year of establishment of the National Indian Association is also mentioned as 1871.

mcqs.question: Which of the following pairs do not match? Find your answer with the help of given code: 1. British India Society - London 2. East India Association - Calcutta 3. National Indian Association - London 4. Indian Association - Bombay Code :
mcqs.explanation: The correct matching is as follows– British India Society (1839) – London East India Association (1866) – London National Indian Association (1870–71) – London Indian Association (1876) – Calcutta

mcqs.question: Which of the following was not one of the political associations to be set up during the pre-congress phase?
mcqs.explanation: In September 1870, the Bristol Indian Association was established. In October 1870, its name was changed to ‘The Indian Association’. This association, established in London by Mary Carpenter, Keshab Chandra Sen and others, worked for the cause of women’s education. Therefore, it was not a political organization. In 1871, its name was again changed to the National Indian Association.

mcqs.question: Given below are two statements, one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R): Assertion (A): Dadabhai Naoroji organised the East India Association in 1866 in London to discuss on Indian questions. Reason (R) : He wanted to influence the British Public Opinion. Choose the correct answer from the code given below:

options.c: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct expla- nation of (A).
options.d: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

mcqs.explanation: Dadabhai Naoroji is also known as the “Grand Old Man of India.” In 1866, he founded the East India Association in London. The purpose behind the establishment of this organization was to discuss Indian issues and to make the British public aware of matters concerning India. Dadabhai Naoroji also wrote a book titled 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India'.

mcqs.question: Consider the following organizations: 1. Bangabhasha Prakasika Sabha 2. Landholders Society 3. Bengal British India Society 4. Indian League Select the correct chronological order of founding of these organizations from the code given below:
mcqs.explanation: Institution Year of Establishment Bangabhasha Prakashika Sabha – 1836 Landholders’ Society – 1838 Bengal British India Society – 1843 Indian League – 1875

British India Society 2. Anand Mohan Bose C. Indian Society 3. William Adams D. Indian Association 4. Dwarkanath Tagore Code : A B C D
mcqs.explanation: The correct matching is as follows– Landholders’ Society – Dwarkanath Tagore British India Society – William Adams Indian Society – Anand Mohan Bose Indian Association – S.N. Banerjee

mcqs.question: Match the List-I with List-II: A. India League 1. Shishir Kumar Ghosh B. Indian Association 2. Anand Mohan Bose C. India National Liberal 3. Syed Ahmad Khan Federation D. United Indian Patriotic 4. Surendranath Association Bannerjee Code : A B C D
mcqs.explanation: The correct matching is as follows– India League – Shishir Kumar Ghosh Indian Association – Anand Mohan Bose and Surendranath Banerjee Indian National Liberal Federation – Surendranath Banerjee United India Patriotic Association – Syed Ahmad Khan

mcqs.question: Match the List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using codes given below : List-I List-II (a) Indian Association 1. Anand Charlu (b) Poona Sarvjanik Sabha 2. Surendra Nath Benerji (c) Bombay Presidency 3. Mahadev Govind Association Ranade (d) Madras Mahajan Sabha 4. Pherozshah Mehta Codes : A B C D
mcqs.explanation: The institutions mentioned in the question and their founders are as follows– Indian Association – Surendranath Banerjee Poona Sarvajanik Sabha – Mahadev Govind Ranade Bombay Presidency Association – Pherozeshah Mehta Madras Mahajan Sabha – Anand Charlu

mcqs.question: Who among the following was the founder of the 'United Indian Patriotic Association' with Syed Ahmad Khan?
mcqs.explanation: As a political organisation, the ‘United Indian Patriotic Association’ was founded in 1888 by Sir Syed Ahmad Khan and Raja Shiv Prasad Singh of Banaras. It is noteworthy that this organisation was established with the objective of opposing the Indian National Congress and promoting close relations between the Muslim community and the British.

mcqs.question: Which one of the following pairs is not correctly matched?

options.c: Royal Asiatic Society of - 1813 A.D. Great Britain
options.d: Land Holders Society of - 1844 A.D. Bengal

mcqs.explanation: In the given question, both options (c) and (d) are incorrectly matched. It is noteworthy that the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain was established in 1823 A.D., and the Landholders’ Society of Bengal was established in 1838 A.D. The other two pairs are correctly matched.

mcqs.question: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer from the code given below the Lists: List-I (Founders) A. British Indian Association B. Bombay Presidency Association C. Central Mohammadan National Association D. Servants of India Society List-II (Founders) 1. Gopal Krishna Gokhale 2. K.T. Telang 3. Radha Kant Dev 4. Sayyid Amir Ali Code : A B C D
mcqs.explanation: The British Indian Association was established in October 1851 in Calcutta. Its founder-members included Rajendralal Mitra, Radhakant Deb (President), Harish Chandra Mukherjee and Debendranath Tagore (General Secretary). The Bombay Presidency Association was established in 1885 in Bombay. Its founder-members included Pherozeshah Mehta, Badruddin Tyabji and K.T. Telang. Syed Amir Ali founded the Central National Muhammadan Association. Gopal Krishna Gokhale founded the Servants of India Society in 1905.

mcqs.question: When was Indian National Congress set up?
mcqs.explanation: The Indian National Congress was founded in 1885 by A.O. Hume, a retired British officer. Its first session was held from 28 to 30 December 1885 at Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit School in Bombay. A total of 72 delegates attended the session. The first session of the Indian National Congress was presided over by Womesh Chandra Bonnerjee (W.C. Bonnerjee), and its first General Secretary was A.O. Hume himself.

mcqs.question: Where was the first session of the Indian National Congress held?
mcqs.explanation: The Indian National Congress was founded in 1885 by A.O. Hume, a retired British officer. Its first session was held from 28 to 30 December 1885 at Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit School in Bombay. A total of 72 delegates attended the session. The first session of the Indian National Congress was presided over by Womesh Chandra Bonnerjee (W.C. Bonnerjee), and its first General Secretary was A.O. Hume himself.

mcqs.question: The Indian National Congress was established during the viceroyalty of:
mcqs.explanation: At the time of the establishment of the Indian National Congress (1885), the Viceroy (and Governor-General) of India was Lord Dufferin (tenure: 1884–1888 A.D.). He mocked the Congress by saying that it was an organisation representing the ‘microscopic minority’.

mcqs.question: Who was the Governor General and Viceroy of India at the time of the formation of the Indian National Congress?
mcqs.explanation: At the time of the establishment of the Indian National Congress (1885), the Viceroy (and Governor-General) of India was Lord Dufferin (tenure: 1884–1888 A.D.). He mocked the Congress by saying that it was an organisation representing the ‘microscopic minority’.

mcqs.question: Who among the following was not present at the founding session of the Indian National Congress:
mcqs.explanation: In 1876, the young nationalists of Bengal formed the Indian Association under the leadership of Surendranath Banerjee and Anand Mohan Bose. In December 1883, the Indian Association organized the Indian National Conference. The second conference was held at Calcutta in December 1885, and it was presided over by Surendranath Banerjee. For this reason, Surendranath Banerjee, being associated with the Indian National Conference, did not attend the founding session of the Indian National Congress in 1885.

mcqs.question: Given below are two statements, one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R). Assertion (A): Most of the early nationalists considered British rule as an act of providence destined to bring modernisation. Reason (R): They complained only against "Un-British rule" in India. Select the correct answer from the codes given below:

options.a: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
options.c: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

mcqs.explanation: A large section of the early nationalist leaders viewed British rule as something ordained by Providence and considered it necessary for bringing modernity to India. They believed that British rule was paving the way for the development of Indian society by introducing industrialization, education, and administrative reforms in India. The grievance of these early nationalists was only against the “Un-British rule” in India. Therefore, both the Assertion and the Reason are true, and Reason (R) is also the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

mcqs.question: First Muslim President of Indian National Congress was:
mcqs.explanation: Badruddin Tyabji was the first Muslim President of the Indian National Congress. He was elected President of the third session of the Indian National Congress, held at Madras from 27 to 30 December 1887.

mcqs.question: Consider the following statements : I. The first Muslim President of Indian National Congress was Badruddin Tyabji. II. The first woman President of Indian National Congress was Sarojini Naidu. Which of the statements above is/are correct ?
mcqs.explanation: Badruddin Tyabji (Madras Session, 1887) was the first Muslim President of the Congress. Sarojini Naidu (Kanpur Session, 1925) was not the first woman President of the Congress; rather, she was the first Indian woman President. The first woman President was Annie Besant, who presided over the Calcutta Session of 1917.

mcqs.question: The first European to be elected as President of the Indian National Congress was
mcqs.explanation: George Yule was the first elected European President of the Indian National Congress. He presided over the fourth session of the Indian National Congress, held at Allahabad in 1888.

mcqs.question: Who among the following was never elected as a President of the ‘Indian National Congress.’
mcqs.explanation: Lala Lajpat Rai became President of the Indian National Congress at the Special Session of Calcutta in 1920. Annie Besant became the first woman President of the Indian National Congress in 1917. Motilal Nehru served as President of the Congress in 1919 and again in 1928. Bal Gangadhar Tilak was never elected President of the Congress.

mcqs.question: In which of the following Sessions of the Indian National Congress Bal Gangadhar Tilak had expressed,”Swaraj is my birthright, I shall have it.”
mcqs.explanation: At the Lucknow Session of the Indian National Congress in 1916, Bal Gangadhar Tilak said, “Swaraj is my birthright, and I shall have it.” In this session, the extremists rejoined the Congress, and through the efforts of Tilak and Annie Besant, an agreement was reached between the Congress and the Muslim League. This agreement is also famous as the Lucknow Pact or the Congress-League Pact.

mcqs.question: The last session of Indian National Congress attended by Bal Gangadhar Tilak was :
mcqs.explanation: Bal Gangadhar Tilak last attended the Indian National Congress at the Amritsar Session in 1919. He opposed Mahatma Gandhi’s policy of boycotting the legislative elections to be held under the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms. Tilak advised the adoption of the policy of “Responsive Cooperation.” Tilak died on 1 August, 1920.

mcqs.question: “The Congress is faltering to its fall and one of my great ambitions while in India is to assist it to a peaceful demise.” This declaration was made by :
mcqs.explanation: The British rulers believed that under the leadership of the Moderates, the Congress had become quite weak and had little hold over the masses; therefore, it could be crushed. The strongest advocate of this policy was Lord Curzon. In 1900, Curzon said: “Congress is tottering and will soon fall. My greatest aim is that this party should come to an end during my stay in India.” In 1903, he wrote to the Governor of Madras: “Ever since I came to India, my policy has been to make Congress impotent by every possible means.”

mcqs.question: Who of the following were elected to collaborate with Mahatma Gandhi who was to author the new Constitution of the Congress as the per resolution of Indian National Congress at Amritsar Session, 1919? 1. B.G. Tilak 2. N.C. Kelkar 3. C.R. Das 4. I.B. Sen Select the correct answer from the code given below: Code :
mcqs.explanation: Mahatma Gandhi wanted the assistance of B.G. Tilak and C.R. Das in drafting the Congress constitution, but due to their other engagements, these two leaders could not make themselves available for this work. As substitutes for these top leaders, their junior associates N.C. Kelkar and I.B. Sen were chosen to assist Mahatma Gandhi in drafting the Congress constitution.

mcqs.question: One Governor-General took part in one of the Congress Sessions. Identify the Governor-General and place where the Session was held :
mcqs.explanation: Lord Willingdon attended the Bombay Session of the Congress in 1915. At that time, he was the Governor of Bombay. It is noteworthy that Willingdon was not the Governor-General then. His tenure as Governor-General and Viceroy of India was from 1931 to 1936.

mcqs.question: Which of the following sessions of the Indian National Congress was presided over by C. Vijay Raghav Chariar?
mcqs.explanation: C. Vijayaraghavachariar presided over the Nagpur Session (1920) of the Indian National Congress. The Lucknow Session (1916) was presided over by Ambika Charan Mazumdar, while the Gaya Session (1922) was presided over by Chittaranjan Das.

mcqs.question: In which one of the following sessions, Congress declared its policy towards the Indian States for the first time?
mcqs.explanation: At the Nagpur Session of 1920, the Indian National Congress declared its policy towards the Indian States and demanded from their rulers that the people should be given a fully responsible government.

mcqs.question: Given below is a list of persons who became Presidents of Indian National Congress. Arrange then in chronological order. Select your answer using the code given below the list. 1. Mahatma Gandhi 2. Jawaharlal Nehru 3. Vallabh Bhai Patel 4. Smt. Sarojini Naidu Code :
mcqs.explanation: Mahatma Gandhi presided over the Belgaum Session of the Congress in 1924. Sarojini Naidu became the first Indian woman President at the annual Congress session held at Kanpur in 1925. Jawaharlal Nehru presided over the Lahore Session in 1929, the Lucknow Session in April 1936, and the Faizpur Session in December 1936, whereas Patel presided over the Karachi Session in 1931.

mcqs.question: Match List-I with the List-II and select the correct answer from the code given below: List - I List - II (Places, where Meetings (President) of Indian National Congress was held) A. Abul Kalam Azad 1. Amritsar, 1919 B. Sarojini Naidu 2. Bombay, 1934 C. Motilal Nehru 3. Kanpur. 1925 D. Dr. Rajendra Prasad 4. Ramgarh, 1940 Code : A B C D
mcqs.explanation: The correct matching is as follows– (President) (Places, where Meetings (President) of Indian National Congress was held) Motilal Nehru – Amritsar, 1919 Sarojini Naidu – Kanpur, 1925 Dr. Rajendra Prasad – Bombay, 1934 Abul Kalam Azad – Ramgarh, 1940

mcqs.question: In which of the following sessions of Indian National Congress, Jawaharlal Nehru spoke of socialism as the key to the solution of India’s problems?
mcqs.explanation: At the Lucknow Session of the Congress in 1936, Jawaharlal Nehru described socialism as the key to solving India’s problems. He said that, apart from socialism, he could see no other path that could free the people of India from poverty, unemployment, and slavery.

mcqs.question: The Haripura Session of Indian National Congress, 1938 was presided over by:
mcqs.explanation: The fifty-first session of the Congress was held at Haripura, Gujarat, from 19 to 21 February 1938. This session was presided over by Subhas Chandra Bose. At this session, the National Planning Committee was constituted, and Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru was appointed its Chairman.

mcqs.question: Match List-I with List -II and select the correct answer from the code given below the lists– A. Dr. M.A. Ansari 1. Haripura B. Purushottam Das Tandon 2. Kanpur C. Sarojini Naidu 3. Madras D. Subhash Chandra Bose 4. Nasik Code : A B C D
mcqs.explanation: The Haripura Session of the Congress (1938) was presided over by Subhas Chandra Bose, the Nasik Session (1950) by Purushottam Das Tandon, the Madras Session (1927) by Dr. M. A. Ansari, and the Kanpur Session (1925) by Sarojini Naidu.

mcqs.question: Who among the following was the President of Indian National Congress continuously for six years?
mcqs.explanation: Abul Kalam Azad remained President of the Indian National Congress continuously for six years, from 1940 to 1946. Before independence, this was the longest tenure.

mcqs.question: Who among the following suggested the winding up of the Indian National Congress after India attained independence?
mcqs.explanation: After India’s independence, Mahatma Gandhi suggested that the Indian National Congress should be dissolved.

mcqs.question: On which occasion was ‘Jana-Gana Mana,’ first sung?
mcqs.explanation: ‘Jana-Gana-Mana’, originally composed and set to music in Bengali by Rabindranath Tagore, was adopted by the Constituent Assembly as the National Anthem of India on 24 January 1950. It was first sung in December 1911 at the Calcutta Session of the Indian National Congress.

mcqs.question: Who of the following continuously from 1904 onwards emphasized on the grant of ‘self-rule’ to India?
mcqs.explanation: Dadabhai Naoroji first raised the demand for self-government or Swaraj for India in 1904 at the International Socialist Congress. In his message to the Benares Session of the Congress in 1905, he also spoke of self-government. In his presidential address at the Congress Session of 1906, he again demanded Swaraj.

mcqs.question: Who among the following was not an outstanding leader of extreme Nationalism?
mcqs.explanation: Gopal Krishna Gokhale belonged to the Moderate camp. He believed in balance, restraint, and a gentle and just approach. He had firm faith that the regeneration of the country could not be achieved through storms of excitement. He believed in the purity of both means and ends.

mcqs.question: Who accused Indian National Congress of practising ‘politics of prayer, petition and protest’:
mcqs.source: U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2005; U.P. U.D.A./L.D.A. (Pre) 2002 U.P. Lower Sub. (Spl) (Pre) 2002; U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2002
mcqs.explanation: After 1906, the Extremist group emerged within the Congress. The four major leaders of this extremist ideology were Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Lala Lajpat Rai, Bipin Chandra Pal, and Aurobindo Ghosh. These leaders made the attainment of Swaraj their main objective. Unlike the Moderate leaders, they did not believe in securing their demands within the constitutional framework. Tilak said: “Our objective is self-reliance, not mendicancy.” He accused the Congress of following the politics of prayer, petition and protest.

mcqs.question: Who called the Indian National Congress as a “Begging Institute” ?
mcqs.explanation: Leaders of the extremist school made adverse remarks about the Congress. One of them, Bipin Chandra Pal, described the Indian National Congress as a “begging institution.”

mcqs.question: Who among the following was not associated with the Moderates in Indian National Congress?
mcqs.explanation: Lala Lajpat Rai was also known as the “Lion of Punjab.” He was a leader of the Extremist group in the Indian National Congress and was the representative of Punjab. He was also called “Punjab Kesari.”

mcqs.question: Who of the following was not a moderate:
mcqs.explanation: The early liberal or moderate policies of the Congress disillusioned the new nationalists, popularly known as Lal-Bal-Pal. Bal Gangadhar Tilak was the pioneer of this new ideology. He was not a Moderate, but a supporter of extremist policies.

mcqs.question: Who among of the following was considered by Lala Lajpat Rai as his political guru?
mcqs.explanation: After reading the life of the Italian revolutionary Mazzini, Lala Lajpat Rai came to regard him as his political guru. Later, he also translated Mazzini’s famous work “The Duties of Man” into Urdu.

mcqs.question: Who among the following leaders was a supporter of ‘Swadeshi’?
mcqs.explanation: Aurobindo Ghosh was one of the major leaders of the Swadeshi Movement launched in protest against the partition of Bengal. Other major leaders of this movement were Lala Lajpat Rai (Punjab), Bal Gangadhar Tilak (Maharashtra), and Bipin Chandra Pal (Bengal).

mcqs.question: Who among the following is known as the father of ‘Indian Unrest’–
mcqs.explanation: Tilak believed in service and sacrifice, and he had the courage to challenge the authority of the government. It was due to his efforts that the Congress changed from an organization that praised the government into one that criticized it. The Anglo-Indian bureaucracy regarded him as a rebel. Sir Valentine Chirol called him the ‘Father of Indian Unrest’. Tilak went to England with the intention of filing a defamation suit against Chirol. Although he lost the case, it produced a proper impact.

mcqs.question: After the sentence of B.G. Tilak, who among the fol- lowing had pleaded for mercy and said: “My interest in Tilak is that of a Sanskrit scholar”?
mcqs.explanation: After Bal Gangadhar Tilak was sentenced, the famous scholar Max Muller pleaded for clemency and said, “My interest in Tilak is that of a Sanskrit Scholar.”

mcqs.question: Assertion (A) : Bal Gangadhar Tilak was a communalist. Reason (R) : He used the religion as a political weapon. Select your answer by using the codes given below :
