options.a: A and R both are correct, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.b: A and R both are correct, but the R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.c: A is correct, but R is wrong.
options.d: A is wrong, but R is correct.

mcqs.explanation: In the given statement and reason, (A) is false, but (R) is true. Tilak was not a communal person. He was the first nationalist leader who tried to establish close contact with the masses, and in this respect he was a forerunner of Mahatma Gandhi. For this purpose, he established akharas, lathi clubs, and cow-protection associations. He started the Shivaji Festival and the Ganapati Festival in Maharashtra so that the spirit of national service might arise among the people. Thus, he did use religion as a political instrument, but its purpose was not communalism; rather, it was to awaken the masses.

mcqs.question: When did Bal Gangadhar Tilak get the title Lokmanya?
mcqs.explanation: In June 1897, the Chapekar brothers killed Rand, the Chairman of the Plague Committee of Poona, and Lieutenant Ayerst. In connection with Rand’s murder, it was alleged that the Brahmins of Poona, under the leadership of Tilak, had conspired in this act. In July 1897, Tilak was arrested under Section 124-A of the Indian Penal Code on the charge of sedition, and after trial he was sentenced to 18 months’ imprisonment. This was strongly opposed throughout the country. As a result, Tilak became popular as an all-India leader, and the people conferred on him the title of ‘Lokmanya’.

mcqs.question: Along with Mahatma Gandhi who amongst the follow- ing Muslims did lift the bier of Bal Gangadhar Tilak?
mcqs.explanation: After the death of Bal Gangadhar Tilak on 1 August 1920, his bier was carried by Maulana Shaukat Ali and Dr. Saifuddin Kitchlew along with Mahatma Gandhi. Maulana Hasrat Mohani recited a mourning poem at that time.

mcqs.question: ‘Abhinava Bharat’ a secret society of revolutionaries was organised by :
mcqs.explanation: Vinayak Damodar Savarkar and his brother Ganesh Damodar Savarkar started an organization named ‘Mitra Mela’, which was renamed by V.D. Savarkar in 1904 at Nasik and established as a secret revolutionary organization under the name ‘Abhinav Bharat’ (Young India Society).

mcqs.question: The revolutionary organisation “Abhinav Bharat’ was set up in 1905 in –
mcqs.explanation: The revolutionary organization ‘Abhinav Bharat’ was established by V.D. Savarkar in Maharashtra (Nasik). However, it was established in 1904 and not in 1905.

mcqs.question: Yugantar Party was led by –
mcqs.explanation: Jatindranath Mukherjee (1879-1915) was a Bengali revolutionary. He was a devoted follower of Vivekananda and Aurobindo Ghose and an active member of revolutionary organizations such as Yugantar, Anushilan Samiti, and the Ghadar Party. He was popularly known as ‘Bagha Jatin’.

mcqs.question: Who had founded the ‘Anushilan Samiti’?
mcqs.explanation: Anushilan Samiti Midanapur Calcutta Dhaka (Oct., (1902) 1906 March, 1902 by Gyanendra Pulin Bihari Das (most organised) 1902 Nath Basu Satish Chandra Basu

mcqs.question: Barindranath Ghosh (acc. to Shekhar Bandhopadhyay's book) * Barindra Ghosh was associated [U.P. Lower Sub. (Pre) 2008]; [U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2016] Anushilan Samiti 5. Aurobindo Ghosh was brilliantly defended in the Alipore Conspiracy Case by –
mcqs.explanation: In the Alipore Conspiracy Case (1908), Aurobindo Ghose was defended by Chittaranjan Das with relentless effort.

mcqs.question: Which among the following organisations was responsible for throwing a bomb at Viceroy Lord Hardinge in Delhi?
mcqs.explanation: The Anushilan Samiti was responsible for throwing a bomb at Viceroy Lord Hardinge in Delhi. The Hardinge Bomb Case is famous as the Delhi Conspiracy Case.

mcqs.question: The Hindustan Republican Association was founded at –
mcqs.explanation: In order to conduct the revolutionary movement in the country in a proper manner, young revolutionaries convened a conference at Kanpur in October 1924 and established a revolutionary organization named the ‘Hindustan Republican Association’ (H.R.A.). Its founders were Sachindra Sanyal (President), Ram Prasad Bismil, Jogesh Chandra Chatterjee, Chandrashekhar Azad, and others.

mcqs.question: Who among the following was not the member of the Hindustan Republican Association (HRA)?
mcqs.explanation: Shiv Verma was not a member of the Hindustan Republican Association (H.R.A.). Later, he became associated with its successor organization, the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (H.S.R.A.). The other three – Bhagat Singh, Chandrashekhar Azad, and Ram Prasad Bismil were members of the H.R.A. Shiv Verma was sentenced to life imprisonment in the Lahore Conspiracy Case.

mcqs.question: Who amongst the following revolutionaries refused to drink the given milk on the eve of his execution and said “Now, I shall take my mother’s milk only.” ?
mcqs.explanation: When milk was offered to the famous revolutionary Pandit Ram Prasad Bismil two days before his execution, he refused it and said, “Now I shall take my mother’s milk only.” In its initial answer key, the Uttar Pradesh Public Service Commission had shown option (c) as the answer to this question, but in the revised answer key, the question was deleted.

mcqs.question: Kakori Conspiracy Case took place in the year :
mcqs.explanation: In October 1924, Sachindra Sanyal, Ram Prasad Bismil, and Chandrashekhar Azad established the revolutionary organization ‘Hindustan Republican Association’ at Kanpur. On 9 August 1925, this organization looted government money by robbing the ‘8 Down Saharanpur- Lucknow Passenger Train’ at a place called Kakori on the Lucknow-Saharanpur section of the Northern Railway. This incident became famous as the Kakori Incident (Kakori Train Action). In this case, 29 revolutionaries were arrested, out of whom Ram Prasad Bismil, Ashfaqulla, Roshan Lal, and Rajendra Lahiri were hanged, while Chandrashekhar Azad remained absconding. He was the only member of the Hindustan Republican Association who never came into police custody. Thus, he escaped the Kakori Case trial. Finally, on 27 February 1931, he was killed in a police encounter at Alfred Park (now Chandrashekhar Azad Park) in Allahabad (present-day Prayagraj). Sachindranath Bakshi, Mukundi Lal, and Manmathnath Gupta were also involved in the trial of the Kakori Case.

mcqs.question: Among the following revolutionaries not associated with Kakori Conspiracy –
mcqs.explanation: Bhagat Singh was not associated with the Kakori Conspiracy Case.

mcqs.question: Who among the following was Government advocate in Kakori Conspiracy Case?
mcqs.explanation: The Kakori incident (Kakori Train Action, 1925) was carried out by the Hindustan Republican Association (HRA). Many persons were arrested in this case and put on trial. Jagat Narayan Mulla was appointed to appear on behalf of the government, while Lakshmi Shankar Mishra, K.C. Dutt, and Jaikaran Nath Mishra appeared for the accused.

mcqs.question: Who among the following was NOT associated with the Kanpur Conspiracy Case of 1924?
mcqs.explanation: In order to check the strength and growing influence of the communist movement, some communists were prosecuted in Kanpur on the basis of an alleged conspiracy. This case became famous as the Kanpur Conspiracy Case. In it, M.N. Roy, Shripad Amrit Dange, Nalini Gupta, Muzaffar Ahmad, Shaukat Usmani, Ghulam Shaukat Husain, and Singaravelu Chettiar were prosecuted.

mcqs.question: “Daro-deewar pe hasrat ki nazar karte hain, khush raho ahle-vatan ham to safar karte hain.’’ was said by:
mcqs.explanation: The above lines are by Wajid Ali Shah, the last Nawab of Awadh. This nazm was used by Indian revolutionaries during imprisonment and at the time of execution.

mcqs.question: Who was the founder of ‘Hindustan Socialist Democratic Union’?

options.a: Gopen Chakravarti, Fanindra Banerjee, Dharni Goswami
options.c: Vyomesh Chandra, Gopen Chakravartee, Sachindra Sanyal
options.d: Vyomesh Chandra Banerjee, Ajay Ghosh, Sachindra Sanyal

mcqs.explanation: No organization by the name Hindustan Socialist Democratic Union existed in history. In Srikrishan ‘Sarala’s book 'Indian Revolutionaries 1757–1947, Vol.-3', the organization formed in 1928 by Bhagat Singh, Chandrashekhar Azad, Shachindra Sanyal and others has been referred to by this name; however, in contemporary documents and authentic works of history, the name of this organization is given as the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA). Thus, there are two errors in the question asked by the Commission: first, in the name of the organization; and second, if the names of the founding members given in the options are considered, Yatindranath Mukherjee had already been martyred in 1915. Gopen Chakravarty and Dharani Goswami were members of the Calcutta Anushilan Samiti, were associated with the communist movement, and were accused in the Meerut Conspiracy Case; but neither of them was a member of the HSRA. Byomesh Chandra Banerjee was a moderate leader and the first President of the Indian National Congress. Therefore, as far as the founding members of the HSRA are concerned, none of the options is correct.

mcqs.question: Hindustan Socialist Republican Association was formed by:
mcqs.explanation: In September 1928, under the leadership of Chandrashekhar Azad, the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (H.S.R.A.) was established at the Feroz Shah Kotla Ground in Delhi. Its objective was to establish a socialist republican state in India. During the protest against the Simon Commission, Saunders, the Assistant Superintendent of Police, was assassinated in December 1928 by Bhagat Singh, Chandrashekhar Azad, and Rajguru. This was the first revolutionary activity of the organization. Two members of the H.S.R.A., Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutt, threw bombs in the Central Legislative Assembly on 8 April 1929, when a debate was going on over the Trade Disputes Bill and the Public Safety Bill. Their purpose was to make the deaf British government hear, not to kill anyone.

mcqs.question: Who among the following changed the name of Hindustan Republic Association established by Sachindra Nath Sanyal to Hindustan Socialist Republican Association –
mcqs.explanation: Vijay Kumar Singh, Shiv Verma, Jaidev Kapoor, Bhagat Singh, Bhagwati Charan Vohra, and Sukhdev, under the leadership of Chandrashekhar Azad, began the work of reorganizing the H.R.A. In the meeting held in September 1928 at Feroz Shah Kotla, Delhi, the name of the H.R.A. was changed to the ‘Hindustan Socialist Republican Association’ (H.S.R.A.). Its main objective was to establish a socialist republican state in India.

mcqs.question: How revolutionary Chandrasekhar Azad was killed by the Britishers –
mcqs.explanation: Even after the arrest of Bhagat Singh, the famous revolutionary Chandrashekhar Azad continued revolutionary activities. He was the only member of the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association who was never caught by the police. However, on 27 February 1931, acting on information given by an informer, the police surrounded him in Alfred Park (now Chandrashekhar Azad Park) in Allahabad (present-day Prayagraj). Till the very end, this immortal son of Mother India bravely faced the brutal police, and when only the last bullet remained, he laid down his life himself.

mcqs.question: Who gave the ‘Inquilab Zindabad’ slogan?
mcqs.source: U.P. Lower Sub. (Pre) 2004; U.P. U.D.A. / L.D.A. (Pre) 2010 U.P. U.D.A./L.D.A. (Spl) (Mains) 2010
mcqs.explanation: The slogan “Inquilab Zindabad” was written by Maulvi Hasrat Mohani, while Bhagat Singh made this slogan popular.

mcqs.question: Lahore conspiracy case resulted in the hanging of 1. Ram Prasad Bismil 2. Roshan Singh 3. Bhagat Singh 4. Sukhdev 5. Rajguru Select the correct answer from the codes given below : Code :
mcqs.explanation: Under the Lahore Conspiracy Case, the Special Tribunal, in October 1930, sentenced Bhagat Singh, Rajguru, and Sukhdev to death. On 23 March 1931, these immortal sons of Mother India were hanged, while Batukeshwar Dutt was sentenced to transportation for life and sent to the Cellular Jail in the Andamans.

mcqs.question: Bhagat Singh’s memorial is situated at –
mcqs.explanation: The Shaheed Bhagat Singh Memorial is located in Firozpur, where every year on 23 March, thousands of people pay tribute.

mcqs.question: Name the first recorded Muslim who was hanged for Indian freedom
mcqs.explanation: Ashfaqullah Khan was the first recorded Muslim to be hanged for India’s independence. He was executed in Faizabad Jail (present-day Ayodhya) on 19 December 1927, at the age of 27, in the Kakori Conspiracy Case. He was born on 22 October 1900 in Shahjahanpur (U.P.). However, if the Revolt of 1857 is also taken into account, then the answer to this question would be Azizuddin, because after suppressing the Delhi Revolt in 1857, the British hanged Mughal prince Mirza Azizuddin along with six other Mughal princes at Delhi Gate in November 1857.

mcqs.question: Given below is a list of some cases. Select their correct chronological order by using the codes given at the end: 1. Lahore case 2. Kakori case 3. Meerut case 4. Kanpur case Code :
mcqs.explanation: The first Lahore Conspiracy Case took place in 1916 after the Ghadar Movement, while the second conspiracy case took place in 1930 in connection with Bhagat Singh and others. The Kanpur Conspiracy Case was of 1924, the Kakori Conspiracy Case (Kakori Train Action) was of 1925, and the Meerut Conspiracy Case was of 1929. With reference to the first Lahore Conspiracy Case, the correct answer will be option (c).

mcqs.question: Which one of the following pairs is not correctly matched?
mcqs.explanation: The Kakori Conspiracy Case refers to the train robbery (Kakori Train Action) carried out on 9 August 1925 under the leadership of the revolutionary Ramprasad Bismil. In this incident, the revolutionaries looted government money being transported by train at a place called Kakori near Lucknow. Revolutionaries such as Chandrashekhar Azad, Sachindra Sanyal, Manmath Nath Gupta, and Rajendra Lahiri were involved in this incident. In the first and second Lahore Conspiracy Cases, the relevant dates were 1916 and 1930 respectively; therefore, option (c) is correctly matched. Similarly, options (a) and (b) are also correctly matched.

mcqs.question: Which of the following pairs is not correctly matched?

options.d: Nasik Conspiracy Case - Ras Bihari Bose

mcqs.explanation: The Delhi Conspiracy Case was related to Amir Chand, the Kakori Conspiracy Case to Ashfaqullah Khan, and the Lahore Conspiracy Case to Jatin Das, whereas Ras Bihari Bose was associated with the Delhi Conspiracy Case. He fled to Japan to avoid arrest. Therefore, option (d) is the correct answer.

mcqs.question: Match List- I with List- II and select the correct answer from the code given below: List- I List- II (Organizations) (Founders) A. Abhinav Bharat 1. V.D. Savarkar B. Mitra Mela 2. G.D. Savarkar C. Indian Republican Army 3. S.N. Sanyal D. Hindustan Republic 4. S. Sen Association Code : A B C D
mcqs.explanation: The correct matching is as follows– Organization Founder Co-founder Abhinav Bharat – V.D. Savarkar Mitra Mela – V.D. Savarkar Indian Republican Army – S. Sen (Surya Sen) Hindustan Republican Association – S.N. Sanyal

mcqs.question: On what charge was Jatin Das arrested:
mcqs.explanation: Jatin Das was arrested in connection with the Lahore Conspiracy Case. He went on a hunger strike in jail to demand political-prisoner status. After a 63-day hunger strike, he died on 13 September 1929.

mcqs.question: Under whose chairmanship a committee was formed to defend the accused in Kakori Case?
mcqs.explanation: Yogesh Chandra Chatterjee, one of the founding members of the Hindustan Republican Association, who was sentenced to life imprisonment in connection with the Kakori Case, clearly wrote in his autobiography 'In Search of Freedom' that Pandit Motilal Nehru formed the Kakori Case Defence Committee under the leadership of Pandit Govind Ballabh Pant. In an article by Shankar Narayan Rao published on the PIB website, it is mentioned that Pandit Motilal Nehru was the chairman of the defence committee in the main trial. Here, taking Chatterjee’s book as the primary source, option (b) is accepted as the correct answer. Initially, the Uttar Pradesh Public Service Commission treated option (d) as correct, but in the revised answer key, option (b) was accepted as correct.

mcqs.question: Match List- I with List- II and select the correct answer from the codes given below the lists: List- I (Associations) List- II (Founders) A. Revolt group 1. Rama Prasad Bismil B. Hindustan Republican 2. Chandra Shekhar Azad Association C. Hindustan Socialist 3. Lala Lajpat Rai Republican 4. Bhagat Singh Association D. Punjab Naujawan 5. Surya Sen Bharat Sabha Code : A B C D
mcqs.explanation: The correct matching is as follows– Revolt Group – Surya Sen Hindustan Republican – Ram Prasad Bismil Association Hindustan Socialist – Chandrashekhar Azad Republican Association Punjab Naujawan Bharat Sabha – Bhagat Singh

mcqs.question: Who among the following was NOT an early member of the 'Naujawan-Sabha' formed in 1926 A.D.?
mcqs.explanation: In 1926, the Naujawan Sabha was founded at Lahore (now in Pakistan) by Sardar Bhagat Singh, Chhabil Das, Yashpal, Ramchandra, Bhagwati Charan Vohra and others. Its objective was to establish a workers’ and peasants’ state in India. Ambika Chakravarti joined it later.

mcqs.question: Given below is a list of organizations. Select those engaged in revolutionary activities, using the codes given below the lists: 1. Abhinav Bharat 2. Anushilan Samiti 3. New Nationalist Party 4. Indian Patriot Association Code :
mcqs.explanation: Abhinav Bharat and Anushilan Samiti were both revolutionary organizations. The ‘Indian Patriotic Association’ was founded by Sir Syed Ahmad Khan in 1888 in opposition to the Congress.

mcqs.question: Which of the following revolutionary was hanged in the Gorakhpur Jail-
mcqs.explanation: The Kakori incident took place on 9 August, 1925. Ram Prasad Bismil, Ashfaqullah Khan, Roshan Singh and Rajendra Lahiri were tried in this case and were sentenced to death. Ram Prasad Bismil was hanged in Gorakhpur Jail. Rajendra Lahiri was hanged in Gonda, Roshan Singh in Allahabad, and Ashfaqullah Khan in Faizabad.

mcqs.question: Who among the revolutionary leaders attempted to assassinate Charles Tegart the hated Police Commis- sioner of Calcutta?
mcqs.explanation: On 12 January, 1924, on Chowringhee Road in Calcutta, the revolutionary leader Gopinath Saha made an unsuccessful attempt to kill Charles Tegart, the notorious Police Commissioner of Calcutta, but unfortunately an Englishman named Ernest Day was shot.

mcqs.question: Who among the following female revolutionary fired at the English Governor (Chancellor) while receiving her degree at the convocation?
mcqs.explanation: In February, 1932, Bina Das fired at the Governor from a very close range while receiving her degree at the convocation.

mcqs.question: Who said, “Criticism and independent thinking are the two necessary traits of a revolutionary”?
mcqs.explanation: Bhagat Singh said, “Criticism and independent thinking are the two necessary traits of a revolutionary.”

mcqs.question: Consider the following events and arrange them in chronological order. I. The foundation of Ghadar Party II. Chittagaon Armoury Raid III. Set up of the ‘Indian Independence Committee’ at Berlin IV. Central Assembly Bomb Case Select the correct answer from the code given below: Code :
mcqs.explanation: The chronological order of the above events is as follows – Foundation of the Ghadar Party – 21 April, 1913 Foundation of the ‘Indian – 1914 Independence Committee’ in Berlin Central Assembly Bomb Case – 8 April, 1929 Chittagong Armoury Raid – 18 April, 1930

mcqs.question: The Indian Home Rule Society in London was started by–
mcqs.explanation: In February, 1905, Shyamji Krishna Varma founded the ‘Indian Home Rule Society’ in London. He also established ‘India House’ there. A newspaper titled ‘The Indian Sociologist’ was also published from there. Due to the special activity of the government machinery in London, Shyamji later moved from there to Paris and finally to Geneva.

mcqs.question: Who among the following founded the ‘Ghadar Party’?
mcqs.explanation: In 1913, Sohan Singh Bhakna founded an organization named the ‘Association of Hindustani Workers of the Pacific Coast’ or the ‘Hindustan Association of the Pacific Coast’. He was its founding president. This organization started a newspaper called ‘Ghadar’, because of which the organization itself came to be known as the ‘Ghadar Party’. Lala Hardayal was the main ideologue and guide of this organization. Since the name of Sohan Singh Bhakna is not given in the options, option (a) is the correct answer.

mcqs.question: Who among the following was NOT associated with Ghadar Party?
mcqs.explanation: The Ghadar Party was founded by Sohan Singh Bhakna on 21 April, 1913, with the objective of liberating India from British rule. It was formed by Indians living in the United States and Canada. The headquarters of the party was situated in San Francisco, USA. Lala Hardayal was the ideological guide of this organization. Prominent members of the Ghadar Party included Ram Chandra, Barkatullah, Rash Behari Bose, Raja Mahendra Pratap, Abdul Rahman, Madam Bhikaji Cama, Bhai Parmanand, Kartar Singh Sarabha, and Pandit Kanshi Ram. On 30 April, 1908, at Muzaffarpur in Bihar, Khudiram Bose and Prafulla Chaki threw a bomb at Kingsford; however, unfortunately, the wife and daughter of Mr. Kennedy, who was sympathetic to the national movement, were killed. After this incident, Prafulla Chaki committed suicide, whereas Khudiram Bose was hanged on 11 August, 1908. At the time of his execution, he was 18 years, 8 months, and 8 days old. Thus, it is clear that Khudiram Bose had no association with the Ghadar Party. Therefore, option (d) is the correct answer.

mcqs.question: Who among the following established a Republican Government abroad?
mcqs.explanation: Raja Mahendra Pratap, along with his associate Barkatullah, formed the first Provisional Government of India at Kabul (Afghanistan) in 1915 during the First World War. Raja Mahendra Pratap himself was its President, while Barkatullah was the Prime Minister. This government was also recognized by Germany and Russia.

mcqs.question: Who is regarded as the “Mother of Indian Revolu- tion”:
mcqs.explanation: Bhikaji Rustom Cama was a supporter of revolutionary nationalism. She carried on revolutionary activities from Europe and America. In 1907, she participated in the International Socialist Congress held at Stuttgart, Germany, where she became the first person to unfurl the flag of Indian independence on foreign soil. At the same conference, she proclaimed with full force her resolve to struggle for freedom. She continued to work for India’s independence from Paris for thirty years. She is renowned as the “Mother of Indian Revolution.”

mcqs.question: Which of the following pair got sentence to be hanged for assassination of the British officers in England -

options.c: Madan Lal Dhingra and Udham Singh
options.d: Kartar Singh Sarabha and Ashfaqullah Khan

mcqs.explanation: Madanlal Dhingra and Udham Singh were sentenced to death on the charge of killing British officials in England. It may be noted that on 1 July, 1909, in London, Madanlal Dhingra shot Curzon Wyllie, adviser to the Secretary of State for India, and Cawas Lalcaca dead. As a result, he was sentenced to death. In March 1940, Udham Singh assassinated Michael O’Dwyer in London, the then Governor of Punjab, who was indirectly responsible for the Jallianwala Bagh massacre; consequently, he too was hanged.
mcqs.chapter: Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movement

mcqs.question: Who one of the following was associated with ‘Kamaga- tamaru episode’?
mcqs.explanation: Komagata Maru was a ship bound for Canada, which Baba Gurdit Singh had hired during the First World War. Carrying 376 passengers, it sailed from Hong Kong to Canada. However, these passengers were not allowed to enter Canada. Although the name of Bhag Singh/Bhagat Singh is also found among those killed in the Komagata Maru episode, no special mention of him in direct connection with this incident is generally found.
mcqs.chapter: Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movement

mcqs.question: Who had established “India Independence League”?
mcqs.source: U.P. P.C.S. (Spl) (Pre) 2008; U.P.U.D.A./L.D.A. (Mains) 2010 U.P. Lower Sub. (Spl) (Pre) 2008
mcqs.explanation: Rash Behari Bose was an Indian expatriate residing in Japan. During 28–30 March, 1942, he organized a conference of Indians in Tokyo to discuss political issues. At the Bangkok Conference held from 14–23 June, 1942, it was given formal shape, and Subhas Chandra Bose was invited. At this conference, Rash Behari Bose founded the “Indian Independence League.”

mcqs.question: Which of the following occurred last:
mcqs.explanation: Among the events mentioned in the question, the earliest was the introduction of the Permanent Settlement system by Lord Cornwallis in 1793. Lord Wellesley (1798–1805) used the Subsidiary Alliance system to bring Indian states within the British political framework. Lord Dalhousie (1848–56) used the Doctrine of Lapse to expand the British Empire. Bengal was partitioned by Lord Curzon in 1905. Thus, option (b) is the correct answer.
mcqs.chapter: Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movement

mcqs.question: Anti partition movement of Bengal was initiated on:
mcqs.explanation: The British Government announced the decision to partition Bengal on 20 July, 1905. On 7 August, 1905, in a historic meeting held at the Town Hall in Calcutta, the Swadeshi Movement was formally declared. In this meeting, the historic boycott resolution was passed. Thereafter, the anti- Partition movement in different parts of Bengal formally began in a united manner. The partition of Bengal came into effect on 16 October, 1905. In the Delhi Durbar of 1911, the annulment of the partition of Bengal was announced.
mcqs.chapter: Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movement

mcqs.question: When did the Anti-Partition Movement begin with a massive demonstration at the Town Hall, Calcutta?
mcqs.explanation: On 7 August, 1905, a huge public meeting was held at the Town Hall in Calcutta, in which the Boycott Resolution was passed and the Swadeshi and Boycott Movement was formally launched. This meeting is regarded as the beginning of the organized mass movement against the Partition of Bengal.
mcqs.chapter: Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movement

mcqs.question: The Lieutenant Governor of Bengal at the time of Partition of Bengal was :
mcqs.explanation: Sir Andrew Henderson Leith Fraser was a British Indian Civil Service officer. He served as the Lieutenant-Governor of Bengal from 1903 to 1908. He played an important role in the plan for the partition of Bengal in 1905.
mcqs.chapter: Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movement

mcqs.question: Who among of the following led the agitation against the partition of Bengal (1905)?
mcqs.explanation: The initial movement against the partition of Bengal in 1905 was led by Surendranath Banerjee.
mcqs.chapter: Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movement

mcqs.question: Who among the following were the critics of Swadeshi' movement and pleaded for a better understanding between the East and the West?
mcqs.explanation: Rabindranath Tagore was a critic of the Swadeshi Movement and a supporter of a better relationship and harmony between Eastern and Western civilizations.
mcqs.chapter: Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movement

mcqs.question: Who was the first to suggest the boycott of British goods in Bengal?
mcqs.explanation: The boycott of British goods in Bengal was first suggested by Krishna Kumar Mitra, the editor of the Bengali journal Sanjivani, in its issue dated 13 July, 1905.
mcqs.chapter: Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movement

mcqs.question: Boycott of British goods was adopted as a national policy in –
mcqs.explanation: Lord Curzon announced the partition of Bengal on 20 July, 1905. As a result, the Swadeshi Movement was declared at the Town Hall in Calcutta on 7 August, 1905. In the same meeting, the historic Boycott Resolution was passed, through which the boycott of British goods was adopted as a national policy.
mcqs.chapter: Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movement

mcqs.question: Partition of Bengal was done mainly for :

options.a: To divide the Hindu and Muslims
options.c: To weaken the growth of Nationalism in Bengal

mcqs.explanation: Although outwardly the British Government stated that its objective was administrative convenience, in reality the partition of Bengal was mainly carried out to weaken the growth of Bengali nationalism. According to the then Viceroy, Lord Curzon, "this was an attempt to dethrone Calcutta and divide the Bengali population, and to put an end to a centre from where the Congress was being directed in Bengal as well as in the rest of the country, and where conspiracies were being hatched".
mcqs.chapter: Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movement

mcqs.question: In which year partition of Bengal made by Lord Curzon was cancelled ?
mcqs.explanation: In December 1911, when British Emperor George V and Queen Mary visited India, a Durbar was organised in Delhi to welcome them. It was in the Delhi Durbar, on 12 December 1911, that the Emperor announced the revocation of the partition of Bengal. At the same time, he also declared Delhi, in place of Calcutta, as the new capital of India. In accordance with this announcement, Bengal was reorganised as a new province. Orissa and Bihar were separated from it. Assam was made a new province, as it had been in 1874, and Sylhet was added to it.
mcqs.chapter: Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movement

mcqs.question: Who was the leader of the Swadeshi Movement in Madras?
mcqs.explanation: The Swadeshi Movement, which began in Bengal, was led by Lokmanya Tilak in Bombay and Pune, by Ajit Singh and Lala Lajpat Rai in Punjab and Uttar Pradesh, by Syed Haider Raza in Delhi, and by Chidambaram Pillai in the Madras Presidency.
mcqs.chapter: Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movement

mcqs.question: Vande Mataram became the theme song of the Indian National Movement during –
mcqs.explanation: During the Swadeshi Movement, 16 October 1905, the day on which the partition came into effect, was observed throughout Bengal as a 'Day of Mourning'. No hearths were lit in homes, people observed fasts, and a strike was declared in Calcutta. The public brought out processions. Early in the morning, group after group of people took bath in the Ganga and then marched through the streets singing ‘Vande Mataram’. It was during this movement that ‘Vande Mataram’ became the theme song of the national movement.
mcqs.chapter: Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movement

mcqs.question: Which of the statement is not correct regarding ‘Swadeshi Movement’?

options.a: Some specific Muslims were joined in it.
options.b: Women’s actively participated in this movement
options.c: Neither this movement affected Bengal farmers and nor they were joined

mcqs.explanation: The Swadeshi Movement could attract only a few notable Muslims from different sections of society. For the first time, women came out of their homes in this movement, began taking part in demonstrations, and started joining sit-ins. However, this movement could not influence the peasants of Bengal, and they also did not join it, with Barisal being the only exception. Mainly, this movement remained confined to the upper and middle classes of the cities. The Swadeshi Movement was not confined only to Bengal; rather, Lala Lajpat Rai, Tilak, and Aurobindo Ghosh spread it throughout the country. Thus, statement (d) is not correct.
mcqs.chapter: Congress: Benaras, Calcutta, and Surat Session

mcqs.question: The British journalist H.W. Nevinson was associated with:
mcqs.explanation: British journalist H.W. Nevinson was associated with the Swadeshi Movement. During this period, he stayed in India for four months and reported for the Manchester Guardian, the Glasgow Herald, and the Daily Chronicle. Later, he published these reports in the form of a book titled 'The New Spirit in India'.
mcqs.chapter: Congress: Benaras, Calcutta, and Surat Session

mcqs.question: Who among the following had founded the ‘Indian Society of Oriental Art’ to revive ancient art traditions of India?
mcqs.explanation: In the atmosphere created by the growing influence of the national movement, Abanindranath Tagore, along with his elder brother Gaganendranath, founded the Indian Society of Oriental Art in 1907. Through this institution, Oriental art values were revived and a new awareness was created in modern Indian art.
mcqs.chapter: Congress: Benaras, Calcutta, and Surat Session

mcqs.question: Gopal Krishna Gokhale presided over the session of Congress in –
mcqs.explanation: Gopal Krishna Gokhale presided over the Benares Session of the Indian National Congress in 1905.
mcqs.chapter: Congress: Benaras, Calcutta, and Surat Session

mcqs.question: In which of the following sessions of Indian National Congress, the word ‘Swaraj’ was uttered for the first time?
mcqs.explanation: The word ‘Swaraj’ was used for the first time from the Congress platform by Dadabhai Naoroji at the Calcutta Session of the Indian National Congress in 1906. While explaining the term ‘Swaraj’, Dadabhai Naoroji also declared it to be the objective of the Indian National Congress at the same session. Initially, the Uttar Pradesh Public Service Commission treated option (b) as the correct answer, but in the revised answer key, the answer was cancelled. Since there is variation regarding the dates associated with the use of the word ‘Swaraj’, the answer was probably cancelled for this reason.
mcqs.chapter: Congress: Benaras, Calcutta, and Surat Session

mcqs.question: The first leader to use the word ‘Swaraj’ was :
mcqs.explanation: Bal Gangadhar Tilak said, “Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it.” However, the word ‘Swaraj’ was first used by Dayanand Saraswati. But among the given options, Tilak was the first to support the demand for Swaraj.
mcqs.chapter: Congress: Benaras, Calcutta, and Surat Session

mcqs.question: Dadabhai Naroji was formally known as :
mcqs.explanation: Dadabhai Naoroji is remembered with great respect as the ‘Grand Old Man of India’. In 1892, he became the first Indian to be elected to the British Parliament from Finsbury on the Liberal Party ticket. He also served as President of the Indian National Congress in 1886, 1893 and 1906.
mcqs.chapter: Congress: Benaras, Calcutta, and Surat Session

mcqs.question: The first Indian to contest election to the British House of Commons was:
mcqs.explanation: The first Indian to contest an election to the House of Commons in Britain was Lal Mohan Ghose in 1885. After that, Dadabhai Naoroji contested the election in 1886, but lost. In 1892, Naoroji won from the Finsbury seat. Since the name of Lal Mohan Ghose is not given in the options, option (a), Dadabhai Naoroji, is treated as the correct answer.
mcqs.chapter: Congress: Benaras, Calcutta, and Surat Session

mcqs.question: Which one of the following statements is not correct about Dadabhai Naoroji?

options.a: He wrote a book ‘Poverty and Un-British Rule in India.’
options.b: He worked as a Professor of Gujarati in the University College, London
options.c: He laid the foundation of woman’s education in Bombay
options.d: He was elected as a member of British Parliament on the ticket of the Conservative Party

mcqs.explanation: Dadabhai Naoroji was elected to the British Parliament in 1892 on the ticket of the Liberal Party. Therefore, statement (d) is incorrect, while the other three statements are true.

mcqs.question: Which one of the following statements is not correct about Dadabhai Naoroji?

options.a: He was the first Indian to be appointed as Professor of Mathematics and Physics at Elphinstone College, Bombay.
options.b: He was elected as a member of British Parliament in 1892.
options.c: He started a Gujarati Journal, ‘Rast Goftar.’
options.d: For four times he had presided over the Indian National Congress.

mcqs.explanation: Dadabhai Naoroji presided over the Indian National Congress three times—in 1886, 1893 and 1906. The other three statements are correct.

mcqs.question: At which session was the Indian National Congress (INC) divided into two groups –’Naram Dal’ and Garam Dal’?
mcqs.explanation: At the 23rd annual session of the Congress, held at Surat in 1907, the Congress split because of differences between the Moderates and the Extremists over the issue of the presidency. The Extremists wanted Lala Lajpat Rai to be elected President, whereas the Moderates supported Rash Behari Ghosh. Ultimately, Rash Behari Ghosh was elected President. The dispute over the resolutions passed in 1906 – Swadeshi, Boycott, National Education and self-government – became deeper, and finally, after open conflict between the two sides, the first split in the Congress took place.

mcqs.question: Who among the following was the founder of All India Muslim League?
mcqs.explanation: In October 1906, the Simla Deputation of Muslims led by Aga Khan considered the formation of a central Muslim organization for the protection of Muslim interests. In keeping with this idea, during the All India Mohammadan Educational Conference held at Dhaka in December 1906, Nawab Salimullah Khan of Dhaka, who was the President of the Reception Committee of the conference and the convener of the political meetings, proposed the formation of the All India Muslim League. Wiqar-ul-Mulk was its President. A 56-member provisional committee was constituted, and Mohsin-ul-Mulk and Wiqar-ul-Mulk were jointly appointed as Secretaries of the organization. The headquarters of the Muslim League were established at Lucknow, and Aga Khan was made its first President. If all three of these names, or any two of them, are given in the options, the order of preference for selecting the founder will be as follows—

mcqs.question: Mohsin-ul-Mulk In the present question, since the first two names are given, Salimullah Khan will be selected as the founder by giving him first preference. * Who was the first President of the Muslim League [U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 1997] - Agha Khan 2. The annual session of the Muslim League in the year 1907 was held at –
mcqs.explanation: The Muslim League was founded in 1906 at Dhaka. Its annual session was held at Karachi in 1907 and at Amritsar in 1908.
mcqs.chapter: Congress: Benaras, Calcutta, and Surat Session

mcqs.question: Consider the following statements – Statement (A) : League refused to accept the Congress Muslim people rights together with the aim being to achieve. Reason (R) : Only the Muslim League has the right of such type. Code :

options.a: Both (A) and (R) are correct, and (R) is correct explanation of (A).
options.b: Both (A) and (R) are correct, and (R) is not correct explanation of (A).

mcqs.explanation: The League refused to recognize the Congress’s right to associate the Muslim masses with the achievement of its objectives because the League considered itself to be the sole representative organization of the Muslims. However, in reality, such an exclusive right did not belong to the Muslim League alone.

mcqs.question: Morley-Minto Reform Bill was passed in :
mcqs.explanation: In 1905, Lord Minto was appointed the Viceroy of India in place of Lord Curzon, and John Morley was appointed the Secretary of State for India. The reforms introduced by them are known as the Morley-Minto Reforms. The constitutional reforms passed by the British Parliament, formally known as the Indian Councils Act, 1909, are generally referred to as the Morley-Minto Reforms.

mcqs.question: The Indian Council Act of 1909 was provided for :
mcqs.explanation: The biggest defect of the Indian Councils Act, 1909 (Morley- Minto Reforms) was the provision of separate electorates for Muslims under the system of communal representation.
mcqs.chapter: Delhi Durbar and Change of Capital

mcqs.question: Seeds of discord were in which event during National Movement and which eventually divided the country, was–

options.d: Reservation of seats and separate electorates for Muslims in legislative assemblies. U.P

mcqs.explanation: The worst aspect of the Morley-Minto Reforms of 1909 was the provision of separate or communal electorates for Muslims. This provision later poisoned the public and communal life of India and ultimately sowed the seeds of the partition of the country.

mcqs.question: It claimed the same communal representation for non- Brahmins as the Morley-Minto reforms had given to Muslims. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
mcqs.explanation: The Justice Party was formed in 1916 in the Madras Presidency. It represented the interests of non-Brahmin communities, especially the lower castes and backward classes. C.N. Mudaliar, T.M. Nair, P. Theagaraya Chetty, etc. were its major leaders. This party accused the Congress of being Brahmin-dominated and demanded social justice, educational opportunities, and caste-based representation. On the pattern of the communal representation granted to Muslims under the Morley-Minto Reforms, this party demanded caste-based representation for non-Brahmins. Therefore, both the given statements are correct.

mcqs.question: Which of the following events took place in the year 1911 ? 1. Partition of Bengal revoked 2. Transfer of capital from Calcutta to Delhi 3. Lucknow pact between Congress and Muslim League Select the correct answer from the code given below : Code :
mcqs.explanation: Annulment of the Partition of Bengal (1911): The Partition of Bengal, carried out in 1905, was announced to be annulled at the Delhi Durbar on 12 December 1911. The administrative reorganization, such as the creation of Orissa, became effective in 1912, but since the announcement of annulment was made in 1911, this is regarded as an event of 1911. Transfer of the capital from Calcutta to Delhi (1911): At the same Delhi Durbar on 12 December 1911, the decision to shift the capital of India from Calcutta to Delhi was announced. The formal transfer and the gradual shifting of offices were completed in 1912; however, the announcement was made in 1911. Lucknow Pact (1916): The Lucknow Pact between the Congress and the Muslim League took place in 1916. Therefore, the correct answer is option (a).
mcqs.chapter: Delhi Durbar and Change of Capital

mcqs.question: The transfer of capital of British India from Calcutta to Delhi was affected during the period of –
mcqs.explanation: During British rule, Calcutta was the capital of India before Delhi. On the occasion of King George V’s visit to India on 12 December 1911, it was announced that the Partition of Bengal would be annulled and that the capital of India would be shifted from Calcutta to Delhi. This transfer took place during the tenure of Lord Hardinge. Delhi became the capital in 1912.
mcqs.chapter: Delhi Durbar and Change of Capital

mcqs.question: A bomb was thrown on the occasion of his State entry into Delhi :
mcqs.explanation: When Lord Hardinge was entering Delhi in a procession on 23 December 1912 on the occasion of the formal transfer of the capital, a bomb was thrown at him in Chandni Chowk.
mcqs.chapter: Delhi Durbar and Change of Capital

mcqs.question: In December, 1916 both Indian National Congress and Indian Muslim League held their session at:
mcqs.explanation: In December 1916, the Indian National Congress and the Indian Muslim League held their sessions at the same time at Lucknow. Ambika Charan Mazumdar presided over the Lucknow Session of the Congress.
mcqs.chapter: Lucknow Session of Congress (The Lucknow Pact)

mcqs.question: The famous ‘Lucknow Pact’ was signed between the Congress and Muslim League in:
mcqs.explanation: In 1916, the Congress and the Muslim League reached an agreement at Lucknow so that a common scheme of constitutional reforms could be adopted. As a result, the “19-point memorandum” gave concrete expression to the contemporary political ideas of both parties.
mcqs.chapter: Delhi Durbar and Change of Capital

mcqs.question: Who among the following was the chief architect or reconciliation between the Extremists and the Moderates?
mcqs.explanation: The Lucknow Session of the Indian National Congress in 1916, presided over by Ambika Charan Mazumdar, was memorable for two reasons. First, the Extremists, who had been excluded from the Congress nine years earlier in 1907, were readmitted to the Congress. Second, an agreement was reached between the Congress and the Muslim League. Annie Besant and Tilak played an important role in bringing about the reunion of the Extremists and the Moderates, while Muhammad Ali Jinnah and Tilak were the main architects of the Congress-League agreement.
mcqs.chapter: Delhi Durbar and Change of Capital

mcqs.question: Which one of the following presents period of unanimity between Indian National Congress and Muslim league?
mcqs.explanation: The period from 1916 to 1922 was the period of accord between the Indian National Congress and the Muslim League. The Lucknow Pact was only a temporary agreement. Despite this pact, the Muslim League maintained its separate identity and continued to advocate separate political rights for Muslims. Up to 1922, both organizations worked together in keeping with this understanding. However, with the launch of the Non-Cooperation Movement, this understanding came to an end, and the League once again reverted to its earlier course.
mcqs.chapter: Delhi Durbar and Change of Capital

mcqs.question: Which one of the following is not correct about the Congress Session of Lucknow, 1916?

options.a: Ambika Charan Majumdar was not the President of this session.
options.b: In this session, the reunion between the liberals and the extremist was established.
options.c: Mahatma Gandhi was apprised of the problems of the peasants of Champaran for the first time.

mcqs.explanation: At the Lucknow Session of the Congress in 1916, Tilak was re-admitted to the Congress. The president of this session, Ambika Charan Mazumdar, said, “After ten years of painful separation and needless disputes caused by misunderstandings, both camps of the Indian national party (the Moderates and the Extremists) have now realized that separation means defeat and unity means victory. The two brothers have come together once again.” It was also at the Lucknow Session of the Congress that Mahatma Gandhi met Rajkumar Shukla, who acquainted him with the problems of the Champaran peasants. Therefore, statement (a) is incorrect, whereas statements (b) and (c) are correct.
mcqs.chapter: Lucknow Session of Congress (The Lucknow Pact)

mcqs.question: Who launched the first Home Rule League Movement?
mcqs.explanation: In India, the Home Rule League Movement was first launched by Annie Besant, although the first Home Rule League had earlier been established in April 1916 by Tilak.

mcqs.question: Two Home Rule Leagues were started in 1915-16 under the leadership of:
mcqs.explanation: In April 1916, Tilak, and in September 1916, Annie Besant, established their respective Home Rule Leagues. Besant promoted her League through 'Commonweal' and 'New India', while Tilak promoted his League through 'Mahratta' and 'Kesari'.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is not associated with Home Rule Movement?
mcqs.explanation: Tilak launched the Home Rule League in April 1916 and Annie Besant in September 1916. S. Subrahmanyam Aiyar was also associated with Annie Besant’s Home Rule League. C.R. Das was not associated with the Home Rule Movement.
mcqs.chapter: Lucknow Session of Congress (The Lucknow Pact)

mcqs.question: Which of the following is not correct about the Home Rule League:

options.a: The plan was first presented in 1914-15 by Annie Besant
options.b: The Home Rule League of Tilak was confined to Maharashtra, Karnataka, Central Provinces and Berar
options.c: The Home Rule League founded by Tilak was much stronger
options.d: Despite the differences between Tilak and Besant, both the Leagues continued to exist

mcqs.explanation: Basically, the plan for establishing the Home Rule League was prepared by Annie Besant. The movement for self- rule began with the publication of the weekly journal 'Commonweal' on 2 January 1914. Keeping in view the objective of self-government within the British Empire, this journal adopted religious freedom, national education, and social and political reforms as its basic programme. To carry forward this programme, two separate Home Rule Leagues were established, and both were complementary to each other. In April 1916, Tilak established the Indian Home Rule League, and five months later, in September 1916, Mrs. Annie Besant established the Home Rule League. Tilak’s League was confined to six branches in Karnataka, Maharashtra (excluding Bombay), the Central Provinces, and Berar. The rest of the country was assigned to Annie Besant’s League. Besant’s League had a very loose organization; any three persons could open a branch anywhere, whereas Tilak’s League had a very strong organization, and the functions and areas of all six branches were clearly defined. The two Leagues did not merge because, in Annie Besant’s words, “Some of his supporters did not like me, and some of my supporters did not like him. But there was no quarrel of any kind between him and me.” Thus, there were no differences between Tilak and Besant.
mcqs.chapter: Lucknow Session of Congress (The Lucknow Pact)

mcqs.question: Karamchand Gandhi was Diwan of :
mcqs.explanation: Karamchand Gandhi was the Diwan of Porbandar, Rajkot, and Wankaner. He was the father of Gandhiji. His nickname was Kaba Gandhi.

mcqs.question: Name of the magazine published by Mahatma Gandhi during his stay in South Africa, was-:
mcqs.explanation: In South Africa, Gandhiji started a newspaper called 'Indian Opinion' (It was published in Gujarati, Hindi, Tamil, and English), and in 1904 he established the 'Phoenix Farm' at Durban.

mcqs.question: M.K. Gandhi was a supporter of –
mcqs.explanation: In Gandhiji’s thought, much greater emphasis was placed on practical idealism than on mere idealism. Like Marx, Gandhiji also wished to see the state removed, and he did not hesitate to be called a “Philosophical Anarchist.”

mcqs.question: The twin principles of Mahatma Gandhi’s Ram Rajya were?

options.d: Right means and right ends U.P

mcqs.explanation: “Truth” and “Non-violence” were the twin principles of Gandhiji’s Ramrajya.

mcqs.question: According to Gandhiji Non-Violence is:

options.b: A way to win political freedom
options.c: The only way to realize God

mcqs.explanation: Mahatma Gandhi made truth and non-violence the foundation of the new society of his dreams. Gandhiji used to say that “Truth and non-violence must be adopted in an absolute sense. Non-violence is the principle of my religion; it is also the ultimate principle of my action. It is the essential duty of a satyagrahi to strive for the attainment of truth through non-violence.”

mcqs.question: Which of the following may be true regarding Gandhi?

options.d: An Individualist among Socialists and a Marxist among Socialist

mcqs.explanation: From a practical point of view, Gandhiji’s ideas regarding the state may be called individualistic. Gandhiji was also a true socialist. He cared not only for the interest of the individual but also for the welfare of society. Gandhiji himself told Louis Fischer, “I am a true socialist. My socialism means Sarvodaya.” Gandhiji’s socialism also shows the influence of Marxism. Gandhiji himself said, “I am engaged in solving the same problem that scientific socialism faces.” Therefore, Gandhiji may be called an individualist among socialists and a Marxist among socialists.

mcqs.question: Which one of the following was the last step in the Gandhian strategy of Satyagraha?
mcqs.explanation: In Gandhiji’s satyagraha strategy, strike occupied the last place.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is not true as per Gandhian Principle?

options.a: The aim of Satyagrahi is to defeat the enemy
options.b: The weapon of Satyagraha is Ahimsa
options.c: Satyagrahi should be firm in his belief
options.d: Satyagrahi should have no ill feeling towards his enemies.

mcqs.explanation: In Gandhiji’s principle of satyagraha, the aim of a satyagrahi is not to defeat the enemy, but to bring about a change of heart and win him over.

mcqs.question: According to Gandhiji, the cruelest form of violence is
mcqs.explanation: Gandhiji had said, “Poverty is the worst form of violence.”

mcqs.question: Given below are two statements, in which one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R): Assertion (A) : The struggles in South Africa prepared Gandhiji to lead the National Movement. Reason (R) : Seeing the militancy of Indians in South Africa, Gandhiji was convinced that the Indian people would be ready for militant struggle and sacrifice for a cause. Select the correct answer using the code given below: Code -

options.a: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is correct explanation of (A).
options.b: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

mcqs.explanation: It was in South Africa that Gandhiji discovered himself. There he emerged from being a shy and timid young man into a successful organiser and leader. It was only after the struggles in South Africa that he prepared himself for leading national movements. The Indians in South Africa had come from diverse backgrounds. Under Gandhiji’s leadership, by following Satyagraha, they succeeded in getting various racist laws changed. Their tendency was completely non-violent; they lacked violence, aggression, etc. Therefore, Reason (R) is incorrect.

mcqs.question: In which of the following railway stations of South Africa, Mahatma Gandhi was thrown out of the train?
mcqs.explanation: During his stay in South Africa, Mahatma Gandhi had to face racial discrimination. Once, despite having a first-class ticket, he was asked to move to an ordinary compartment. When he resisted, he was thrown out of the train at Pietermaritzburg railway station.

mcqs.question: Which one of the following sessions of Indian National Congress was for the first time attended by M.K. Gandhi:
mcqs.explanation: Mahatma Gandhi first participated in the Calcutta Session of the Congress held in 1901.

mcqs.question: Where did Gandhiji adopt ‘Seva Dharma’?
mcqs.explanation: During his stay in South Africa, Mahatma Gandhi served as an attendant in a charitable hospital opened by the Parsi Rustomji and began the work of serving the sick and the distressed. There he also volunteered as a compounder. During the Boer War too, he looked after and served the wounded soldiers.

mcqs.question: Who among the following was the ‘Political Guru’ of Mahatma Gandhi?
mcqs.explanation: Gokhale was a true liberal in his political philosophy. He believed in impartiality and gentle justice. He had complete faith that the regeneration of the country could not be achieved through waves of political excitement. He believed in the purity of both means and ends. Influenced by these very ideas of Gokhale, Gandhiji accepted him as his political guru.

mcqs.question: As per Mahatma Gandhi politics meant –
mcqs.explanation: Mahatma Gandhi regarded politics as an instrument for social uplift and public welfare. In this regard, Gandhiji’s most important suggestion in the political sphere was the decentralisation of power. By decentralised power, he meant enabling village panchayats to manage and administer their own villages actively.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a feature of politics of the Gandhian model?
mcqs.explanation: The model of politics presented by Gandhiji included morality, religion, and humanity, but in his ideal political system there was no place for the state, that is, for authority or power. He wanted to establish a stateless society.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about Mahatma Gandhi are true? 1. He received his early education in Rajkot. 2. He married Kasturba at the age of 13. 3. He studied law at the Inner Temple, London. 4. He was most influenced by Ruskin’s book 'Unto the Last'. Select the correct answer from the code given below: Code :
mcqs.explanation: Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi was born on 2 October, 1869, at Porbandar in Gujarat. He received his early education successively at Porbandar and Rajkot. Mahatma Gandhi was married to Kasturba Gandhi at a very young age, when he was 13 years old. He studied law at the Inner Temple, London. Mahatma Gandhi was greatly influenced by Ruskin’s book 'Unto This Last'.

mcqs.question: Whose work has influenced the Gandhian concept?
mcqs.explanation: Among non-religious writers, Gandhian thought was most influenced by Thoreau, Ruskin, and Tolstoy. Gandhi derived inspiration for civil disobedience and refusal to pay taxes from Thoreau. From Ruskin, Gandhi learned the dignity of physical labour, and Tolstoy’s famous statement, “The Kingdom of God is Within You,” deeply influenced him and became the basis of his non-violent non-cooperation.

mcqs.question: Who amongst the following coined the word ‘Satyagraha’?
mcqs.explanation: Mahatma Gandhi’s nephew Maganlal Gandhi used the word ‘Sadagraha’ in a competition, for which he received a prize. The word 'Sadagraha' meant firmness in a good cause or truth. Later, Mahatma Gandhi modified it and changed it into ‘Satyagraha.’ Thus, it is clear that the word ‘Satyagraha’ was first given its final form and used by Mahatma Gandhi.

mcqs.question: Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi is best known for which of the following?

options.a: Use of passive resistance to achieve Indian Independence.
options.b: Desire to establish an Islamic nation.
options.c: Opposition to Hindus holding political office.
options.d: Encouragement of violence to end British rule.

mcqs.explanation: The struggle conducted by Gandhiji in South Africa was called passive resistance, but later Gandhi chose the word Satyagraha in place of passive resistance. This method was used most extensively in the struggle for Indian independence, although Gandhi distinguished between Satyagraha and passive resistance. According to him, passive resistance is a political weapon, whereas Satyagraha is a moral force.

mcqs.question: Who among the following used to say “Wrong means never lead us to right ends”?
mcqs.explanation: Mahatma Gandhi used to say, “Wrong means never lead us to the right ends.”

mcqs.question: Who among the following was the strong supporter of the principle that “Which is morally wrong, can never be politically right”?
mcqs.explanation: Mahatma Gandhi was a strong supporter of the establishment of moral values in politics. He believed that politics devoid of morality could drive the state into ruin. He held that whatever is morally wrong can never be politically right.

mcqs.question: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched regarding propounding the principle of Trusteeship of Mahatma Gandhi?
mcqs.explanation: Gandhiji established his law firm in Johannesburg in 1903, where he lived till 1910. The principle of Trusteeship is associated with his South African phase. In the other options, the years mentioned with the cities are not correct, because during those years Gandhi was in Johannesburg.

mcqs.question: Which one of the following statements is not correct about Gandhian economy?

options.a: He laid emphasis on the economy based on non- violence.
options.b: Centralisation lead to exploitation and inequality, hence centralisation is opponent of formation of non- violent society
options.c: He was not in favour of mechanisation in India
options.d: He did not favour mechanisation in U.S.A.

mcqs.explanation: Gandhiji believed that the economy of every country should be determined by keeping in mind its climate, land, and the nature of its inhabitants. On this basis, as far as America was concerned, he did not oppose mechanization there. On the other hand, Gandhiji supported options (a), (b), and (c).

mcqs.question: According to M.K. Gandhi socio-economic improve- ment of untouchables can be brought about :

options.c: By earmarking funds for their socio-economic development
options.d: By establishing cottage industry for them

mcqs.explanation: Gandhiji’s economic policy opposed all forms of exploitation, whether such exploitation was by one class over another within the country or from outside. To remove this, Gandhiji wanted to establish such a system in which an individual could work and labour in a free environment through his own efforts. For this, he wanted the revival of indigenous industries so that people could get sufficient food and not suffer from hunger. For this purpose, Gandhiji laid emphasis on cottage industries such as making jaggery, pressing oil, paper making, leather work, etc. Gandhiji believed that this would help in bringing about the economic and social upliftment of the poor and the oppressed.

mcqs.question: What does ‘Gandhian Innovation’ mean?

options.d: To produce more from less input for more people

mcqs.explanation: ‘Gandhian Innovation’ means “more production for more people at less investment.” This terminology was first used by Professor Prahalad and R.A. Mashelkar.

mcqs.question: Who opposed Planned Development in India?
mcqs.explanation: Among the given options, Mahatma Gandhi opposed planned development in India. Gandhiji was, in fact, opposed to industrialization and mechanization. While supporting cottage and rural industries, he regarded the village as the basic unit of the economy. He gave greater importance to labour-intensive enterprises instead of the use of machines so that maximum employment could be generated. Under his concept of Gram Swaraj, the village was an economic unit where all the needs of the residents could be fulfilled by products made there itself.

mcqs.question: Which one of the following was favoured by Nehru but not favoured by Gandhi?
mcqs.explanation: Nehru followed Gandhiji’s political and social principles such as truth, non-violence, and opposition to untouchability, but there were deep differences between the two on many economic principles. While Gandhiji emphasized the development of small-scale and cottage industries for India’s economic progress, Nehru was in favour of heavy industrialization.

mcqs.question: Who among of the following had told: “Destruction is the best method of dealing with the foreign clothes”?
mcqs.explanation: Mahatma Gandhi linked the destruction of foreign cloth with the self-respect of the nation and said that “the destruction is the best of dealing with foreign cloths.”

mcqs.question: Gandhi’s boycott of British made products was effective because the British considered India, a major :
mcqs.explanation: Gandhi’s boycott of British manufactured products became effective because Britain regarded India as a large market for manufactured goods.

mcqs.question: Which of the following Movement is not related to Gandhiji?
mcqs.explanation: Gandhiji was not associated with the Swadeshi Movement. The Swadeshi Movement took place in 1905 in protest against the partition of Bengal, and at that time Mahatma Gandhi was in South Africa.

mcqs.question: Which one of the following Satyagrahas was not lead by Mahatma Gandhi?
mcqs.explanation: Gandhiji led the Kheda Satyagraha (1918), the Civil Disobedience Movement (1930), and the Quit India Movement (1942), whereas the Bardoli Satyagraha (1928) was led not by Gandhiji but by Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is/are correct regarding Gandhi?

options.a: Fought hard to improve the status of casteless untouchables

mcqs.explanation: Gandhiji fought vigorously to improve the condition of the untouchables. Gandhiji used to say, “Service to the Harijans is the breath of my life; therefore, without it I cannot live even for a moment.” Gandhiji launched both the Non-Cooperation Movement and the Civil Disobedience Movement. Hence, option (d) is the correct answer.

mcqs.question: The prefix ‘Mahatma’ was added to the name of Gandhi:

options.b: During the Satyagraha against Rowlatt Act
options.c: In the Amritsar Session of the Indian National Congress, 1919
options.d: At the beginning of the Khilafat Movement

mcqs.explanation: Rabindranath Tagore first addressed him as ‘Mahatma’ because of his successful leadership of the Champaran Satyagraha.

mcqs.question: Who was the first person to call Mahatma Gandhi, ‘Father of Nation’?
mcqs.explanation: Subhas Chandra Bose was the first to call Mahatma Gandhi the ‘Father of the Nation’.

mcqs.question: Who addressed Gandhiji as ‘one-man boundary force’?
mcqs.explanation: Lord Mountbatten addressed Gandhiji as the ‘One Man Boundary Force’ and said, “What 50,000 armed soldiers could not do, Gandhiji accomplished.”

mcqs.question: Who one of the following had commanded Mahatma Gandhi to spend the first year in India ‘with his ears open but his mouth shut’?
mcqs.explanation: Mahatma Gandhi regarded Gopal Krishna Gokhale as his political guru. After returning to India from South Africa in 1915, it was Gopal Krishna Gokhale who advised Mahatma Gandhi to spend his first year in India “with his ears open but mouth shut.” Gokhale advised him to travel across the country for one year and understand the real condition of the country.

mcqs.question: Mahatma Gandhi delivered his first public speech in India at –
mcqs.explanation: Mahatma Gandhi delivered his first public speech in India in February 1916 on the occasion of the inauguration of Banaras Hindu University.

mcqs.question: From where did Gandhiji launch his mission of freeing bonded labour?
mcqs.explanation: Mahatma Gandhi began the Satyagraha movement in India from Champaran in Bihar. In Champaran, the farmers were forced by the British to cultivate indigo on 3/20 of their landholding (three kathas in a bigha). This was known as the Tinkathia system. If the farmers refused to cultivate indigo, the British subjected them to severe oppression. In addition, nearly 40 kinds of taxes had been imposed on them. Rajkumar Shukla, a farmer from Bihar, met Gandhiji and appealed to him to free the peasants from British oppression. During Gandhi’s stay in Calcutta, Rajkumar Shukla accompanied him, and in April 1917 Gandhi went to Champaran and started Satyagraha to free the peasants from British exploitation and forced labour. In July 1917, the Champaran Agrarian Committee was formed. Gandhiji was also one of its members. On the basis of this committee’s report, the Tinkathia system was abolished.

mcqs.question: Those who joined Mahatma Gandhi during the Champaran Satyagraha included:

options.a: Vallabh Bhai Patel and Vinoba Bhave
options.c: Rajendra Prasad and Anugraha Narain Sinha

mcqs.explanation: Pandit Rajkumar Shukla had invited Mahatma Gandhi to come to Champaran and inquire into the problems of the peasants. Gandhi’s associates in the inquiry into the Champaran issue included Dr. Rajendra Prasad, Mahadev Desai, C.F. Andrews, Dr. Anugrah Narayan Sinha, Raj Kishore Prasad, H.S. Polak, etc., along with Acharya J.B. Kripalani.

mcqs.question: Who among the following was not the member of Champaran Agrarian Enquiry Committee?
mcqs.explanation: F.G. Slye was the Chairman of the Champaran Agrarian Inquiry Committee. Its members were D.J. Reid, Mahatma Gandhi, L.C. Adami, Raja Hariprasad Narayan Singh, and G. Rainey, while M.E.L. Tanner was its Secretary.

mcqs.question: After returning from South Africa, Gandhiji launched his first successful Satyagraha in :
mcqs.explanation: After returning from South Africa in January 1915, Gandhi launched his first successful Satyagraha in 1917 in the Champaran district of Bihar.

mcqs.question: Which one of the following statements is not correct about Champaran Satyagraha?

options.a: It was connected with the peasants
options.c: Dr. Rajendra Prasad and J.B. Kripalani co-operated with M.K. Gandhi in it.
options.d: It was the first movement launched by M.K. Gandhi on All India level.

mcqs.explanation: The Champaran Satyagraha was confined only to Champaran, and the first movement launched by Gandhi at the national level was the Rowlatt Satyagraha (1919). The first three statements regarding the Champaran Satyagraha are correct.

mcqs.question: Who had opposed the Champaran Satyagraha of Mahatma Gandhi?
mcqs.explanation: N.G. Ranga opposed Mahatma Gandhi’s Champaran Satyagraha, whereas Rabindranath Tagore gave Gandhi the title of ‘Mahatma’ during the Champaran Satyagraha itself.

mcqs.question: In the contexts of Indian history, which of the following statements is/are correct regarding Vaikom Satyagraha? 1. It was a satyagraha against untouchability and caste discrimination. 2. Mahatma Gandhi participated in this Satyagraha. Select the correct answer using the codes given below. Codes :
mcqs.explanation: A social protest was organized in the then Travancore (now part of Kerala) against untouchability and caste discrimination in Kerala’s Hindu society, which came to be known as the Vaikom Satyagraha (1924-25). Although Gandhi did not participate directly in this movement, it received his guidance and support. Since the second statement does not specify whether the participation was direct or indirect, it may also be treated as correct.

mcqs.question: Which one of the following Jails was named as ‘Mandir’ by Gandhiji?
mcqs.explanation: Gandhi was sent as a prisoner to Yeravda Jail (located in Pune district, Maharashtra) in 1930. From there, he used to send weekly letters containing his messages to the residents of the Sabarmati Ashram. Reflecting on his experiences and spiritual progress in Yeravda Jail, Gandhi described Yeravda Prison as a ‘temple’.

mcqs.question: Gandhiji started his first Satyagraha against:

options.c: Payment of low wages to workers

mcqs.explanation: Gandhi first experimented with Satyagraha in Champaran in 1917, and after that he used it for the second time in February–March 1918 in support of the industrial workers of the Ahmedabad cotton mills who were protesting against lower wages. Since Champaran is not given among the options in the present question, the Ahmedabad Satyagraha is to be treated as the first Satyagraha for answering this question. In Ahmedabad, there was a dispute between the mill owners and the workers over the plague bonus. After Gandhi’s three-day fast, which was his first hunger strike in India, the mill owners agreed to settle the matter through arbitration, and ultimately the workers received the bonus.

mcqs.question: Which of the following struggles of Mahatma Gandhi was related to industrial workers-
mcqs.explanation: After the success of Champaran, Gandhi’s next experiment in 1918 was to intervene in a dispute between the mill owners and the workers of a cotton textile mill in Ahmedabad over wages. This dispute was related to the plague bonus. After the plague epidemic ended, the owners wanted to discontinue this bonus, whereas the workers demanded that it should continue. After making a detailed study of production cost, profit, and the cost of living of the workers, Gandhi declared that the workers should get a 35 percent bonus. After Gandhi’s fast, the tribunal constituted accepted his view.

mcqs.question: In 1918, the United Provinces Kisan Sabha was formed by which of the following leaders?
mcqs.explanation: The activists of the Home Rule League were quite active in Awadh. They began organizing the peasants. The organization was named the ‘Kisan Sabha’. In February 1918, the ‘United Provinces Kisan Sabha’ was established through the efforts of Indra Narayan Dwivedi, Gauri Shankar Mishra, and Madan Mohan Malaviya.

mcqs.question: Where had Baba Ramchandra organized the farmers?
mcqs.explanation: Baba Ramchandra belonged to a Brahmin family of Maharashtra. By the middle of 1920, he emerged as a peasant leader and began organizing the peasants of Awadh. He had extraordinary organizational ability. In 1920, through his efforts, the ‘Awadh Kisan Sabha’ was formed at Pratapgarh.

mcqs.question: In the 1930s, peasant movements were started in different parts of the country at the instance of various leaders. Match them with their respective areas of influence. A. Sahajanand Saraswati1. Hyderabad B. Khudai Khidmatgars 2. Southern Assam C. Swami Ramanand 3. Bihar D. Abdul Hamid Khan 4. NWFP Code : A B C D
mcqs.explanation: Sahajanand Saraswati was the founder of the Bihar Provincial Kisan Sabha. In the North-West Frontier Province (NWFP), the Khudai Khidmatgar or Red Shirt organization, led by Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan, played an active role in the Civil Disobedience Movement. Swami Ramanand was associated with Hyderabad, and Abdul Hamid Khan with Southern Assam.

mcqs.question: Who among the following was elected as General Secretary of ‘All India Kishan Congress’ established in Lucknow?
mcqs.explanation: In April 1936, the ‘All India Kisan Congress’ was established at Lucknow, and later its name was changed to the ‘All India Kisan Sabha’. Swami Sahajanand Saraswati, founder of the Bihar Provincial Kisan Sabha, was its first President, and N.G. Ranga, a leading leader of the peasant movement in Andhra and a scholar of agrarian issues, was elected its General Secretary. Along with the Congress session at Faizpur, the second session of the All India Kisan Congress was also held there, which was presided over by N.G. Ranga.

mcqs.question: Which one of the following Congress leaders had participated in the first meeting of All India Kisan Sabha?
mcqs.explanation: Jawaharlal Nehru also addressed the first All India Kisan Sabha (1936) held at Lucknow.

mcqs.question: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below the Lists: List-I A. Bardoli Satyagraha B. Bhartiya Kisan Vidyalaya C. Bengal Praja Party D. Bakashat Agitation List-II 1. Swami Shraddhananda Saraswati 2. Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel 3. Fazlul Haq 4. N.G. Ranga Code : A B C D
mcqs.explanation: In 1928, the peasant movement in the Bardoli taluka of Surat district was led by Vallabhbhai Patel, which became famous as the Bardoli Satyagraha. It was due to the success of this movement that the women of Bardoli conferred upon Patel the title of ‘Sardar’. Bharatiya Kisan Sansthan was founded by N.G. Ranga. In 1929, Fazlul Haq founded the Praja Party, which later came to be known as the Bengal Praja Party. After the elections held in 1937, he formed the government in Bengal in alliance with the Muslim League. Bihar’s Bakasht (self-cultivated land) struggle is associated with Swami Shraddhanand Saraswati.

mcqs.question: In which State was the Bhoodan Movement first started?
mcqs.explanation: The Bhoodan Movement was started by Acharya Vinoba Bhave on 18 April 1951 from the village of Pochampalli in the Telangana region of the then Andhra Pradesh (now in the state of Telangana).

mcqs.question: The objective of this party was to work within the Congress so that it could be made a more revolution inclined party and an organisation of the common people. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
mcqs.explanation: First, in 1925, the Labour Swaraj Party was formed within the Congress in Bengal, which was transformed into the Bengal Workers’ and Peasants’ Party in 1926. Thereafter, in 1926, the Congress Labour Party that had emerged within the Congress in Bombay Province gave rise, in 1927, to the Workers’ and Peasants’ Party of Bombay Province. After this, in 1928, similar parties were formed in Punjab under the name of the Kirti Kisan Party and then in the United Provinces as Workers’ and Peasants’ Parties. At the conference of these labour and peasant groups from different provinces held in Calcutta in December 1928, the ‘All India Workers’ and Peasants’ Party’ was formed as an all-India organization. Thus, Statement 1 is not correct. The objective of this party was to work within the Congress itself while providing an appropriate platform for the demands of workers and peasants, so that the Congress could be transformed into a party with a more revolutionary orientation and an organization of the common people. Therefore, Statement 2 is correct. Hence, the correct answer is option (d).

mcqs.question: The first Trade Union was founded in India in the year 1918 by
mcqs.explanation: The Madras Labour Union, established in 1918 under the leadership of V.P. Wadia, was the first modern labour union organization in India.

mcqs.question: Who was the first President of All India Trade Union Congress?
mcqs.explanation: The All India Trade Union Congress (AITUC) was established by N.M. Joshi on 31 October 1920 in Bombay. It was established in the context of the formation of the International Labour Organization in 1919. Therefore, Indian labour organizations decided to unite among themselves. Its first President was Lala Lajpat Rai, while Joseph Baptista was the Vice-President and Diwan Chaman Lall was the General Secretary.

mcqs.question: Who presided over the first session of the All India Trade Union Congress (AITUC) in Bombay (now Mumbai)?
mcqs.explanation: AITUC was established by N.M. Joshi on 31 October 1920 in Bombay. The first session was presided over by the famous nationalist leader Lala Lajpat Rai.

mcqs.question: Who among the following had presided over the All India Trade Union Congress held at Nagpur in 1929?
mcqs.explanation: In 1929, the Nagpur session of the ‘All India Trade Union Congress’ (A.I.T.U.C.) was presided over by Jawaharlal Nehru. It was also at the Nagpur session that the A.I.T.U.C. split because of differences between the communists and the reformists. The Nehru Report was criticized in this session; therefore, the rightists separated and, under the leadership of N.M. Joshi and V.V. Giri, formed the ‘Indian Trade Union Federation’ (I.T.U.F.).

mcqs.question: Who among the following was the President of the ‘All India Trade Union Congress’ in 1929?
mcqs.explanation: During 1928–29, Jawaharlal Nehru was the President of the All India Trade Union Congress. In 1929, its Nagpur session was presided over by Subhas Chandra Bose. Therefore, among the given options, the required answer is option (c).

mcqs.question: Kanpur conspiracy case was against the leaders of :
mcqs.explanation: To check the strength and growing influence of the communist movement, the British government prosecuted some communists by making a conspiracy case at Kanpur. This case became famous as the ‘Kanpur Conspiracy Case’. In 1924, the British government put M.N. Roy, Shripad Amrit Dange, Muzaffar Ahmad, Shaukat Usmani, Ghulam Shaukat Hussain, Ramcharan Lal Sharma and Singaravelu Chettiar on trial at Kanpur. The government alleged that they were hatching a conspiracy whose objective was to establish a revolutionary organization in India. The Peshawar Conspiracy Case and the Meerut Conspiracy Case were also against the leaders of the communist movement.

mcqs.question: Which of the following trials attracted world-wide publicity and drew sympathetic comments from Albert Einstein, H.G. Wells, Harold Laski and Roosevelt in favour of the convicts?
mcqs.explanation: In the Meerut Conspiracy Case, which was conducted during 1929-33, Shripad Amrit Dange, Muzaffar Ahmad, P.C. Joshi, Shaukat Usmani and several other labour leaders were tried for sedition. It was discussed throughout the world, and Albert Einstein, H.G.
