mcqs.explanation: Among the women mentioned in the question, Shanti Ghosh was not associated with the Quit India Movement. It is noteworthy that in December 1931, two schoolgirls from Bengal, Shanti Ghosh and Suniti Chowdhury, shot dead a District Magistrate. All the other women freedom fighters given in the options were associated with the Quit India Movement.
mcqs.chapter: Individual Satyagraha, Cripps Mission and Quit India Movement

mcqs.question: Given below is a list of places. Name those where parallel governments were established during ‘Quit India Movement.’ Select your answer from the code given below the list: 1. Ballia 2. Satara 3. Hazaribagh 4. Meerut Code :
mcqs.explanation: An important feature of the Quit India Movement was the establishment of parallel governments in many places in the country. During 1942, parallel governments were established in three major places in the country: (I) Ballia – in August 1942 under the leadership of Chittu Pandey (II) Tamluk (Midnapore), Bengal – from December 1942 to August 1944; the Jatiya Sarkar here initiated programmes to help cyclone victims (III) Satara (Maharashtra) – from August 1943 to May 1946; this was the longest-lasting parallel government. A parallel government was established here under the name of Prati Sarkar; its prominent leaders were Y.V. Chavan and Nana Patil. Apart from these, a parallel government also existed for some time in Talcher of Odisha.
mcqs.chapter: Individual Satyagraha, Cripps Mission and Quit India Movement

mcqs.question: Assertion (A) :The Quit India Movement marked the culmination of Indian National Movement. Reason (R) : After the Quit India Movement it was a need of time to find a suitable mechanism for transfer of power. Select the correct answer from the code given below: Code :

options.a: (A) and (R) are individually true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.b: (A) and (R) are individually true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

mcqs.explanation: Undoubtedly, the Quit India Movement was brutally suppressed by the Government, yet this movement made the greatest contribution to the independence that came in 1947. The call of “Quit India” given in August 1942 compelled the British to leave India five years later.
mcqs.chapter: Individual Satyagraha, Cripps Mission and Quit India Movement

mcqs.question: 'Operation Rubicon' was the code word proposed to be adopted by British Government in India with reference to which of the following?

options.a: Gandhi's fast unto death in Jail
options.c: Gandhi's participation in Round Table Conference

mcqs.explanation: During the Quit India Movement, when Mahatma Gandhi was detained in the Aga Khan Palace, his health was deteriorating rapidly because of his fast unto death. On the advice of doctors, the British Government in India considered that if Gandhi were to die, the Bombay Government would send the code word ‘Rubicon’ to the provincial governments.
mcqs.chapter: Individual Satyagraha, Cripps Mission and Quit India Movement

mcqs.question: Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose was born in the city of :
mcqs.explanation: Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose was born on 23 January, 1897, at Cuttack in Odisha. He obtained his Bachelor’s degree from Calcutta University in 1919 and qualified for the Indian Civil Service (I.C.S.) in 1920. He became the President of the Congress at Haripura in 1938 and at Tripuri in 1939. In 1939, he resigned from the presidentship of the Congress and founded the Forward Bloc, and in 1941 he went to Germany. He took command of the Azad Hind Fauj in 1943. He is generally remembered as ‘Netaji’.
mcqs.chapter: Subhash Chandra Bose and Azad Hind Fauj

mcqs.question: Major Iwaichi Fujiwara Select correct answer by using codes given below:
mcqs.explanation: In December, 1941, in the forests of northern Malaya, the unit of the 14th Punjab Regiment led by Captain Mohan Singh was defeated by the Japanese army. The British Lieutenant Colonel L.V. Fitzpatrick of this unit became a prisoner of war, but after Gyani Pritam Singh, an Indian Sikh living in Bangkok, took responsibility for them, Captain Mohan Singh and the other Indian soldiers were given the status of ‘friends of Japan’ instead of prisoners of war. Gyani Pritam Singh was a member of the Ghadar Party and was working in Bangkok for Indian independence. Pritam Singh wanted to organize an independent Indian army with Japanese assistance. In fact, Japanese Major Iwaichi Fujiwara and Gyani Pritam Singh encouraged Captain Mohan Singh to lead the ‘Indian National Army’. By the end of December, 1941, Captain Mohan Singh agreed to this. In 1942, the ‘Indian National Army’ was formed under the leadership of Mohan Singh, and it included Indian soldiers of the British army who had been defeated during Japan’s Malayan campaign. Clearly, the idea of the I.N.A. was put forward by Gyani Pritam Singh and Fujiwara, while Captain Mohan Singh provided its first leadership.
mcqs.chapter: Individual Satyagraha, Cripps Mission and Quit India Movement

mcqs.question: Who suggested the idea of the Indian National Army–
mcqs.explanation: Since the names of Gyani Pritam Singh and Major Fujiwara are not included in the options given in the question, the correct option would be Mohan Singh.
mcqs.chapter: Individual Satyagraha, Cripps Mission and Quit India Movement

mcqs.question: The first commander of “Indian National Army” was –
mcqs.explanation: Captain Mohan Singh became the first Commander of the ‘Indian National Army’ or ‘Azad Hind Fauj’.
mcqs.chapter: Subhash Chandra Bose and Azad Hind Fauj

mcqs.question: Subhash Chandra Bose announced the establishment of Provisional Government of Free India on –
mcqs.explanation: On 4 July, 1943, Rash Behari Bose handed over the command of the Azad Hind Fauj to Subhas Chandra Bose. On 21 October, 1943, Subhas Chandra Bose formed the Provisional Government of Free India (Azad Hind Government) in Singapore.
mcqs.chapter: Subhash Chandra Bose and Azad Hind Fauj

mcqs.question: Which of the following countries did not recognize the Azad Hind Government?
mcqs.explanation: In fact, Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose’s Azad Hind Government was recognized only by a few Axis-supporting countries or governments under their sphere of influence, such as Japan, Germany, Italy, Thailand, Burma, Manchukuo, the Wang Jingwei regime of Nanjing China, Croatia, and the Philippines; Indonesia was not among them.
mcqs.chapter: Subhash Chandra Bose and Azad Hind Fauj

mcqs.question: Which Indian revolutionary helped Subhash Chandra Bose in the establishment of Azad Hind Fauj?
mcqs.explanation: Subhas Chandra Bose reached Tokyo in June 1943. Soon afterwards, Rash Behari Bose resigned from the post of President of the Indian Independence League in favor of Subhas Chandra Bose. Subhas Chandra Bose was declared the Supreme Commander of the Azad Hind Fauj.
mcqs.chapter: Subhash Chandra Bose and Azad Hind Fauj

mcqs.question: What was the name of the female Regiment constituted as a part of the Azad Hind Fauj by Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose?
mcqs.explanation: Subhas Chandra Bose established the Rani Jhansi Regiment for women, named after Rani Lakshmibai. The other brigades of the Azad Hind Fauj were the Azad Brigade, Subhas Brigade, Nehru Brigade, and Gandhi Brigade.
mcqs.chapter: Subhash Chandra Bose and Azad Hind Fauj

mcqs.question: Which one of the following was NOT associated with Indian National Army (I.N.A.)?
mcqs.explanation: The British Government arrested the officers and soldiers of the Azad Hind Fauj and put them on trial in November 1945. In this trial, Prem Kumar Sehgal, Gurbaksh Singh Dhillon, and Shah Nawaz were sentenced to life imprisonment, while Rashid Ali was sentenced to seven years’ imprisonment. However, in view of the widespread public opposition and the strong protest among Indian soldiers in the British Army, the then Army Chief, Field Marshal Claude Auchinleck, set aside their sentences. B.C. Dutt was not associated with the Azad Hind Fauj.
mcqs.chapter: Subhash Chandra Bose and Azad Hind Fauj

mcqs.question: Who among the following had headed the group of advocates to argue the case on behalf of The Indian National Army in 1945 in the Red Fort trials?
mcqs.explanation: The arrested officers and soldiers of the Azad Hind Fauj (I.N.A.) were tried in 1945 at the Red Fort in Delhi. In this famous trial, the defence was conducted by Kailash Nath Katju, Sir Tej Bahadur Sapru, Asaf Ali, Jawaharlal Nehru, Bhulabhai Desai, and others. This group of lawyers was headed by Bhulabhai Desai.
mcqs.chapter: Subhash Chandra Bose and Azad Hind Fauj

mcqs.question: The ‘Azad Hind Fauj Day’ was observed on–
mcqs.explanation: ‘Azad Hind Fauj Day’ was observed on 12 November, 1945, while Azad Hind Fauj Week was observed from 5 to 11 November, 1945.
mcqs.chapter: Subhash Chandra Bose and Azad Hind Fauj

mcqs.question: Who was the Political Guru of Subhash Chandra Bose?
mcqs.explanation: Deshbandhu Chittaranjan Das was the political guru of Subhas Chandra Bose.
mcqs.chapter: Subhash Chandra Bose and Azad Hind Fauj

mcqs.question: Who among the following called Subhash Chandra Bose as ‘Desh Nayak.’
mcqs.explanation: After Subhas Chandra Bose became the President of the Indian National Congress in 1938, Gurudev Rabindranath Tagore honoured him at Shantiniketan with the title ‘Desh Nayak’. Mahatma Gandhi called him the ‘Patriot of patriots’.
mcqs.chapter: Subhash Chandra Bose and Azad Hind Fauj

mcqs.question: Who gave the slogan ‘Jai Hind’?
mcqs.explanation: The slogan ‘Jai Hind’ was given by Subhas Chandra Bose. It was the form of salutation in the Azad Hind Fauj, and today it has become a national slogan.
mcqs.chapter: Subhash Chandra Bose and Azad Hind Fauj

mcqs.question: Consider the following events and arrange them in correct chronological order starting from the earliest to the last activity: 1. Royal Indian Navy Revolt 2. Announcement of Cabinet Mission 3. Formation of Interim Government 4. Arrival of a UK Parliamentary Delegation in Delhi Select the correct answer from the codes given below:
mcqs.explanation: The British Parliamentary Delegation arrived in Delhi in January 1946. This delegation met the leading Indian leaders and sought to understand their views on independence. The Royal Indian Navy Revolt took place in February 1946, and the Cabinet Mission arrived in India on 24 March 1946. Under the declaration of 24 August 1946, the Interim Government of India was formed on 2 September 1946 on the basis of the Cabinet Mission Plan. Thus, the correct chronological order of the above events is 4, 1, 2, 3. In its initial answer key, the

mcqs.question: The ‘Cabinet-Mission’ of 1946 was led by:
mcqs.explanation: On 26 July 1945, the British Cabinet under the leadership of Attlee assumed power in Britain. After the naval revolt, the British Government decided on 19 February 1946 to send a delegation to India for constitutional reforms. This Cabinet Mission arrived in Delhi on 24 March 1946. Its head was the Secretary of State for India, Lord Pethick-Lawrence, and the other two members were Stafford Cripps and A.V. Alexander.

mcqs.question: Which one of the following had proposed a three-tier polity for India?
mcqs.explanation: The Cabinet Mission proposed a three-tier system of government for India. Under this, the provinces were to be divided into three groups—A, B and C.
mcqs.chapter: Subhash Chandra Bose and Azad Hind Fauj

mcqs.question: Given below are two statements, one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R). Assertion (A) : In 1946, the Muslim League withdrew its acceptance of the Cabinet Mission Plan. Reason (R) : The Muslim League joined the interim government formed in 1946. Select the correct answer from the codes given below.

options.a: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.b: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

mcqs.explanation: The Cabinet Mission Plan was accepted very unwillingly by both the Congress and the League. The Congress was unhappy with the grouping of provinces, and the League was unhappy because Pakistan had not been accepted. On 10 July 1946, Nehru stated that grouping was not compulsory and that Assam and the North-West Frontier Province could refuse to join the respective groups. After this, the Muslim League rejected the Cabinet Mission Plan and adopted the proposal for Direct Action. Later, the Viceroy invited Jawaharlal Nehru of the Congress to form the Interim Government. The Muslim League was also asked to join it, but it refused. However, later, on the Viceroy’s renewed advice, it agreed through the resolution of 13 October 1946 to join the Interim Government in order to protect Muslim interests. Thus, both the assertion and the reason are true, but the reason is not the correct explanation of the assertion.

mcqs.question: Which one of the following leaders of the Congress was totally in favour of Cabinet Mission Plan?
mcqs.explanation: Among the given Congress leaders, Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel was completely in favour of the Cabinet Mission Plan. He considered this plan suitable for preserving the unity of India and made important efforts to bring Jawaharlal Nehru and other Congress leaders in support of it.

mcqs.question: Who was the President of Indian National Congress during the visit of Cabinet Mission to India?
mcqs.explanation: Maulana Abul Kalam Azad was the President of the Indian National Congress when the Cabinet Mission arrived in India. The Congress Working Committee had given him full authority to hold discussions with the Cabinet Mission. He met the members of the Cabinet Mission for the first time on 6 April 1946.

mcqs.question: Who prepared "C.R. Formula" to remove the political deadlock between Muslim League and Indian National Congress?
mcqs.explanation: C. Rajagopalachari, an influential leader of the Madras Province, presented in 1944, with Gandhiji’s approval, a plan for a compromise between the Muslim League and the Indian National Congress in order to resolve the political deadlock between the two parties. This plan came to be known as the ‘C.R. Formula’. Jinnah rejected this formula.

mcqs.question: In the leadership of Pt. Jawaharlal Nehru interim Government formed in –
mcqs.explanation: After the Congress accepted the latest proposals of the Viceroy, Lord Wavell invited Congress President Jawaharlal Nehru on 12 August, 1946, to form the Interim Government. On 24 August, 1946, India’s first Interim National Government under the leadership of Pt. Nehru was announced, and it was formed on 2 September, 1946. Initially, the Muslim League did not participate in it.

mcqs.question: In the Interim Government (1946) who held the Railways Portfolio?
mcqs.explanation: In the Interim Government of 1946, the Railways and Transport Department was assigned to Asaf Ali.

mcqs.question: Who among the following was the Finance Minister in Nehru’s interim Government in 1946?
mcqs.explanation: In 1946, after much persuasion by Lord Wavell, the League agreed to join the Interim Government. In October, 1946, five members of the League joined the government. Liaqat Ali was made the Finance Minister, and while presenting the new budget, he imposed very heavy taxes on industrialists and traders.

mcqs.question: Who among the following was not minister in interim Government formed on 2nd September, 1946?
mcqs.explanation: Neither Liaqat Ali Khan nor Abul Kalam Azad was a minister in the Interim Government formed on 2 September, 1946. The 12 Congress ministers included in this government were Pt. Jawaharlal Nehru, Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, Dr. Rajendra Prasad, Asaf Ali, Rajagopalachari, Sarat Chandra Bose, Dr. John Mathai, Sardar Baldev Singh, Sir Shafaat Ahmad Khan, Jagjivan Ram, Syed Ali Zaheer, and C.S. Bhabha. However, Liaqat Ali was also not included initially in the Interim Government formed on 2 September, 1946. Five members of the Muslim League, including Liaqat Ali, were made ministers in the government on 26 October, 1946, as a result of which three Congress members—Syed Ali Zaheer, Sarat Chandra Bose, and Sir Shafaat Ahmad Khan—had to leave the government. B.R. Ambedkar was also not a member of the Interim Government.

mcqs.question: Muslim League observed the ‘Direct Action Day’ on :
mcqs.explanation: The date 16 August, 1946, was fixed by the Muslim League for ‘Direct Action Day’. Rejecting the Viceroy’s decision regarding the Interim Government, the Muslim League demanded the establishment of an independent and fully sovereign Pakistan state. Through this action, the League intended to spread riots and create an atmosphere of terror in order to demonstrate that Hindus and Muslims could not live together. Noakhali was a major centre of the riots.

mcqs.question: Which one of the following parties was in power in the U.K. when India got independence. ?
mcqs.explanation: At the time of India’s independence, Clement R. Attlee was the British Prime Minister. He remained in office from 1945 to 1951. During this period, the Labour Party was in power in Britain.

mcqs.question: Which plan became the platform of Indian Independence?
mcqs.explanation: Mountbatten fixed August 15, 1947, as the date for the transfer of power to India. After nearly two months of negotiations, Mountbatten came to the conclusion that partition was the only option. Therefore, in line with Attlee’s statement, he prepared a plan for the partition of India, which was known as the ‘Mountbatten Plan’.

mcqs.question: The British Parliament passed the Indian Independence Act in –
mcqs.explanation: In accordance with the Mountbatten Plan (June 3, 1947), the British Parliament passed the ‘Indian Independence Act’ in July, 1947, under which the date of August 15, 1947, was fixed for the establishment of the two Dominions, India and Pakistan. This Act became effective after receiving Royal Assent on July 18, 1947.

mcqs.question: Assertion (A) : Britain made India free in 1947. Reason (R) : Britain had become weak during the second World War. In the context of the above two statements, which of the following is/are correct? Code :

options.a: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.b: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not a correct explanation of (A).

mcqs.source: U.P. P.C.S. (Pre) 2001; U.P. P.S.C. (GIC) 2010 U.P. Lower Sub.(Spl.) (Pre) 2003
mcqs.explanation: Both Statement (A) and Reason (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A). The British had been weakened by the Second World War. Cripps said in the House of Commons: “One option was to carry out severe repression in India and be prepared to keep British troops stationed in India for many years, which certainly the people of this country (Britain) would not permit, because, as we all know, we are already short of manpower.”

mcqs.question: Assertion (A) : The Indian National Congress accepted the Mountbatten plan. Reason (R) : It believed in two-nation theory. Select the correct answer from the code given below: Code :

options.a: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.b: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

mcqs.explanation: Statement (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false. The Indian National Congress accepted the Mountbatten Plan not because it believed in the two-nation theory, but because that was the only option to deal with the growing danger of communal riots.

mcqs.question: Who headed the Boundary Commission appointed in 1947 in the context of India’s partition?
mcqs.explanation: Sir Cyril Radcliffe chaired the Boundary Commissions appointed in 1947 in connection with the partition of India. He was entrusted with demarcating the partition boundary in Punjab and Bengal, which came to be known as the Radcliffe Line.

mcqs.question: Who among the following was the Chairman of the Congress Session of Delhi wherein resolution of divided India was passed on June 15, 1947?
mcqs.explanation: When the Congress General Committee approved the proposal for the partition of India in Delhi on June 15, 1947, Acharya J.B. Kripalani was the President of the Congress.

mcqs.question: Who among the following had seconded the resolution on the partition in the meeting of All India Congress Committee held in New Delhi in 1947?
mcqs.explanation: At the meeting of the All India Congress Committee held on June 14, 1947, to confirm the partition plan of June 3, 1947, Govind Ballabh Pant moved the proposal for the partition of India, and Maulana Abul Kalam Azad seconded it.

mcqs.question: Who of the following took the passing of a resolution on the partition in the meeting of the Congress Committee(1947) as a “Surrender of Nationalism in favour of Communalism.”
mcqs.explanation: Dr. Saifuddin Kitchlew regarded the passing of the partition proposal by the Congress Committee meeting in 1947 as “the surrender of nationalism in favour of communalism.” Dr. Kitchlew, the President of the Punjab Provincial Congress Committee, was a strong opponent of partition. After India’s independence, he separated himself from the Congress Party and joined the Communist Party of India.

mcqs.question: In the meeting of All India Committee on June 14-15, 1947; who among voted against the partition of India?
mcqs.explanation: In the meeting of the All India Congress Committee held on 14–15 June, 1947, Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan (Frontier Gandhi), along with Dr. Kitchlew, Purushottam Das Tandon, etc., voted against the partition of India.

mcqs.question: Who sang ‘Hindustan Hamara’ of Iqbal and ‘Jan-gan- man’ in the Central Assembly at midnight of 14/15 August, 1947?
mcqs.explanation: On the midnight of 14/15 August, 1947, in the Central Assembly, “Jana-Gana-Mana” and Iqbal’s song “Sare Jahan Se Achha Hindostan Hamara” were sung by Sucheta Kripalani.

mcqs.question: Who appointed the first Prime Minister of India?
mcqs.explanation: On the first occasion, Pt. Jawaharlal Nehru was appointed to the office of Prime Minister of India by the then Governor- General, Lord Mountbatten.

mcqs.question: Who among the following was the first Governor- General of free India?
mcqs.explanation: The first Governor-General of independent India was Lord Mountbatten (1947–48), and the first Indian Governor- General was Chakravarti Rajagopalachari (1948–50).

mcqs.question: Who among the following was the first Law Minister of India?
mcqs.explanation: The first Law Minister of independent India was B.R. Ambedkar. At the time of independence, on the advice of Mahatma Gandhi, he was invited to assume the office of Union Law Minister. In this role, he worked as the Chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Constitution.

mcqs.question: Who represented the Indian National Congress in the Partition Council headed by Lord Mountbatten? 1. Abul Kalam Azad 2. Jawaharlal Nehru 3. Sardar Patel 4. Rajendra Prasad Select the correct answer from the code given below: Code :
mcqs.explanation: In the Partition Council formed under the chairmanship of Lord Mountbatten, Jawaharlal Nehru and Sardar Patel represented the Indian National Congress. Thereafter, Lord Mountbatten presented his plan on 3 June.

mcqs.question: Who among the following was the President of the Indian National Congress on 15th August, 1947?
mcqs.explanation: At the time of the partition of India, J.B. Kripalani was the President of the Indian National Congress. He became President at the Meerut Session on 23 November, 1946, and remained President until November 1947. After his resignation, Dr. Rajendra Prasad was made President.

mcqs.question: In August 1947, who of the following leaders did not participate anywhere in Independence Day celebrations?
mcqs.explanation: On the occasion of independence in August 1947, Mahatma Gandhi was in Noakhali, Bengal, trying to bring communal riots under control. Therefore, he did not participate in any of the celebrations held on that occasion.

mcqs.question: “Indian Nationalism was the child of the British Rule.” Who made this statement?
mcqs.explanation: R. Copland wrote in clear words, “Indian nationalism was indeed the offspring of British rule.”

mcqs.question: Who among the following said that “the most notable achievement of the British Rule was the unification of India”?
mcqs.explanation: On the unification of India under British rule, K.M. Panikkar said, “The most important achievement of British rule was the unification of India.”

mcqs.question: Most of the integration of princely states in the Union of India had taken place in which year?
mcqs.explanation: Most of the princely states were merged into the Indian Union in 1947. By 15 August 1947, all princely states except Junagadh, Jammu and Kashmir, and Hyderabad had joined India, and by the end of 1948, these three states too were compelled, in due course, to accede.

mcqs.question: Which one of the following native States was a party to the ‘Stand-Still’ Agreement:
mcqs.explanation: The Standstill Agreement was signed on 29 November 1947 between the Hyderabad State and the Dominion of India. This agreement was signed by Mir Laik Ali, the Prime Minister of Hyderabad State, and Lord Mountbatten, the Governor-General of the Dominion of India.

mcqs.question: In which of the following Acts for the first time provision was made for the post of Governor-General of Bengal?
mcqs.explanation: The British government passed the Regulating Act of 1773 to remove the corruption and maladministration prevailing in the Company. Under this Act, the Madras and Bombay Presidencies were brought under the Calcutta Presidency. The Governor of Bengal was thereafter called the Governor- General. Warren Hastings was appointed the first Governor- General of Bengal.

mcqs.question: The Supreme Court was set up for the first time in India under the:
mcqs.explanation: By the Regulating Act of 1773, a Supreme Court was established for the first time at Calcutta. It consisted of one Chief Justice and three other judges. This Supreme Court was to function as a general court, a court under the law of the land, a court of admiralty, and an ecclesiastical court. This Supreme Court was constituted in 1774, and Elijah Impey was appointed as its Chief Justice, while Robert Chambers, Stephen Caesar Le Maistre, and John Hyde were appointed as the other judges.

mcqs.question: Which Act gave the right to reject the decision of the committee to Governor-General?
mcqs.explanation: In 1786, a Bill was placed before the British Parliament with the intention of persuading Cornwallis to accept the office of Governor-General. He wanted to hold the powers of both Governor-General and Commander-in-Chief. Under the new Act, this was accepted, and in special circumstances he was also given the authority to overrule the decisions of his Council and enforce his own decisions.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is one of the reasons for considering the Charter Act of 1813 important for India?

options.a: It banned propaganda by Christian Missionaries in India.
options.c: It made a financial allocation for the education of Indian people.
options.d: It approved the development of a railway system in India.

mcqs.explanation: The provision that made the Charter Act of 1813 important for India was that a sum of one lakh rupees per year was to be set apart for the encouragement of learned Indians, for the improvement and revival of literature, and for the promotion and introduction of scientific knowledge in the Indian territories. Under this clause, the government undertook the responsibility of spreading education among the people.

mcqs.question: Which of among following had recommended to hold the Indian Civil Service Examination simultaneously in India & England?
mcqs.explanation: The Montagu-Chelmsford Report, 1918, recommended that Indian participation in the administration should be increased. The report also recommended that the Civil Services Examination should be conducted simultaneously in England and India and that one-third of the higher civil posts should be reserved for Indians. It was on the basis of the recommendations of the Montagu-Chelmsford Report that, from 1922, the Civil Services Examination began to be held simultaneously in England and India. In its report submitted in 1887, the Aitchison Commission had recommended that the Civil Services Examination should not be conducted simultaneously in England and India.

mcqs.question: Which of the following Acts for the first time created a functioning Legislative Council in India?
mcqs.explanation: By the Charter Act of 1853, a definite step was taken towards separating the executive and legislative powers. For the first time in India, a separate Legislative Council was established. This Legislative Council could have 12 members.

mcqs.question: Under which Act, Board of control was established –
mcqs.explanation: By Pitt’s India Act, 1784, a department of the British Government was created in England, which was called the Board of Control. Its main function was to control the policies of the Court of Directors.

mcqs.question: British East India Company lost the monopoly of Tea trade by –
mcqs.explanation: Under the Charter Act of 1813, the Company still retained its monopoly over trade with China and over the tea trade, but by the Charter Act of 1833, the Company’s commercial rights were completely abolished. Thereafter, the Company’s function was reduced merely to governing India on behalf of the British Government.

mcqs.question: In which of the following year almost the entire area of present Uttar Pradesh was separated from Bengal Presidency and placed under Agra Presidency?
mcqs.explanation: Under the Charter Act of 1833, on 14 November 1834, the fourth Presidency, the Agra Presidency, was created by separating this region from the Bengal Presidency. It included almost the entire area of present Uttar Pradesh. The other three Presidencies were Bengal, Bombay and Madras.

mcqs.question: Which of the following Acts transferred the Government of India from East India Company to the Crown?
mcqs.explanation: By the Government of India Act, 1858, control of Indian administration was taken away from the East India Company and handed over to the British Crown.
